The youth, well-attired and enveloped in a mantle, has come; he becomes even more excellent as he is born.
Wise poets, seeking the divine with minds intent on sacred study, lead him forward.
The youth, well-clothed and girt about, has come hither; he becomes more excellent as he is born. The wise sages, devout in thought and seeking the gods with their minds, lead him upward.
The meaning is: "a youth with firm limbs, characterized by the features described in the *Aṣṭādhyāyī*";
"well-attired" means endowed with beautiful garments and a girdle;
"encircled" means likewise wrapped in a [sacrificial] cord.
Such is the sacrificial post (yūpa).
It has come, it is coming.
That very post, being born—that is, becoming preeminent above all trees—becomes superior.

The wise ones—the intelligent, those who seek the gods with their minds, the well-reflective ones endowed with meditation on all sides, and the seers (kavayaḥ) of far-reaching vision—raise up that very sacrificial post (yūpa), making it lofty.

Regarding this matter, the Brāhmaṇa says: "The youth, well-clothed and girt about, has come"—with these words he puts on [the garment]. Indeed, the youth is well-clothed when he is enveloped by the vital breaths (*prāṇa*). "He becomes more excellent as he is born"—he indeed becomes more and more excellent as he is born. "The wise sages, seeking the gods with their minds, lead him up"—those who are performers of the rites are indeed the sages; they lead him up. (Ai. Brā. 2.2).
*Yuvā*: from the root *yu*, the suffix *kanin* is applied according to the rule "kaninyu-utripati-kṣa" etc.;
due to its *kittva* (indicatory *k*), there is an absence of *guṇa*.
The substitution [of *u* for *ū*] occurs;
by the rule that the first syllable is udātta,
it becomes *suvāsāḥ*.
In the sense of "covering" (*ācchādane*),
with the suffix *asun* being understood from the previous rule, the suffix *asun* is applied by the rule *vaserṇin*.
Due to the presence of the marker *ṇ*, there is vṛddhi substitution for the penultimate vowel.
In *lormana-mī*, the initial vowel of the second member (*uttarapada*) is udātta. *Parivītaḥ*:
from the root *vyeñ* in the sense of "covering."
The suffix *kta* is applied in the sense of the object (*karman*).
Due to its inclusion in the *yajādi* group, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*).
By the rule "the immediately preceding [element] is a *gati*," the initial member retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*).
He went (*agāt*).
In the *luṅ* [aorist] of the root *iṇ* in the sense of "going," there is the substitution of *gā* by the rule *iṇo gā luṅi*. By the rule *gatisthā*, there is the elision of the suffix *sic*.
The augment *aṭ* [is applied]: *śreyān*.
[This is derived from] *praśasya* with the suffix *īyasun* by the rule "when a dual number or a word expressing division is present as an upapada."
In that [context], there is the substitution [of *śra-*] by the rule "praśasyasya śraḥ";
then the *guṇa* [vowel substitution];
and because it ends in *nic*, it has the udātta accent on the first syllable.
The single substitute is udātta on the first syllable:
*svādhyāḥ*.
[The root] *dhyai* is used in the sense of "thinking."
The prefix *su-* is placed before the verbal root. The suffix *kvip* is applied according to the rule "it is seen after other roots as well.
Due to the inclusion of the root *dṛś*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*).
By the rule "saṃprasāraṇācca," there is substitution of the preceding [vowel] for the following; by the rule "halaḥ," there is lengthening;
and in the case of the suffix *jasi*, there is the substitution of *yaṇ* by the rule "eranekācaḥ."
The word has the original accent of its final member (*kuduttarapadaprakṛtisvara*).
By the rule "udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ," the *jas* suffix becomes *svarita*. Thus: *devayantaḥ*.
In the word *sūpāyati*, the suffix *kyac* is applied according to the rule *supa ātmanaḥ kyac*; because the suffix is marked with the *cit* indicator, it is accented on its final syllable.

[Variants: 1. kha-ga-ja-ṇa-na-bha read "gatiprakṛti"; 2. kha-ga-ja-ṇa-na-bha do not have the substitution of *i* for the vowel by the rule *ghumāsthā*; 3. kha-ga-ja-ṇa-na-bha omit the augment *aṭ*; 4. ta-la read the accent of the preceding member; 5. la refers to the rules of the *Aṣṭādhyāyī*.
Born, he is born in the auspiciousness of the days, increasing in the assembly and in the sacrificial rite.
The wise and skillful ones purify themselves through their inspired thought; the sage, seeking the gods, raises his voice.

He has been born; he is being born at the auspicious dawning of the days, increasing in the assembly of men. The wise, skillful ones purify him with their inspired thought. The sage, seeking the gods, raises his voice. 5.
Born upon the earth, first arisen as a sacrificial post (*yūpa*) in the assembly;
*marya* is a name for a human being—
growing in the sacrificial session (*vidatha*) accompanied by them.
*Vidatha* is a name for sacrifice, as it is listed among the names of sacrifice in *Nighaṇṭu* 3.17.5: "The *vidatha* is the *savana*.
In that sacrifice, growing great and shining on all sides through the ghee-food, the girdle, and the sprinkling, he is born in the auspiciousness of the days.
The meaning is that by means of the sacrificial post (*vidvāra*)—through the tethering of the animals—he brings about auspicious days by way of accomplishing the sacrifice.
The skillful performers of ritual action, the wise and highly intelligent Adhvaryus and others, purify that sacrificial post with their intellect through washing and other means.
Those who go to the gods shall maintain that supreme wealth of the gods where the gods dwell.
The meaning is "let them bestow."

*Nimittāyuḥ*: From the root *ḍumiñ* in the sense of "throwing," in the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*) with the suffix *us*, there is an absence of *guṇa* due to its being treated as *kit* by the rule "the *liṭ* following a non-conjunct [consonant] is *kit*.
Because of its connection with the word *yat*, it does not undergo the *anighāta* (lack of suppression) accent.

According to the rule "when [two vowels] remain, the accent of the suffix is stronger," the accent belongs to the suffix. *Svadhitiḥ*: from the roots *svaccha* (to cut) and *apa-dā* (to take away), and *dhā* (to hold) with the suffix *kin*.

*Svadhitih* means an axe; it is so called because one's own (*sva*) certain edge (*dhārā*) is placed (*dhīyate*) or applied by it. He hewed it. This form is derived from the root *takṣū* (or *tvakṣū*), meaning "to make thin," in the perfect tense (*liṭ*) with the suffix *nal*, resulting in the form *tatakṣa*. The nasal (*n*) has been dropped due to the rule *ranivātaḥ*.
The initial syllable of the word preceding the suffix *liti* is udātta.

Regarding *svaravaḥ*: from the root *svara* in the sense of "sound" (*śabda*) and "affliction" (*upatāpa*), with the suffix *nini* being understood from the previous rule, the suffix *u* is applied according to the rule beginning with "śvasṛsnahihrapi," etc.
It begins with the udātta accent on *ni*.
In that [word], there is the suffix *vāṃp*.
From the root *dhā* in the sense of "ceasing from motion," the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*) is used in the Vedic language (*chandasi*).
Its *kasu* [instrumental case] is:
"O Vasus, Ekājas, Adhrigūs! O Ādityas, Rudras, Vasus, Sunīthās, Heaven and Earth, Earth and the Intermediate Space!"
May the gods, being of one accord, protect the sacrifice; may they raise aloft the banner of the rite.

The Ādityas, the Rudras, the Vasus, the good leaders, Heaven and Earth, the Earth, and the Mid-region—may the gods, being of one accord, protect the sacrifice; may they raise aloft the banner of the rite. 8.

The *sunīthāḥ* are the excellent leaders of the sacrifice; the *ādityāḥ* are the twelve Ādityas; the *rudrāḥ* are the eleven Rudras; the *vasavaḥ* are the eight Vasus—or alternatively, they are those with excellent guidance (*sunīthāḥ*), excellent leaders (*sunayaḥ*). For it is heard in scripture: "The *nīthas* are the hymns and recitations, as well as the *ukthas* and *amadās*" (AiB 2.36). *Dyāvākṣāmā* refers to Heaven and Earth. *Pṛthivī*—the suffix *-tyayaḥ* is added to *pṛthu*. *Pṛthu* means wide or extensive. And the *antarikṣa* (the intermediate space). *Sajoṣasaḥ*: all these *devāḥ* (gods), being of one mind and united with one another, *bhuvekarudradīyam*—may they protect and guard this sacrifice. Furthermore, may they raise high, that is, erect, this sacrificial post (*yūpa*), which is the banner or the indicator of the *adhvarasya* sacrifice. **Etymological Notes:** *Ādityāḥ*: Offspring of Aditi. By the rule "from *ditya*, *aditi*, and *āditya* when followed by a word for offspring," the suffix *ṇya* is applied. Because of the *jit* designation, there is *vṛddhi* of the first vowel. The accent is that of the suffix. *Rudrāḥ*: They cause everyone to weep at the time of the end. By the rule "from *rud*, the suffix *ṇi* and elision [of the *ṇ*]," the suffix *rapratyaya* is applied. Upon its conjunction, there is elision of the *ṇi*. The accent is that of the suffix. The case-ending *jas* is unaccented because it belongs to the *sup* group. By the rule "a single substitute [for an accented and an unaccented vowel] is accented like the first," the single substitute is accented on the first syllable. *Vasavaḥ*: From the root *vas* "to dwell. With the suffix *upratyaya* following the continued application of "nit," according to the rule beginning with "śastṛ, snihiti, tapyasi, vasi," etc. Because of the *nit* designation, it is accented on the first syllable. *Sunīthāḥ*: From the root *ṇīñ* "to lead. By the rule "from *hani*, *kṛpi*, *nami*, *kāśi*, etc.," the suffix *kvan* is applied. Because of the *kit* designation, there is no *guṇa*. By the rule "the final syllable of the second member is accented in compounds ending in *thā*, *tha*, *va*, or *ka*," the final syllable of the second member is accented. *Dyāvākṣāmā*: *Dyauḥ* and *kṣāmā*. By the rule "for *div*, the substitute *dyāvā*," the form *dyāvā* is used. By the rule "in a dual compound of deities," both members retain their original accents. *Pṛthivī*: From the root *pratha* "to spread. By the rule "from *prath*, the suffix *pivan* and vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*)," there is the suffix *pivan* and vocalization. By the rule "after *piñ* and *jñu*, the feminine suffix *ṅīp* and the substitution of *āditya*," the suffix *ṅīp* is applied. It is accented on the final syllable by the accent of the suffix. *Avantu*: From the root *ava* "to protect. There is the *nighāta* (elision of the accent). *Kṛṇvantu*: From the root *kṛvi* "to injure" or "to do. By the rule "after *dhin* and *kṛṇvi*, the suffix *up* and the substitution of *a*," the suffix *up* is applied. The letter *a* is also the substitute for the final syllable. There is the *nighāta* (elision of the accent).
Like swans moving in rows, the sacrificial posts have come to us, clothed in white;
being raised up by the sages in the east, they go even upon the path of the gods.
Like swans, moving in rows, the bright sacrificial posts have come toward us, clothed [in raiment]. Being raised up by the sages in the east, they go as gods to the path of the gods. 9.

The bright, shining objects called *raśanā* (girdles) are wearing [them], that is, they are covering themselves; the sacrificial posts (*svaru*) are provided with *svaru*-spikes; they are arranged in rows, that is, in lines, moving forward.
Here is the illustration:
"like swans."

Just as swans flying in rows through the sky appear beautiful, so too those sacrificial posts (yūpas), shining brightly, have come to us. Furthermore, being raised up by the wise—the Adhvaryu priests and others—in the eastern part, that is, in front of the Āhavanīya fire, those radiant sacrificial posts have reached the path of the gods, the dwelling place of the gods, namely the intermediate space (antarikṣa). [As it is said:
"Pātha is the intermediate space; it is explained by its connection with the word 'path'."

1. [The syllables] kha, ga, gha, ca, na, pa, bha, and sa are approved. 2. Ca [is used] by means of its connection with that continuity. 3. Ga, ca, bha, la, and kṣamā. 4. Na and la; "called 'the girdle'" (araśanākhyāni) does not exist. 5. La [is placed] in the eastern part of the Āhavanīya fire. 222. The Ṛgveda.
Thus says Yāska (Nirukta 6.7).

Regarding the rule "pāthonadībhyāṃ ḍyaṇ" (Pāṇini Sūtra 4.4.111), the author of the Vṛtti also stated: "pāthaḥ is the intermediate space (antarikṣa). [The gods] weave or reach such an intermediate space.
The meaning is that the sacrificial posts (yūpas), being raised by the Adhvaryu and other priests, exist pervading the intermediate space (antarikṣa) due to their extreme height;
they are "like swans" (haṃsā iva).
According to the rule “ivena vibhaktyalopaḥ,” the accent of the preceding word [the first member of the compound] is retained.
*Śreṇiśaḥ*:
[the suffix] *śas* is applied by the rule “*bahulārthāt*” [Pāṇini 4.2.39]; it has the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).

*Śukra*: From the root *śuc* in the sense of "to shine," this word is derived with the suffix *ran*, being an irregular formation (*nipātana*) according to the rule beginning with *ṛtrendrāgra*; thus, it is oxytone (accented on the final syllable). *Aguḥ*.
The root *iṇ* means "to go. From this, the form [nivātaḥ] is derived in the *luṅ* tense. It means "sheltered from the wind" (*nivāta*).

Like the peaks of mountains, the sacrificial posts appear together, standing firm upon the earth. Resounding like the voices of priests in the invocation, may they protect us in the contests for booty.

Like mountain peaks, the sacrificial posts with their crossbeams appear together upon the earth; being praised by the invoking priests during the invocation, may they protect us in the contests of battle. 10.
‘The sacrificial posts (svaravaḥ) are provided with sounding-holes (svaravantaḥ), equipped with cross-pieces (capālavantaḥ), and fitted with rings (pratimuktakaṭakāḥ).
Such sacrificial posts were seen—seen clearly—as if they were the very horns of the earth, or like the horns of buffaloes and other beasts.
And furthermore, in the invocation (vihave).
A *vihava* is a sacrifice (*yajña*) wherein various oblations (*havīṃṣi*) are offered;
in that sacrifice, by the *vāghats*, that is, the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*).
For it is read among the names of the officiating priests in the Nirukta (3.18.3): "The *vāghat*s are the officiating priests who spread the sacrificial grass."
‘Śropamāṇāḥ’: hearing the sound characterized as praise being uttered by them;
such sacrificial posts (yūpas) [are used] ‘in the contests for troops’ (*pṛtanājyeṣu*).
The word *pṛtanājya* denotes battle.
Because it is listed among the names for battle in the passage "ājau pṛtanājyam" (Nirukta 2.17.9),
[the term] *pṛtanājyeṣu* refers to battles;
that is to say, in places of slaughter.
"May the *śṛṅgāṇi* (horns) protect and guard us, the sacrificers.

Regarding the word *śṛṅgāṇi*: from the root *śṛ*, meaning "to injure," [the suffix] *gan* is added according to the rule *śṛṇāterhrasvaśca* (Uṇādi Sūtra 1.123), along with the augment *nuṭ* and the shortening of the root vowel.
*Nisvara*: *dadṛśe*.
By the rule "In the Veda, the *luṅ* and *liṭ* [are used]," the *liṭ* is used in the sense of the *laṅ* (imperfect).
In the word *iryā*, by the rule *ireco re*, there is the substitution of *re* for *ire*;
[this results in] the elision of the accent (*nighāta*).
"O Lord of the Forest, grow with a hundred shoots; may we grow with a thousand shoots."

O Lord of the Forest, you whom this sharpened axe has brought forth for great good fortune—may you grow with a hundred branches; may we grow with a thousand branches, O Lord of the Forest, you whom this sharpened axe has brought forth for great good fortune. (11)
"O Lord of the Forest, you who have been cut at the root, O stump, though you have but one shoot, may you grow forth with a hundred branches—may you manifest specifically.

And we too, possessing a thousand shoots through the lineage of sons, grandsons, and descendants, being possessed of a thousand branches, may we grow forth—may we manifest specifically. This sharpened-edged axe, O stump, [is for] you, for the sake of great fortune."

11 | 1. In the manuscripts kha, ga, ca, ja, pha: ‘kaṭāḥ; in ṇa: ‘kaṣṭakāḥ; in na: pramuktakaṣṭakāḥ. 2. In the manuscripts kha, ga, ja, ṇa, na, bha: in the sense of luṅ; in ca: in the sense of luṅ; in la: in the sense of liṭ.
3. In the manuscripts Kha, Ga, Va, Ja, Ṇa, Na, and Ma, there is no mention of *anighāta*.
4. In manuscript Gha, there is the reading *chinnayūpamūla*.
5. In the manuscripts Kha, Ga, Gha, Ca, Ja, Ṇa, Pha, and Bha, the phrase *aputra...paramparayā* is absent.

He brought forth—that is, he caused to attain—*saubhāgya*, great fortune, characterized by many sounds, according to the ritual procedure (*prakalpena*). In *sahasrabal̥hāḥ*: the word *sahasra* is oxytone because it is the middle member in a compound beginning with a noun (*karmādi*). In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the accent of the first member remains as its original form (*prakṛtisvara*). Regarding *rahaṃ*: from the root *rah* in the sense of "manifestation" (*prādurbhāve*), in the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*) the augment *yāmuṭ* is added by the rule *kidāśiṣi*. The *s* is elided by the rule *skoḥ saṃyogādyoḥ*. The suffix *aṅ* is applied by the rule *liṅyāśiṣyaṅ*. The substitution of *iy* for *a* occurs by the rule *ato yeyaḥ*. The *y* is elided by the rule *lopo vyorvali*. Then the *guṇa* substitution takes place. Thus we have *praṇināya*. This is the form of the root *ṇīñ* in the sense of "leading/attaining," in the perfect tense (*liṭ*) with the suffix *ṇal*. It is not subject to the low tone (*anighāta*) because it begins a new *pāda*. The preceding vowel receives the acute accent (*udātta*) by the rule *liti*. (4)
The ninth hymn, consisting of nine verses beginning with "sakhāyas tava," belongs to Viśvāmitra.
Regarding this, the Anukramaṇī states: "sakhāyaḥ; nine [verses], in Bṛhatī meter, ending in Triṣṭubh.
All other [verses] are Triṣṭubh.
The remaining eight are *bṛhatī*s.
They are employed as *sūktas* in the *bārhata* meters for the *prātaranuvāka* and the *āśvina-śastra*.
This is prescribed in the section beginning with "Now, of this" (*athetasyāḥ*) in the Sūtra: "O friends, come to this Agni" (*sakhāyas ta vāyam agnim ā yāhi*; Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 4.13).
We mortals, your friends, call upon you, the god,
for protection— the Son of the Waters, the fortunate one, who shines brightly, who is well-disposed toward us, and who is free from blemish.
We mortals, as friends, choose you for our protection—the god, the son of the waters, the fortunate one, the brightly shining, the well-disposed, the peerless. 1.
Viśvāmitra praises:

O Agni, we—mortal priests who are your friends because we assist you by offering oblations such as Soma and other sacrificial foods—choose you for our protection. We choose you, the Son of Waters (Aponapāt), the fortunate one endowed with excellent wealth, the one of beautiful luster, the one of noble renown, the one who easily carries us across [to success], the one free from affliction, such a god as you, for our aid. We choose you for our preservation.

*Sakhāyaḥ*: [This is derived from] the root *hyā* in the sense of "speaking" (*prakathane*). With the prefix *samāna-* as an upapada, and with the suffix *iṇ* following the rule for the suffix *ḍit*, [we have] *samāne hya-ścodāttaḥ*. Thus, with *samāna-* as the upapada, and while the term *ḍit* is understood to carry over, the suffix *iṇ* is applied to the root *hyāti*.
Because it has the marker *ṭ*, there is elision of the *ṭi* portion;
by connection with that, there is elision of the *y*. By the rule "In the Veda, [the word] *samāna* [becomes] *sa*, except for *mūrdhan*," there is the substitution of *sa*.
The first syllable of the *upapada* is acute.
Following the recurrence of the term *ṇit*, there is the designation *ṇit* by Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.1.92 (*satyur asaṃbuddhau*).
Then, the *vṛddhi* and *ay* substitutions take place.
The first syllable is udātta. *vavṛmahe*.
[From] the root *vṛṅ* in the sense of “to choose.”

The suffix *liṭ* applies while the rule "in Vedic [usage], the *luṅ*, *laṅ*, and *liṭ* [are used for all tenses]" is in force. There is the presence of the *krādi-gaṇa* and the *vādi-gaṇa*. There is *nighāta* (accentual suppression).

*Ūtaye*: In the case of the root *ava* meaning "to protect," with the word *udāttaḥ* (acute-accented) being understood from the previous rule, it is an indeclinable (*nipāta*) by virtue of the rule *ūtiyūtijūtisātihetikīrtayaśca*, and thus it is acute-accented on the final syllable. *Apām*.
By the rule *ūḍidam*, the case ending is acute. [The word] *subhagam* has its first syllable of the second member accented by the rule *ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi*.
*Supratītim*: by the rule *ṛtādyaśca*, the first syllable of the final member of the compound is udātta.
When you, being urged on by the woods, went forth from your mother as a child, you did not forget that in the beginning; for you have returned here to be present among us once again.

When you, being urged on, entered the woods and went toward your mother, the waters—that turning back of yours was not to be effaced even in the beginning, since you, though far away, became present here.
1. ta-°svaratvam | 2. la-°saṃyogeti° | 3. ta-°guṇaḥ’ is not present | 4. sa-vaiśvāmitrasyārtham | 5. gha-pa-°viśvāmitraḥ stauti’ is not present | 6. ga-ca-na-la-sa-°tvā’ is not present.

O Agni, "kāyamānaḥ" means desiring; "avanā" means the forests; "kānanāni" means the woods. Because you, having left those [forests], "ajagan"—that is, you went to—"mātṛḥ," meaning the waters which are like mothers, you remain there in the waters, having entered them and become tranquil. Therefore, "nivartanam" means your constant dwelling right there, by which destruction is indicated. That destruction "na pramṛṣye"—it is not endured, it is not tolerated. Why? To this he says: because "yat," for which reason, being "dūre," existing in invisibility, you "abhavaḥ," you came to be "iha," in these wooden pieces belonging to us in the form of fire-sticks (*araṇi*). Through friction, you come into our presence in a mere moment. Therefore, your dwelling at a distance does not please us. Regarding this point, Yāska says: "Kāyamānaḥ is *cāyamānaḥ* or *kāmayamānaḥ*. 'O Agni, since you went to the woods, the mothers, becoming tranquil—that return of yours, O Agni, is not endured, because though you are far away, you come into being here while being born'" (Nirukta 4.14). *Kāyamānaḥ*: from the root *kam*, "to desire. With the affix *ṇiṅ*, the present tense (*laṭ*) takes the suffix *śānac*; the elision of the letter *m* is Vedic (*chāndasa*). *Ajagan*: from the root *gam*, "to go. In the *laṅ* tense, the *śap* suffix is elided according to the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi. The *s* suffix is elided by the rule "halaṅyādi. The change to *n* occurs by the rule "mo no dhātoḥ. Due to its connection with the word *yat*, it is not unaccented (*anighāta*); it bears the accent of the augment *aṭ*. *Pramṛṣye*: from the root *mṛṣ*, "to endure. By transposition (*vyatyaya*), the suffix *tap* is used in the passive sense. The *t* is elided by the rule "lopasta ātmanepadeṣu. It bears the accent of the root. *Abhavaḥ*: according to the rule "chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ," the *laṅ* is used in the sense of the present tense (*laṭ*). Due to its connection with *yat*, it is not unaccented.
You have grown beyond the harsh; thus you are well-disposed.
Some go forth, others sit around, resting in the lap of those whose friendship you have sought.
You have grown exceedingly fierce; yet now you are indeed well-disposed. Others go forth, while others sit around you, upon whose lap you rest. || 3 ||

O Agni, you desire to carry beyond—that is, you intensely wish to fulfill—the unthirsting prayer of the praiser by granting it its appropriate fruit; and thus, you remain well-disposed with a satisfied mind. Furthermore, among those sixteen officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) upon whom you have relied in friendship, the other twelve priests, beginning with the *adhvaryu*, proceed toward the *hotṛ* with excellence.
The others—the four beginning with the Udgātṛ—'sit around,' meaning they remain seated all around.
*vavakṣatha*: This is the form of the root *vah* (meaning "to carry" or "to reach") in the desiderative (*san*);
the absence of the reduplication [of the *v*] in the reduplicated syllable is a Vedic archaism, as in the word *sammataḥ*.

The *liṭ* suffix occurs after that [root] ending in the sense of the present; [specifically] after the *thala* suffix. By the rule "the augment *iṭ* is added to an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix beginning with a consonant," the augment *iṭ* is applied.
The suffix *ām* [prescribed] by the rule "kāspratyayādām" does not occur because it is a mantra. *nivātaḥ*. *pra*.
‘Prasamupoda’ is a dual form.
‘Yanti’ is the present tense (laṭ) form of the root ‘iṇ’ meaning ‘to go’.
Due to the connection with the word *anya* in the rule "ekānyābhyāṃ samarthābhyām," there is no *nighāta* (anudātta accent) for the preceding word.
They sit (*āsate*). [The root] *ās* is used in the sense of "sitting."
Because it is superior, there is no destruction.
You are the sword;
[the root] *as* means "to exist."
The letter *s* is elided by the rule "there is elision of the *s* of *tās*";
however, it is not elided [as a sandhi stop] because of its connection with the following word (*yadvṛtta*).
Having passed beyond the constant friendships and having passed beyond the constant enmities,
the guileless and observant ones found him who was hidden, like a lion lurking in the waters.
Having passed beyond all enemies and beyond the eternal flowing waters, they—unerring and guileless—found him resting in the waters like a lion. 4.

1. To protect the forests of *gha*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *pa*, and *la*; not to protect the forests of *na*. 2. The occurrence of *ṇa*, *ta*, and *sa*. 3. With *la* in the middle. 4. Appropriate for *ta*. 5. *Gha* in counsel; *sa* in mantra. 6. The abundance of *gha* and *pa*.

O Agni, you who are free from deceit, O gods who bear no malice—wise, exceedingly far-seeing, and ancient—all of you, having overcome with power the enemies who parch and destroy, found him as he was going forth; they followed and obtained him, who had passed beyond the swift, many, and gathering armies, who was established in the waters, hidden there like a lion entered into a cave, and as terrible as a lion. They sought him out and seized him.

*Īyivāṃsam*: This is derived from the root *iṇ* (meaning "to go") with the suffix *kvasu*, and is established as an irregular form (*nipātita*) by Pāṇini’s rule 3.2.109: *upeyivān-anāśvān-anūcānaś-ca*. It bears the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
From the root *sridh*, meaning "to destroy" or "to dry up," the suffix *kvip* is applied by the rule "kvip ca. The accent belongs to the verbal root.
From the root *sṛj*,
meaning "to go";
the letter *j* is replaced by *c* through metathesis.
The *laṭ* [present tense] suffix is replaced by *śatṛ*; it receives the accent of a suffix (*pratyayasvara*). *Avindan*.
‘Vida lābhe’ is the form [of the root] in the *laṅ* tense.
‘Nicirāsaḥ’:
exceedingly long-lasting.
By the rule *ājaserasuk*, the suffix *asuk* is applied.
It receives the accent of the compound (*samāsasvara*).
Thus: *adruhaḥ*.
The root *druh* is used in the sense of "desire to harm.
The suffix *kvip* is applied in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*) according to the rule beginning with *saṃpadādi*.
In the *bahuvrīhi* compound, the final syllable of the second member is acute by virtue of the rule *nañsubhyām*.
*Dhṛtam*: Regarding the root *dhṛñ* in the sense of "service" (*sevā*), there is a prohibition of the suffix *it* by the rule *śruvakaḥ kiti*. It bears the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
Like a well-dressed woman, he has come to us of his own accord, though hidden from view;
Mātariśvan brought him hither from afar, having churned him forth for the gods.
Like one who has been well-nourished, Agni himself, thus concealed, was brought hither by Mātariśvan from afar, having been churned out from among the gods. 5.

Mātariśvan, the wind, has brought this Agni from afar for the sake of the gods—him who was thus, by his own will, hidden and concealed within the waters, and then produced by churning all around. Therein lies the illustration: *sasuvāṃsam iva*. Just as a father might forcibly bring back a son who is wandering or going away of his own accord, so did he bring him. [The word] *sasuvāṃsam* is derived from the root *sṛ* (to go) with the suffix *liṭ*; its *kasu* affix; and since it is stated that "there is no elision of the case-ending when joined with *iva*," the accent belongs to the affix. [The word] *tmanā*: in the mantras, the word *ātman* undergoes the substitution of *āṅ*, resulting in the elision of the vowel *a* of *ātmanaḥ*. [The word] *itthā*: the suffix *thā* is applied by transposition according to the rule "thā is used in the sense of cause in Vedic [language]. It takes the accent of the affix. [The word] *enam*: in the case of subsequent reference (*anvādeśa*), the form *ena* is substituted for the second case ending according to the rule "dvitīyāṭauḥsvenaḥ," and it is unaccented. [The word] *nayat*: this is the form of the root *ṇīñ* (to lead) in the *laṅ* tense; the absence of the augment *aṭ* is a Vedic peculiarity. [The word] *mātariśvā*: he is one who "breathes" (*śvasiti*) in the mother, the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*); he is thus established as a conventional term by the rule beginning with "śru-bakṣan. ||5||
O carrier of oblations to the gods, mortals have seized you;
O youngest one, through your wisdom, you protect all human beings from evil.
The mortal has grasped you, O bearer of oblations to the gods, so that you may protect all sacrifices for humanity through your wisdom, O most youthful one. 6.

1. *pa*—without interval; 2. *la*—having approached with great force; 3. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-’*—the vowel of the suffix does not exist; 4. *gha*—by churning; 5. *gha*—by one's own will; 6. *ta-*—this [suffix] does not exist.

O Havyavāhana (Bearer of Oblations), O Agni worthy of carrying the oblations (*havya*), mortals—the Adhvaryus and others—took you, who were thus hidden within the waters, for the sake of the gods, that is, for the sake of the deity Pūṣan. They seized you.

O Agni, most youthful one, benefactor of men (*mānuṣa*), because you protect (*abhipāsa*) from all sides all our sacrifices (*viśvān yajñān*) through your ritual action (*ṛtvā*)—that is, through your majesty and your work—therefore [the gods] seized you; this is the connection with the preceding verse. The root *grah* means "to take" (*upādāne*);
because it belongs to the *kryādi* class, the suffix *śnā* is applied.
In *grahajyāvaya*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*).
In *hmahorbhaś candasi*, the letter *h* is replaced by *bh*.
By the rule *tiṅṅatiṅaḥ*, there is the *nighāta* (anudātta) accent.
*Havyavāhana*:
from the verbal root *vah*, meaning "to carry" or "to convey";
with the suffix *yuṭ* being understood [from the grammatical rule], the suffix *yuṭ* is applied according to the rule *hanye'nantaḥpādam*.
There is vṛddhi substitution for the upadhā vowel.
The substitution of *y* occurs for [the semivowel]. Because it begins with a prefix (*apādādi*), it possesses the quality of being unaccented (*anudātta*) according to the Ātmanepada rules.
*Viśvān*:
From the root *viś* in the sense of "entering," the suffix *kan* is applied according to the rule *aśimṛpilaṭiraṇikaṇvaṭiviśibhyaḥ kan*.
Due to the *kittva* (the suffix being marked with *k*), there is an absence of *guṇa* substitution.

In the case of roots beginning with *ad* and so forth, there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix *sva*. Because it does not end in the vowel *a*, the substitute *ad* is applied for the *jha* [suffix]. There is no suppression of accent (*anighāta*) due to the connection with *yathā*. By the rule "and when a *tiṅ* ending has an acute accent," the movement (*gati*) is suppressed. The accent belongs to the verbal root (*dhātusvara*).
Offer oblations to him who performs the perfect sacrifice, the sharp one with purifying luster;
serve the god with obedience—the swift, agile, ancient messenger worthy of praise.

Offer oblations to him who makes the sacrifice well-performed, who is sharp and purifying in his luster; serve with obedience the divine one—the swift, tireless messenger, ancient and worthy of praise. 8.

The sacrificer urges the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*): "O priests, offer oblations with *āhuti*s all around this Agni—him whose radiance is purifying (*pāvaka-śociṣam*), who lies latent within wood and plants (*śīram*), who is possessed of a beautiful sacrifice (*svadhvaram*). Furthermore, quickly honor him with service (*śruṣṭī saparyata*)—this Agni who is swift (*āśum*) in his activity, the messenger (*dūtam*) who acts as the invoker for the gods, the agile one (*ajiram*) who goes swiftly, the ancient one (*pratnam*), the one worthy of praise (*īḍyam*), the shining god (*devam*). Regarding *śruṣṭī*: Yāska states that it is a name for "quickly. Therefore, "honor him quickly. **juhota**: From the root *hu* (in the sense of giving or eating), this is the imperative (*loṭ*). By the rule *juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ*, there is *ślu*-elision of the suffix *śap*. By the rule *śluḥ*, there is reduplication. By the rule *loṭo laṅvat*, it takes the form of the *laṅ* (imperfect); thus, by *tasthasthamipām*, the *tha* is replaced by *ta*. With the word *chandasi* understood, by *tasanasanathanāśca*, the *ta* is replaced by *ta*. *viśvādruṇaḥ*: The *nighāta* (anudātta) accent. *svadhvaram*: In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, by the rule *nansubhyām*, the final syllable of the second member bears the udātta accent. *śīram*: From the root *śīṅ* (to sleep). By the rule *sphāyitañcivañci...* etc., the suffix *ravap* is added. Because it is *kit*, there is no *guṇa* substitution. It has the accent of the affix (*prāyayasvara*). In *pāvakaśociṣam*: *pāva* is the act of purifying, i.e., purity. That which causes this is *pāvaka*. By the rule *āto 'nupasarge kaḥ*, the suffix *ka* is added. It has the accent of the affix. In the *bahuvrīhi*, by the rule *prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*, the first member retains its original accent. *āśum*: From the root *aśu* (to pervade), by the rule *kṛvāpājimi...* etc., the suffix *uṇ* is added. There is *vṛddhi* of the penultimate vowel. It has the accent of the affix. *ajiram*: From the root *aja* (to move or throw), by the rule *ajiraśiśaraśiśithala*, it is a *nipātana* ending in the suffix *kirac*; thus, it has the final udātta accent. *pratnam*: By the rule *pragasya chandasi galopaśca*, there is elision of *ga*. Due to the word *ca*, the suffix *tan* is added. It has the accent of the affix. *īḍyam*: From the root *īḍ* (to praise), the suffix *ṇyat* is added. By the rule *īḍavanda...*, it has the initial udātta accent. *saparyata*: From the word *sapara*, by the rule *kaṇḍvādibhyo yak*, the suffix *yak* is added; it functions in the sense of honoring. This is the second person plural of the imperative (*loṭ*). The suffix *śap* is added. By the rule *ato guṇe*, there is the single-substitute (*pūrvarūpa*) form. It has the *nighāta* accent.
Three thousand, three hundred, and thirty-nine gods have worshipped Agni;
they have sprinkled him with clarified butter and spread the sacrificial grass for him, and then they have established him as the Hotṛ priest.

Three hundred and three thousand gods, and thirty-nine more, have worshipped Agni; they have sprinkled him with clarified butter, they have spread the sacrificial grass for him, and then they have seated him as the Hotṛ priest.
1. The suffixes *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, and *añ* [are applied].

2. In the versions *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, and *bha*, the rule "from this, the suffix *ṇyat*" does not exist. Three times three hundred, three thousand, and thirty-nine—[that is,] those numbering three thousand three hundred and thirty-nine—gods (*devāḥ*) worshipped (*asaparyan*), that is, honored, this Agni.
Furthermore, those gods sprinkled—that is, poured—clarified butter (*ghṛta*) over this Agni;
likewise, for the sake of that Agni, they spread the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). By means of the sacrificial grass, they performed the act of strewing, which is the covering of the altar (*vedi*).
Immediately after that, those gods, having appointed this Agni as the *hotṛ* priest upon that sacrificial grass (*barhis*), seated him there—that is, they established him.
The connection with the preceding clause is: "May these gods vie with this Agni, who is worthy of worship by the gods.
Furthermore, the number of the gods is stated in the *Bṛhadāraṇyaka*: "These are indeed the glories, and the gods are thirty-three."

"Which are those thirty-three? Eight Vasus, eleven Rudras, and twelve Ādityas—those are thirty-one; Indra and Prajāpati are the thirty-second and thirty-third" (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 3.9.1). [The word] *śata* [is derived from] *daśanām daśatām*, with the substitution of *śa* and the suffix *ta*.
ten (10)

*vagamat* means "he came. The suffix *luṅ* is used here in the sense of the imperative (*loḍ-artha*) according to the rule *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*. Because it is treated as *lṛṭ*, the augment *aṭ* is absent by the rule *bahulaṃ chandasyamāṅyoge*. There is *nighāta* (suppression of accent). [The word] *ajñānaḥ*: from the root *akṣū* meaning "manifestation," "eating," or "motion"; by transposition (*vyatyaya*), the suffix *jñānac* is applied in the sense of the object. *citrā* has the acute accent on the final syllable. [The word] *haviṣmate*: the word *havis* ends in the suffix *isi* according to the rule *arciśuci-* etc., and thus has the acute accent on the final syllable. Since the technical rule *svaravidhau vyañjanamavidyamānavat* ("in rules concerning accents, a consonant is as if non-existent") is not observed here, the *tup* suffix lacks the acute accent; instead, the accent of the *isi* suffix remains.
Bring forth a lofty, ancient word for Agni, the Hotṛ-priest, who,
like a wise ordainer, bears the lights of inspired thought.
Bring forth a full and lofty word for the Hotṛ, for Agni—the disposer who bears the lights of inspired hymns. 5.
The sacrificer speaks to the *hotṛ* and the other priests:

"O *hotṛ*s and others, bring forth—that is, accomplish—the great, ancient speech, consisting of hymns (*stotra*), liturgical recitations (*śastra*), and so forth, which was composed by our ancestors; [this speech] for Agni, the wise ordainer of the world, the invoker of the gods, who bears the lights—the splendors consisting of the performance and coordination of the Maruts—for the sake of the inspired ones, the sages, the intelligent priests such as the *adhvaryu*s.
The particle *naḥ* here serves merely to fill out the meter, as there is no logical connection [for its meaning].
Or rather, "like the Creator" (vedhase na):
just as the Creator, the Supreme Lord, the ordainer of the world, produces the luminaries such as the sun and so forth, so too [does he].
Regarding the word *pra*, in Vedic usage it may be separated [from its verb], according to the rule "even those that are separated," and thus it is connected with the word *bharata*.
"Pūryam" means "that which was performed by the ancestors";
[this is derived from] the rule "pūrvaiḥ kṛtam inayau ca," whereby the suffix *ya* is applied.
Due to its being designated as *bha*, there is the elision of the vowel *a*.
The term *pratyayasvara* [is derived as follows]: *bharata*.
The root *bhṛñ* in the sense of "supporting" (*bharaṇe*) belongs to the *bhūvādi* class.
The *nighāta* (elision of accent).
*Bṛhat*: it has the acute accent on the final syllable due to the rule "In the sense of the present tense, *pṛṣat* and *bṛhat* [are *nipātana* formations]."
*bibhrate* [is derived from the root] *bhṛñ* in the sense of "bearing" (*bharaṇe*). [The suffix] *ślu* [is applied] by the rule *juhotyādibhyaḥ*.
In *bhajāmi ta*, there is the substitution of *i* (itvam). In *abhyastānām ādiḥ*, there is the acute accent (*udātta*) on the first syllable.
May our songs increase Agni, from whom the praiseworthy one was born,
he who is beautiful to behold for the sake of great strength and wealth.
May our songs of praise increase Agni, from whom the praiseworthy one is born, he who is beautiful to behold for the sake of great strength and wealth. 6.

This Agni who is born—that which is worthy of praise (*ukthya*)—through these songs (*giraḥ*) consisting of hymns of praise; for the word *uktha* denotes that which is praiseworthy, as seen from its inclusion among the names [of Agni] in the Nirukta: "He who cannot be overcome is *ukthya*" (Nirukta 3.8.6). The meaning is that he becomes exceedingly worthy of praise. And this Agni who is beautiful (*darśataḥ*) to behold for the sake of great strength (*vāja*), food (*draviṇa*), and wealth (*dhana*)—may our songs, those words consisting of praise, increase (*vardhantu*) this very Agni; that is, may they magnify him. The meaning is: "May they honor him. [Grammatical derivation of *vardhantu*: from the root *vṛdh* "to grow," with the causative suffix (*ṇic*). The *guṇa* substitution occurs because the penultimate vowel is light. By the rule "in the Veda both ways" (*chandasyubhayathā*), the suffix is treated as having the force of an *ārdhadhātuka*, resulting in the elision of the *ṇi*. The *jhi* ending is replaced by *anta*; the *u* is substituted by the rule "eraḥ" (Pāṇini 3.4.86); and the *anudātta* accent is applied. [Derivation of *ukthya*: from the root *vac* "to speak," with the suffix *thak* according to the rule "pānitudivacirica... etc. Because it is a *kit* suffix, there is *saṃprasāraṇa* (vowel substitution) by the rule "vacisvapi... etc. *Uktha* is a liturgical recitation (*śastra*). He is *ukthya* because he exists therein as one to be praised. The suffix *yat* is added by the rule "in the sense of 'existing there' in the Veda" (*bhave chandasi*); the *y* is elided by the rule "yasya..."].

1. *ta* occurs in the sense of individual inclusion (*vyaktigatamiśraṇa*). 2. *gha*, *pa*, and *na* are suffixes for ordinal numbers (*pūraṇa*). 3. *ta* is used in the sense of "done by" (*kṛtam*). 4. *ta* belongs to the *juhotyādi* class; [in the root] *bhṛ*, the substitution of *i* occurs for the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) according to the rule *bhṛmṛdaśayaji*. 5. *la* denotes that which is praiseworthy (*praśasya*) and not blameworthy (*anabhīśasya*). 6. Regarding the statement "the letters *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, and *la* do not exist," this indicates elision (*lopa*); the circumflex accent (*svarita*) is indicated by the rule *tisvaritam*; [the suffix] *atac* is applied according to the rule *bhṛmṛdaśayaji*; and it is udātta (acute) at the end of the *cikhad* group.
O Agni, most skilled in sacrifice, worship the gods at the ritual for the one who seeks the gods;
as the joyous Hotṛ, you shine forth, driving away our enemies.
O Agni, most excellent sacrificer at the ritual, worship the gods for the one who seeks the gods; as the joyous Hotṛ priest, you shine forth, transcending all failures. 7.

O Agni, you who are the most excellent sacrificer (*yajiṣṭha*), the best of those who offer sacrifice, perform the worship for the sake of the sacrificer who desires the gods in this ritual (*adhvara*)—that is, for the one who seeks the gods through his own self; worship the gods for that purpose, honoring those who are to be sacrificed to and so forth. Furthermore, as the invoker (*hotṛ*) of the gods, the delightful one who gladdens the sacrificer, you, having overcome the enemies who destroy, shine forth preeminently; you are resplendent. *Yajiṣṭha*: By the rule *tuśchandasi*, the suffix *iṣṭhan* is applied. By the rule *turithemayaḥsu*, there is the elision of *tu*. Because it is marked with *ṇi*, it is acutely accented on the first syllable. *Devayate*: Because the suffix *kyac* is marked with *cit*, it has the udātta accent. The suffix *śap* is unaccented because it is marked with *pi*, and the suffix *śatṛ* is unaccented by the accent of the *lārvadhātuka* [present participle]. When these two undergo a single substitution with *kyac*, by the rule *ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ*, the word *devayac* is acutely accented on the final syllable. Then, by the rule *śataranumaḥ*, the case-ending is acutely accented. *Yaja*: From the root *yaja* meaning "worship of gods, making alliance, giving," the imperative (*loṭ*) is used. The suffix *sip* is replaced by *hi*. By the rule *ato heḥ*, *hi* is elided. There is the *nighāta* (elision) of the accent. *Rājasi*: From the root *rāj* meaning "to shine. There is the *nighāta* [of the accent].
O Purifier, shine forth for us with brilliant and heroic strength;
be near to your worshippers for their well-being.
O Purifier, shine forth for us with brilliant and heroic strength; be present among our praisers for their well-being. 8.

O Purifier (*pāvaka*), O Agni, you who dry up the sin belonging to us—being the one established in the preceding mantra—shine (*dīdihi*) for us (*asme*) with splendor (*dyumat*), that is, endowed with radiance; and with excellent heroism (*suvīrya*), meaning possessed of noble power, wealth fit for giving and enjoyment. Or rather, shine and blaze for our sake so that there may be splendor joined with vigor and excellent heroism. Furthermore, for the well-being (*svastaye*)—the dative used in the sense of the genitive—of the Hotṛ and others who offer hymns of praise concerning you, be most near (*antaḥ*), that is, remain exceedingly close to them for their security and peace. [Grammatical Notes: *Pāvaka*: From the root *pūṣ* (to purify), with the suffix *vul*. Due to the *ṇit*-nature of the suffix, there is *vṛddhi*; *vo* is replaced by *ak*. Because it is in the vocative case, it has the low-pitched (*anudātta*) accent according to Pāṇini 8.1.19. *Dīdihi*: From the root *div* (to play, etc.), with the suffix *yaṅ*. By the rule "lengthening of the vowel in *tujādi*" roots, there is lengthening of the reduplicated syllable. By the rule "a rule preceded by a technical designation (*saṃjñā*) is not obligatory," there is no *guṇa* of the reduplicated syllable. By the rule "frequently in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*), there is elision (*luk*) of the *yaṅ*. In the imperative (*loṭ*), the first person singular ending is *mip*. By the statement "the *carkarīta* [reduplicated present] takes the *parasmaipada* endings and is treated like the beginning," there is elision of the *śap*. *Sip* is replaced by *hi*. By the rule "elision of *v* and *y* before a consonant" (*lopo vyorvali*), there is elision of *v*. Since *hi* is not marked with *pit*, there is no *guṇa*. It receives the *nighāta* (low) accent. * Dyumat*: By the rule "for *div*, *ut*," the vowel *u* is substituted. By the rule "after a short vowel and *tuṭ*," the suffix *matup* is acute-accented (*udātta*). *Suvīryam*: By the rule "also *vīra* and *vīrya*," the beginning of the second member of the compound is acute-accented. *Antaḥ*: That which has an end (*anta*) is *antika* (near). By the rule "from *at*, the suffixes *ini* and *ṭhan*," the suffix *ṭhan* is applied. "Most near" is formed by adding *tamap* according to the rule "in the sense of excess. By the rule "in *tama*, there is the substitute *tā*," the *tā* portion is elided. Because of the *nit*-nature of the suffix, the first syllable is acute-accented. * Svastaye*: The accent is that of the nominal stem (*prātipadika-svara*).

1. *la*—Worship the gods (*devān pūjaya*). 2. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-na-bha-sa*—You exist near [them] (*vartasi*; variant *na-vartase*; variant *ja-ṇa-vartasva*). 3. *ta*—The substitution of *boraka*; the substitution of *āv*. 4. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa*—And the *carkarīta* [intensive]. 5. *ta-la*—Absence of *guṇa*. 232. The Ṛgveda.
The inspired poets, ever-vigilant and chanting their hymns, kindle you—
the immortal bearer of oblations, the increaser of strength.
Thee, the immortal bearer of oblations, who increasest through strength, the inspired singers, ever watchful, kindle together with their hymns. 9.

O Agni, the *viprās*—the inspirers of hymns, the *jāgṛvāṃsaḥ*—awake through vigilance in the performance of rites such as the Agnihotra, the *vipanvavaḥ*—for the word *vipanvan* denotes the wise; this is evident from its inclusion among the names [of the wise] in the Nirukta (3.15.17): "The wise one (*vipaścit*) is *vipanvan*"—these wise singers kindle you, the *havyavāham*, the bearer of oblations, the *amartyam*, the immortal one free from the law of death, the *sahovṛdham*, who increases by means of force (*sahas*) in the form of friction; they thus fully illuminate you with offerings of Soma, clarified butter, and other substances. [Etymological notes: *Viprāḥ*: From the root *ḍuvap* (to sow/secrete seed). From this root, the suffix *ran* is applied according to the rule "*ṛjendrāgravajravipra*" (Uṇādi-sūtra), resulting in the vowel change to *i*. Being a *nī* suffix, it is udātta on the first syllable. *Vipanvavaḥ*: One who goes (*yāti*) toward various praises (*panam*, from *pan* to praise) is a *vipanvyuḥ*. The suffix *ku* is applied according to the rule "*mṛgavādayaśca*"; the elision of the vowel *a* is Vedic. The accent is that of the suffix. *Jāgṛvāṃsaḥ*: From the root *jāgṛ* (to wake). From this, the *liṭ* suffix is used, followed by the suffix *kasu*. The augment *num* is added according to the rule "*ugidacām*". The absence of reduplication is Vedic. The absence of the *iṭ* augment follows the restriction "*vasvekājādasām*". The *guṇa* substitution does not occur due to the rule "*jāgro'viciṇṇalṅitsu*", because there the specific suffix *kasu* is intended to be included. The accent is that of the suffix. *Indhate*: From the root *ji-indhī* (to shine/ignite). This has an internal causative sense. It receives the *nighāta* (suppressed) accent. *Havyavāham*: From the root *vaha* (to carry). The suffix *ṇvi* is applied according to the rule "*vahaśca*". There is *vṛddhi* of the penultimate vowel. The accent is the original accent of the second member of the compound. *Sahovṛdham*: From the root *vṛṣu* (to increase). The suffix *kvip* is applied according to the rule "*kvip ca*". [End of Section 8]

The eleventh hymn, consisting of nine verses, beginning with "agnihotrā," is addressed to Agni; it is by Viśvāmitra and is in the Gāyatrī meter, as indicated by the statement "agnihotrā gāyatram. This hymn is employed in the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina Śastra for the purpose of their respective liturgical recitations.
For it is stated in the Sūtra: "From the Agnihotra, [the verse] 'He goes' is used by way of a Khila" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 4.13).

At the Ādhāna, for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering of the first Pavamāneṣṭi, the Yājyā is "agnihotrā," and the Puronuvākyā is "sa havyavāḍ amartyaḥ. For the Sviṣṭakṛt offering of the second Pavamāneṣṭi, the Anuvākyā is "sāhvān."
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "The two *saṃyājyā* verses are 'sāhvān viśvā abhiyujaḥ' and 'abhimīḷe purohitam'" (*Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 2.1).
In the *dhyas* of the *ābhiplavika* periods, at the third pressing during the *maitrāvaruṇa* recitation, the verse "abhi prayāṃsi" serves as an optional *anurūpa*.
Regarding this, the Sūtra says: "'pra vo vājāḥ', 'abhi yavaḥ', and 'abhi prayāṃsi vāhasā'" (*Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 7.8).
The priest who maintains the sacred fires is the guardian of the sacrifice; he knows the ritual in its continuous succession.
Agni is the invoker, the domestic priest of the sacrifice, he who observes all people; he knows the sacrifice in its proper sequence. 1.

Viśvāmitra praises [Agni]: "The *hotṛ*, the invoker of the gods; the *purohita*, who is beneficial by bringing about desired results right before one's eyes—or rather, the *purohita* because he is placed (*hita*) in front (*puraḥ*), in the eastern part, in the form of the Āhavanīya fire; the *vicarṣaṇi*, the special beholder of the *adhvara*, the sacrifice—[as seen] from the list of names where it is read as 'vicarṣaṇi' and 'viśvacarṣaṇi'—that Agni, being such, knows (*veda*) the sacrifice, such as the Agniṣṭoma and others, sequentially (*ānuṣak*) and all at once. Regarding the word *veda*: from the root *vid* in the sense of "knowing," the substitution of *ṇal* for the *tip* ending occurs according to the rule "vido laṭo vā. There is the *guṇa* strengthening of the light penultimate vowel, and the *nighāta* (suppression) of the accent. Regarding *ānuṣak*: it means that which follows along (*anu-patati*) on all sides (*ā*). From the root *sañj* (variant *gañj*) in the sense of "joining" or "attaching," the *dhātu-sakāra* becomes *sakāra*. The suffix *kvip* is applied according to the rule "kvip ca. By the rule "aniditām," there is the elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-lopa*). The prefix *ā-* takes the *ṣatva* change according to the rule "upasargāt sunoti."

1. In the *sa* manuscript, there is the phrase "in the continuity of the seed-thread" (*sabījaṃ tantusaṃtāne*). 2. In the *la* manuscript, the word "due to the lack of restriction" (*aniyamāt*) is absent. 3. In the *sa* manuscript, it refers to the *pāvamāneṣṭi* sacrifice.
He, the mortal carrier of oblations, the eager messenger, beloved by all— Agni brings them together through our prayer.
He, the bearer of oblations, the mortal, the eager one, the messenger, well-disposed—Agni brings them together through prayer. 2.

The carrier of oblations (*havyavāṭ*), the bearer of your offerings, the immortal (*amartya*)—one who is free from the nature of death—the eager one (*uśig*), desiring the oblation, the messenger of the gods, established for the sake of *cana*, that is, for the food characterized by the oblation; or rather, *cano-hita*: he for whom the food characterized by the oblation is beneficial (*hita*). Such an Agni, through *dhiyā*—that is, through wisdom—*samṛṇvati*, he unites; [the poet] prays that he, being endowed with wisdom regarding the sphere of ritual action, may likewise endow us with such wisdom, even though we are not yet so endowed. *Havyavāṭ*: from the root *vah* "to carry. By the rule *vahaśca*, the suffix *ṇtri* is added. The changes to *ṭh*, *jaś*, and *ca* take place. The accent is on the first syllable of the second member of the compound. *Uśig*: from the root *vaś* "to desire. With the suffix *ij* following the rule *vaśeḥ kicca* while *hanjiḥ* is understood, the suffix *ij* is applied. Because of its *kit*-nature, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) according to the rule *pra-hi-vyā*. The accent is that of the suffix. *Cano-hita*: *canaḥ* is derived from the root *cāy* with the suffix *asun* and a short vowel, according to the rule *cāyater ase hrasvaśca*. From the word *canaḥ*, the augment *kuṭ* is added by the word *cakāra*. There is elision of the *n* in that [augment]. It is accented on the first syllable due to the *nighāta* rule. Since the rule *punaścanaso 'chandasi gati-saṃjñā vaktavyā* prescribes the designation *gati* for *canaḥ* in the Vedic language, the rule *gatiranantaraḥ* applies, resulting in the original accent (*prakṛtisvaratvam*). However, in a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the original accent falls on the first member. *Dhiyā*: the case-ending is accented according to the rule *sāvekācaḥ*. *Ṛṇvati*: from the root *ṛṇu* "to go. In the *leṭ* mood, the suffix *tu* is added because it belongs to the *tanādi* class.
