Agni, the ancient banner of the sacrifice, stirs with wisdom; for his purpose is swift.
Agni, the banner of the sacrifice, through wisdom, perceives; he is the ancient one, for his purpose is swift. 3.

The ancient Agni, the first banner—the indicator—of the sacrifice such as the *agnihotra* and others, being of such a nature, perceives (*cetati*) everything through his wisdom (*dhiyā*). Furthermore, the light of this Agni, whose nature is movement, is indeed the deliverer (*taraṇi*)—that is to say, the dispeller—of this darkness seen in the sky. He perceives (*cetati*): from the root *citī* (to perceive), with the suffix *ti*; it is unaccented (*nighāta*). *Artham*: from the root *ṛ* (to go); by the rule "after *uṣi*, *ku*, *gā*, and *āti*, the suffix *than*," the suffix *than* is applied; there is *guṇa* substitution; because it ends in *ni*, it is udātta on the first syllable. *Taraṇi*: from the root *tṛ* (to cross over); by the rule beginning with "after *ati*, *sṛ*, *bhṛ*, *dhṛ*, *mi*," etc., the suffix *ani* is applied; there is *guṇa* substitution; it takes the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
The gods made Agni their messenger— the Son of Strength, Jātavedas, renowned from afar.
The gods have made Agni their son, renowned from afar, the knower of all beings born of strength, the bearer of oblations. || 4 ||

The gods, the consumers of oblations, made this Agni—the son of strength (saḥasaḥ sūnum), so called because he is produced by the power of churning; the one of ancient renown (sanaśrutam), famous for his eternity; the knower of all beings (jātavedasam), whose wisdom is born—into the bearer of oblations (vahnim), the carrier of the sacrificial offerings.

1. [The letters] gha, ta, pa, sa, and ha [are used]. 2. After *ja*, *ṇa*, and *cana*, [the suffix] *-ita* is used for the sake of understanding (*canase*). 3. [The letters] kha, ja, ṇa, na, bha, and va [are used]. 4. For the root *lagati*, there is the preservation of the original accent (*prakṛtisvaratvam*). 5. After kha, ga, ca, ja, and ṇa, the root *jñā* [is used]. 6. Immediately after *ta* and *la*, the letter *hi* signifies that which has the nature of crossing over (*taraṇasvabhāvam*), meaning it has the nature of spreading everywhere; or rather, it is the fiery energy (*tejaḥ*) whose nature is movement, which is the crossing over (*taraṇa*) of this darkness visible in space—[it is indeed singular]. 7. [The letters] gha and pa [denote] that which causes cessation (*nivartakam*). 8. Because of being produced (*niṣpadyamānatvāt*). 9. Regarding its eternal nature (*sanātanatve*). 5. - 30

They performed [the act]. *Sanaśrutam*: from the root *śru* (to hear), with the suffix *ka* in the sense of the object (*karman*). By the rule "the third case [is used] for the object," there is the preservation of the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member of the compound. *Bahim*: from the root *vah* (to carry). With the suffix *niḥ* still in force, the suffix *nip* is applied by the rule "after *vahi*, *śri*, etc. *Akuṇvata*: from the root *kṛvi* (in the sense of harming or making). Because it is marked with *it*, there is the addition of *nuṭ*. By the rule "after *bhi* and *nṛṣṇi*, *u* with the substitution of *a*," the suffix *up* is applied; the letter *a* is also the substitute for the final portion. In the *laṅ* tense, there is a transposition (*vyatyaya*) resulting in the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) ending *-ata*. There is the *nighāta* (elision of the accent).
He who cannot be deceived, the leader of the human tribes, whose chariot is ever swift and full of heroes.
Unassailable, the leader of the human tribes, Agni is ever a swift chariot for men. 5.

Being the leader of human beings, those born of Manu, the clans, and the progeny—going before them by showing the path of truth—he has come as one who goes. Therefore, he is "tūṇīḥ," meaning he is endowed with haste and free from indolence in order to favor those subjects by setting them toward Vedic rites. He is a "ratha," like a chariot because of carrying oblations; he is "navas" (new) always and at all times in that activity, ever fresh through constant churning. Such an "agni" (fire) is "adābhya," unassailable; the meaning is that he cannot be thwarted by anyone.
*Adābhyaḥ*:
from the root *dambh* (meaning "to deceive"),
with the suffix *ṇyat* in the passive sense (*karmaṇi*), according to the rule stating that it should be stated as "after *dabh*."
There is the vṛddhi substitution for the *u* of the prefix (*upa*). In *adābhyaḥ* (from *na* + *dābhyaḥ*),
because it is a negative (*nan*) compound and specifically a *tatpuruṣa* used in the sense of similarity (*tulyārtha*), the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member is maintained.
*Puraetā*: [derived from] the root *iṇ* meaning "to go," with the suffix *tṛc* according to the rule "ṇvul-tṛcau."
The suffix [guṇa] is udātta on the final syllable because it is a feminine suffix (cittvāt).
[The word is] *mānuṣīṇām*.
The suffix *añ* is applied by the rule "mano-jātau anyatau puk ca";
the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is applied by the rule "ṭiḍḍhāṇañ";
and because of the indicatory letter *ñ*, the word is udātta-accented on its first syllable.
*Tūṇīḥ*:
From the verbal root *jvar* in the sense of "exertion" (*saṃśrama*),

with the suffix *niḥ* being understood from the previous rule, the suffix *ni* is applied according to the rule "after the roots *vah*, *śri*, *yu*, *du*, *glā*, *hā*, and *aś*, [the suffix] *ni* [is added]."
By the rule beginning with "jvarākhara," the suffix *ū* is added.
Because that [suffix] has the marker *ñ*, it is udātta on its first syllable.
In the *saṃhitā*, there is a lengthening by the rule "ḍhalope pūrvasya."
*Ratha*:
The suffix *kvan* is applied by the rule "after the roots *han*, *kuṣ*, *nī*, *ram*, and *kāś*, [the suffix *kvan* is added].
Due to its *kit* status, the nasal is elided by the rule beginning with "for roots taught with an anudātta vowel, etc. (Pāṇini 6.4.37).
Because of the substitution of *ñit*, it is udātta on the first syllable.
*Sadā* is udātta on the first syllable because it is listed among the *svarādi* group as being udātta on the first syllable.
Overcoming all assailants, the immortal will-power of the gods is Agni, the most abundant possessor of all wealth.
Overcoming all assailants, the immortal Agni—the will of the gods—is indeed the most abundant in all goods. 6.

Overpowering—that is, subduing by his own strength and eclipsing—all the attacking armies; therefore, being immortal and not subject to the harm of enemies, the *kratu* (performer) of the gods—the one who nourishes them through the offering of oblations—such is Agni, the most abundant in all things.
The word *tuviśva* signifies "much," as it is listed among the names for "many" in the *Nighaṇṭu* (3.1.2), where it says "tuvi and puru."
The word *śravaḥ* denotes food, as stated in the *Nirukta*: "The name for food is *śravaḥ*, for it is heard" (*Nirukta* 10.3).
Thus, [the two] exist as being endowed with an abundance of various kinds of food to an exceeding degree.
The sense is: since this is so, may he therefore also endow us with many kinds of food.
*Sāhvān*:

This is the accusative dual of the root *apah* in the sense of "enduring" (*marṣaṇe*). Due to the rule of irregular formation (*nipātana*) stating "the forms *dāśvān*, *sāhvān*, and *mīḍhvān*," there is no reduplication, no insertion of the augment *iṭ*, and it takes the *parasmaipada* (active voice) ending. It bears the accent of the *kvasu* suffix.
*Kratuḥ*. [The suffix] *kru* is applied after the root *kṛ*. Due to its being marked with *k*, there is an absence of *guṇa* substitution.
The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
[The word] *tuviśvavastamaḥ* [is derived from] the root *tu*,
which [is used] in the senses of "existence," "injury," and "decay."

From this [root], the *auṇādika* suffix *kip* is applied. Due to its *kittva* (indicatory *k*), there is an absence of *guṇa*. 1. The suffix *lanip*. 2. In the word *viśām*, meaning "of subjects," it does not exist [in some versions]. 3. In the manuscripts *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *na*, *bha*, and *sa*, the form is *yantā*. 4. In the manuscripts *gha*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *pa*, and *ta*, it is *tūṇistvarāvān*. 5. In manuscript *gha* and *pa*, the phrase "endowed with haste" (*tvarāyuktaḥ*) does not exist. 6. In manuscript *la*, it is "in that respective action" (*tattatkarmaṇi*). 7. In the manuscripts *kha*, *ga*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, and *sa*, it is *daṃbhetheti*; in manuscript *na* and *sa*, it is *daṃbhetheti*. 8. In manuscript *ta*, it is *nambhā* in the compound. 9. In manuscript *ta*, the phrase "for this very reason" (*ata eva*) does not exist.

The suffix -asun is udātta at the end [of the word]. *Śravaḥ* (glory): from the root *śru* in the sense of "hearing. It is that in which [glory] is heard; thus, the suffix -asun is applied in the sense of the object (*karman*). In the sense of "exceedingly," *tubiśravas* is formed with the suffix *-tamap* according to the rule "in the sense of excellence, *tamap*. In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, there is the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member.

"Towards the offerings, with his vehicle, the mortal who gives has attained [the glory] of him whose radiance is purifying. (7) *Abhi* | *prayāṃsi* | *vāhasā* | *dāśvān* | *aśnoti* | *martyaḥ* | *kṣayam* | *pāvaka-śociṣaḥ* || 7 ||
"The mortal man, the sacrificer who has given—that is, the giver of oblations—attains from all sides, everywhere, nourishing foods by means of Agni, the bearer of oblations.
Furthermore, he attains his home from the presence of Agni, whose radiance is purifying."
*Prayāṃsi*.
From the root *prīñ*, meaning "to heat," with the causative sense (*ṇyartha*) inherent within it, the suffix *asun* is applied.
The foods (*prayāṃsi*) are so called because they please those who eat;
it is *ādyudātta* (accented on the first syllable) due to the suffix *-ni*.
[The word] *vāhasā*.

With the word ‘ṇit’ understood from the previous rule, the suffix *asun* is applied by the rule ‘vahilādhābhyaśchandasi’. Because it is marked as *ṇit*, there is vṛddhi of the penultimate vowel; the resulting accent is the *nissvara*.
*dāśvān*:

From the root *dāśṛ* in the sense of "giving," by the rule of irregular formation (*nipātana*) stating "dāśvān, sāhvān," there is no insertion of the augment *iṭ* nor reduplication when the suffix *kvasu* follows. It bears the accent of the suffix *krun*.
He attains (*aśnoti*).
[The root] *aś* means "to pervade.
The active voice (*parasmaipada*) occurs by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*).
The elision of the accent.

May we, as inspired sages, attain through our prayers all the well-established [blessings] of Agni Jātavedas. 8. May we, as inspired sages, attain through our prayers all the well-established [blessings] of Agni Jātavedas. 8.

"O wise ones—learned priests such as the *hotṛ* and others who possess born wisdom—we, through nine hymns of praise (*manman*) worthy of reflection belonging to Agni, may we obtain from all sides and attain all well-placed, well-bestowed, and most excellently established treasures, as if they were desired objects. The term *jātavedasaḥ* serves as a specific epithet; he who knows all that has been born is *jātavedas*, meaning "the omniscient one."
Since such a quality of being "born of itself" (jātavedas) is appropriate only for fire, it is fitting that it serves as its specific epithet.
*Sudhitā*:

This is derived from the root *ḍudhāñ* (meaning "to hold" and "to nourish") in its past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*) form. With the word "in the Veda" (*chandasi*) being understood as a governing rule, it is established by the rule "sudhitavasudhitaḥ," etc.
The elision of the suffix *ś* is applied according to the rule "the rest [are irregular] in the Veda, abundantly" (*śeṣchandasi bahulam*).
In the phrase "gatiranantaraḥ," the word *gati* retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*). [May we] attain (*aśyāma*).
The root is *aś* in the sense of pervading (*vyāpti*).
By the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," there is elision (luk) of the suffix śa;
the Parasmaipada ending occurs by way of transposition (vyatyaya);
and the augment yāsuṭ is applied according to the rule "yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdāttaḥ."

By the rule *liṅaḥ salopaḥ*, there is the elision of the *s* [of the suffix]. Because it lacks the final vowel *a*, the substitution of *iy* does not occur. The *s* of the suffix *mas* is elided by the rule *nityaṃ ṅitaḥ*.
The elision (nighāta).
By means of *manmabhiḥ*. [The root] *man* is used in the sense of "perceiving" (*avabodhana*).
The suffix *manin* is applied [to form this word] according to the rule "it is seen after other [roots] as well";
it is without accent (*nissvara*).

O Agni, may we win all desirable things in the contests for booty; in you alone the gods have placed their desires. 9. O Agni! All desirable things—in the contests for booty—may we win. In you, O gods, have they set their hopes. 9.
O Agni, may we win—that is, may we obtain—all desirable, choice, and praiseworthy riches in battles;
for the gods, who were previously worshipped by us, [act] for the sake of bestowing upon us the fruits of our intent.
1. kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-bha: the accentuation of the preceding word. 2. kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa: ‘aminā’ is not present. 3. ta: viprāḥ (sages). 4. la: stomaiḥ (with hymns). 5. ta-la: yajñeṣu (in sacrifices).

"Into you they have entered from all sides"—this is the meaning. The sense is: "In every way, may we obtain the fruit from your presence. Regarding *vāryā*: from the root *vṛṅ* (in the sense of "to partake of"), the suffix *ṇyat* is applied by the rule *ṛhalorṇyat*. By the rule *śeśchandasi bahulam*, the *ś* is elided. By the rule *iḍavanda0* and others, it is udātta on the first syllable. In *vājeṣu*, it is udātta on the first syllable because it belongs to the *vṛṣādi* group. Regarding *saniṣāmahe*: from the roots *vana* or *paṇa* (in the sense of "to partake of"), the *ṣ* is changed to *s* by the rule *dhāravādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ*. In the *leṭ* tense, *sip* is added by the rule *sibbahulam*. Since *sip* is an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix, the augment *iṭ* is applied. The augment *aṭ* is added by the rule *leṭo-ḍāṭau*. The middle voice (*ātmanepada*) occurs by metrical transposition (*vyatyaya*). There is the *nighāta* (elision of accent). Regarding *tve*: for the word *yuṣmad*, the substitute *tvā* is used in the locative case. By the rule *supāṃ suluk*, this is a substitute for the case-ending. By the rule *śe* (Pāṇini 6.1.13), it receives the designation *pragṛhya*. Regarding *īrire*: from the root *īra* (in the sense of "motion"), the substitute *ire* is applied to the *liṭ* suffix. The augment *āṭ* does not occur here because of the rule *ijādeśa gurumataḥ0*. There is *nighāta*.
Since "grammatical rules are optional in the Veda," there is no substitution of *piba*.
[The form] *ipitā* is derived from the root *iṣ* meaning "to go" with the suffix *niṣṭhā*; by the rule *tīpasaha*, the augment *iṭ* is added.
Since the augment *iṭ* is grave (*anudātta*) by the rule "the augments are grave," the *svarita* accent remains.

O Indra and Agni, together with the singer, the conscious sacrifice proceeds; through this [hymn], drink this pressed [soma]. 2. O Indra and Agni! With the singer. Together. The sacrifice. Proceeds. Conscious. Through this. Drink. This. Pressed [soma]. 2.

O Indra and Agni, this sacrifice—which serves as an aid for the singer, the praiser, in the attainment of fruits characterized by heaven and other rewards—and which is the conscious means of the Jyotiṣṭoma and other sacrifices, acting as the animator and nourisher of the senses, this Soma approaches you both.
Being gratified by this speech consisting of our praise, drink, drink this pressed Soma, which has been prepared through the rites of extraction and other refinements.
*jigāti*. The root *gā*, meaning "to praise," is used here in the sense of "going. In Vedic (*chandas*), [the form] *juhoti*—

"O Indra and Agni, you who are the gratifiers of [the gods], the subduers of enemies, the slayers of Vṛtra—the evil one—those who are victorious together, unconquered by anyone, and the supreme bestowers of food (vāja), I invoke you both here at this rite for the purpose of drinking Soma."
*vṛtrahaṇā*: [The root] *han* [is used in the senses of] "killing" (*hiṃsā*) and "going" (*gati*). [The suffix] *kvip* is applied by the rule *brahmaṇavṛtreṣu kvip*.

The substitution of *ṇ* [for *n*] occurs by the rule *ekājuttarapade ṇaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.4.12). The accent is that of the original form of the second member of the compound (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara*). [Thus, one says: *huve*.

When there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix after the root *haya-* by the rule "in the Veda [the suffix is] frequently elided," the term "vocalization" (*saṃprasāraṇa*) from the preceding rule "there is vocalization of *ha*" continues to apply; thus, by the rule "frequently in the Veda," vocalization occurs.
This results in the substitution of *uvaṅ*.
The middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is used by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*).
The elision (*nighāta*). [In the word] *sajitvānā*, [the root is] *ji* in the sense of "to conquer."

The suffix *kanin* is applied by the rule *śīṅkuśiruhajidhisisṛbhyaḥ* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.553). Due to its being marked with *k*, there is an absence of *guṇa* substitution; due to its being marked with *p*, the augment *tuk* is added.

In the rule "samānasya chandasyamūrdha," there is the substitution of *sa* for *samāna*; it has the accent of the original form of the final member of a compound (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratva*). [The word is] *aparājitā*.
In the negative compound *nañsamāsa*, by the rule "in a *tatpuruṣa* with a word of similar meaning as the first member," there is the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member.

In *indrāgnī*, although the rule "also in a *devatā-dvandva*" would have required the original accent of both members, this is prohibited by the rule "not when the second member begins with an unaccented vowel" (*nottarapade 'nudāttādau*); therefore, the accent of the compound itself applies.
*vājasātamā* [is derived from] the root *paṇu* in the sense of "giving. From this [root], the suffix *viṭ* is applied according to the rule *janasanakhanakramagamaḥ*.
The vowel *ā* [is substituted] by the rule "the *anunāsika* of *vidvas* shall be [ā]";
*tamap* is applied by the rule "the suffix *tamap* is used in the sense of excellence";
and the original accent of the final member of the compound is retained according to the rule "the original accent of the final member applies to *kṛt*-derived compounds."
The chanters, skilled in hymns and knowing the ways of praise, sing forth to you both;
O Indra and Agni, I choose for myself strengthening nourishments.
The singers, knowing the paths, praise you both with hymns; O Indra and Agni, I choose for myself nourishing food. ||5||

"O Indra and Agni, the *ukthin*s [praise you]. *Uktha* means a recitation (*śastra*). Those who conclude with that—the Hotṛ and other priests—*pra arcanti*: they honor you both in this ritual with words in the form of hymns. Likewise, the *jaritāraḥ*, the singers who know the melodies (*nīthāvidaḥ*), those skilled in chanting the Sāmans such as the Udgātṛ and others, praise you both for the attainment of their desired fruits. I too, for the sake of obtaining food (*iṣaḥ*), choose you both, O Indra and Agni; I worship you from all sides. This is the meaning. Regarding *vām*: since the word *yuṣmad* (you) is followed by five [words] in the second case, the substitution *vām* occurs according to the rule "for *yuṣmad* and *asmad* in the genitive, dative, and second case," and it is unaccented (*anudātta*). *Arcanti*: from the root *arca* in the sense of "worship. It receives the *nighāta* accent. *Ukthinaḥ*: from the root *vac* in the sense of "speaking. The suffix *thak* is applied in the sense of the object according to the rule "pātṛ-tudi-ciri-ciri... There is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) according to the rule "vacisvapi... etc. *Uktha* means a recitation (*śastra*). Those who have *uktha* are *ukthinaḥ*. The suffix *ini* is applied according to the rule "ata iniṭhanau. The *y* is elided according to the rule "yasya. It has the accent of the preceding vowel. *Nīthāvidaḥ*: from the root *ṇīñ* in the sense of "leading. The suffix *kvan* is applied according to the rule "hani-kuṣi-nirami... etc. Due to its being *kit*, there is no *guṇa* strengthening. From the root *vid* in the sense of "knowing," the suffix *kip* is applied according to the rule "kip ca. It has the accent of the original form of the subsequent member of a compound (*kṛduttarapada-prakṛtisvaratvam*). *Indrāgnī*: because it is used in address (*āmantrita*), it has the acute accent on the first syllable. *Vṛṇe*: from the root *vṛṅ* in the sense of "choosing" or "honoring. It receives the *nighāta* accent. [End of Section 11]
O Indra and Agni, you two shook down the ninety forts held by the Dāsa as their lord,
all at once through a single deed.
O Indra and Agni, you two together with a single deed shook down ninety forts belonging to the Dāsas.

Regarding the phrase "he 'indrāgnī' dāsapatnīḥ": *dāsas* are enemies who "dāsayanti," that is, who "upakṣapayanti" (weaken or destroy). Those whose husbands (*patayas*)—meaning protectors—are such *dāsas* are called *dāsapatnīs*.

"Navatim" means ninety; "purah" refers to such cities of the enemies. "Ekena karmaṇā" means by a single act. 1. "Na-samānajetārau": those who do not conquer each other, but are habitually victorious over others. 2. "La-parasparāpekṣayā jayaśīlau": those who are habitually victorious in relation to one another. 2. "Kha-ga-ca-pa-bha-vāṃ yuvām": O you two, who possess the qualities [denoted by] kha, ga, ca, pa, and bha.
3. [The letters] sa, ga, ca, ja, ṇa, pha, bha, and na are accompanied by [the nasal class].
4. [The letters] gha, pa, śa, and ṣa possess the *śastra* (aspirated quality).
5. In the case of kha, ga, ca, pha, bha, and 'vi-da-jñāne', there is no *udātta* (acute) accent.
6. In the versions kha, ga, ca, ja, ṇa, bha, and sa, the word "upakṣapayanti" does not exist.

With a single effort, you two together shook [them] simultaneously; the ellipsis is "I invoke those Indra and Agni. Regarding *navatitam*: it is the state of nine groups of ten. The suffix *ti* is added, and by the accent rule for *prāyaya*, it is udātta on the final syllable. Regarding *dāspatnīḥ*: from the root *dasu* meaning "to destroy" (*upakṣaye*), one who destroys is a *dāsa*. It ends in the suffix *ac* (pacādyajanta). Being a word denoting a mental state (*cittavat*), it is udātta on the final syllable. Those women whose husbands are always *dāsas*—since it is stated in the *gaṇa* on Pāṇini 4.1.35 that [the suffix *ṅīp* is applied] after *dāsa* in the sense of *sapatnī* etc.—the suffix *ṅīp* is optionally applied according to Pāṇini 4.1.34 (*vibhāṣā sapūrvasya*). The vowel *i* is changed to *n*. In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, there is the preservation of the original accent of the first member (*pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*). Regarding *adhūnutam*: from the root *dhūñ* meaning "to shake" (*kampane*). In the *laṭ* (present) tense, *śnu* is substituted for the root due to its inclusion in the *svādi* group. There is the *nighāta* (elision of the accent of the finite verb). Regarding *ekena*: from the root *iṇ* meaning "to go" (*gatau*). The suffix *kan* is added according to the rule "after *ibhī*, *kṛ*, *pā*, *śal*, *yat*, *mi*, and *ci*, [the suffix] *kan* [is added]. By the rule for *niravādi*, it is udātta on the initial syllable.

O Indra and Agni, from the vicinity of the work, the inspired thoughts proceed forth along the paths of the Eternal Order (Ṛta). 7. O Indra and Agni! From the vicinity of the work, the inspired thoughts proceed forth along the paths of the Eternal Order. 7.

O Indra and Agni, the prayers, the establishers of Soma, the Hotṛ-priests and others who follow the paths—the ways of *ṛta*, the fruit of ritual action—approach you from all sides, moving forward in proximity to the work being performed by us.
Therefore, the sense is: "Come both of you for the sake of drinking the Soma."
Or rather:
the *dhītayaḥ* (devotions), that is, the hymns of praise, proceed toward the paths of *ṛta*—the sacrifice—on all sides;
therefore, you two have come as objects worthy of praise.
They go. [The root] *iṇ* means "to go";
there is the substitution of *yaṇ*.
The elision of the accent (nighāta).
Regarding *dhītayaḥ*:

from the root *dhā* in the sense of "drinking" (*pāne*), the suffix *ktic* is applied in the active sense (*kartari*) by the rule "the suffixes *ktin* and *ktic* are used in the formation of names" (*saṃjñāyām*).
By the rule "ghumāsthā," there is the substitution of *i* for the vowel; because it possesses the quality of being *cit*, it is accented on the final syllable.

O Indra and Agni, yours are mighty powers, excellent abodes, and heroic deeds; for you two, the conquest of enemies has been established. 8. O Indra and Agni! Mighty! Yours! Excellent abodes! And heroic deeds! For you two! The conquest of enemies! Established! 8.
O Indra and Agni, your two powers (*taviṣāṇi*), strengths, and foods (*prayauṃsi*) are well-established in their respective stations, existing in mutual inseparability.
Likewise, that which is "non-solar"—the impelling power through growth—is placed and resides within you two alone.
Therefore, the sense is that in all rites, beginning with the drinking of Soma, Indra and Agni exist together.
*vām*: in the dual case of the sixth [case], *vām* is the substitute for *su*. *sudhasthāni*.
The root *chā* means "to cease from motion. [The suffix] *ka* is applied after a verbal root ending in long *ā* when no upasarga is present.
In the Vedic language (*chandasi*), the word *saha* is replaced by *sadhā* according to the rule *sadhamādasthayoś chandasi*.

O Indra and Agni, you adorn the luminous realms of heaven for the sake of spoils; that heroic power of yours is renowned. 9. O Indra and Agni! The luminous realms! Of heaven! Around! For the spoils! You adorn! That! Of you two! Is known! Forward! Heroic power! 9.
O Indra and Agni, you two who illuminate the luminous realms of heaven, the abode of light— you adorn yourselves on all sides in battles,
being victorious everywhere after having conquered the enemies.
That very prowess and capability of yours clearly proclaims such triumph in combat.
Or rather, [the word] *vājinau* [is used] in the sense of "you two" (*yuṣmad*) in the context of battles (*vājeṣu*). [Note:
1. The reading *ja-ṇa-mārgam* is absent; 2. The rule *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-ma-bha- ‘kticktau ca saṃjñāyām’* does not exist.]

3. *gha-pa-ṛddhidvārā dhayā* (of the waters). "In battles you overwhelm the enemies; you overcome them. The rest is as before. *rocanā*: From the root *ruc* in the sense of "to shine," the suffix *yuc* is applied according to the rule *anudāttetaśca halādeḥ*. It is unaccented (*anudātta*) because it is marked with the *c*-sign. *bhūpathaḥ*: From the root *bhūp* in the sense of "adornment. There is a *nighāta* (elision of the accent). *ceti*: From the root *citī* in the sense of "perception" (*saṃjñāna*). This [root] has the causative meaning (*antarbhāvita-ṇyartha*) inherent within it. The suffix *śap* is elided according to the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*. The elision of the letter *t* is Vedic (*chāndasa*). ||12|| ||1||
In the second anuvāka there are seventeen hymns.
Among them, the seventeenth hymn, beginning with "pra vo devāya," has Viśvāmitra as its seer, Agni as its deity, and is composed in the Anuṣṭubh meter.
Thus it is stated in the Anukramaṇī: "pra vaḥ sapta; ṛṣvān nuṣṭubham."
The seer is Viśvāmitra’s son, Ṛṣa Ṛṣiḥ. According to the technical convention beginning with "maṇḍala," the deity is Agni.
In the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, this hymn serves as the Ājya-śastra.
In the section beginning with "parādvairyāvāvṛtte," it is stated in the sūtra: "One should continue [the recitation] with *pra vo devāyājyam*" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 5.9).

This very hymn is used in the Prātaranuvāka and the Ābhiplavika Śastra for the Agni who was previously established in the preceding mantra, [for whom] "these two worlds, heaven and earth (*rodasī*), are under his control."

The meaning is that, because fire is the illuminator, they possess their own illumination dependent upon it. Furthermore, Yāska [states in Nirukta 7.23]: "The *ūtayaḥ* are the gods who protect by bestowing fruits upon the sacrificer; they 'accompany' (*sacante*)—that is, serve—the strength (*dakṣa*) or power of this fire.
The meaning is that they are dependent on the fire, since the fire is the one that consumes the oblation offered by the sacrificer.

Such is that Agni: "Ṛtāvā," meaning one whose actions are true, and whose intentions are true. Furthermore, the sacrificers—possessing oblations (*haviṣmantaḥ*), having prepared the sacrificial offerings—because he carries the oblation, they "praise" (*īḷate*) that very Agni with words in the form of hymns; that is, they worship him.
Furthermore, "desiring to win"—that is, wishing to obtain wealth and other such things—they take refuge in that very Agni for the sake of protection (*avase*).

*Ṛtāvā*: From the word *ṛta*, by the rule "it denotes that which belongs to it," and by the statement "the suffixes *van* and *vanip* are to be mentioned in the Vedic language (*chandas*"), the suffix *vanip* is applied.
The lengthening of the vowel occurs according to the rule "it is seen [to apply] even in other cases."
Since the suffix *vanip* is *pit*, it is unaccented; thus, the accent of the nominal stem (*prātipadika-svara*) remains.
They associate (*sacante*). [The root] *pac* means "to associate."
The middle voice (*ātmanepada*) occurs by way of transposition;
there is no loss of accent (*anighāta*) due to its connection with *yad-vṛtta*. [They] will strive.
"Sanilābhaḥ" means "desiring that. [The suffix] *kyac* is applied after a nominal ending in the sense of "for oneself," according to the rule "supa ātmanaḥ kyac."

The augment *suk* is prescribed after all nominal stems (*prātipadika*) when the sense is "longing" (*lālasā*), according to the rule "the suffix *kyac* should be stated [after them]"; thus, when *kyac* follows, there is the addition of *suk*.
The accent is that of *kyac*.
He is the controller of these sages; for he is indeed the master of sacrifices.
O Agni, serve him for you—he who is the giver and the protector of wealth.
He is their controller, he is the inspired singer; for he is the purpose of these sacrifices. Pay homage to that Agni for you—he who is the giver and the protector of wealth. 3.

The wise Brahmin, skilled in ritual action—that Agni—is the instigator there for those sacrificers who have performed the offering of oblations despite a lapse in time, by demonstrating the rites as they were prescribed. Furthermore, that Agni is the controller of sacrifices such as the Jyotiṣṭoma, acting as the regulator through the bestowal of their fruits;
for "hi" indicates what is well-known.
For this very reason, he is indeed "the controller of all.
Furthermore, that Agni is "the giver," the bestower of the fruits of rituals such as the Jyotiṣṭoma; he is "magham," which means "wealth worthy of honor.
This is because the word "magham" is listed among its names in the Nirukta (2.10.1) with the gloss "rekṇaḥ" (heritage/property).
And he bestows that wealth upon the wife.
O priests, do you honor—that very Agni who belongs to you—with the offering of oblations;
for the root *duvasyati* means "to serve," as it is listed among the names [of Agni] in the Nirukta (3.5.5): "He bows down (*namasyati*), he honors (*duvasyati*)."
*Yantā*: This is the form of the root *yam* (in the sense of "to cease") in the *tṛc* suffix;
by the rule *ṛdhuśanas*, etc., the substitution of *an* for the final vowel occurs.
*citsvaraḥ* | For indeed,
[the rule] *nipātasya* [prescribes] the long vowel.
*Duvasyata*: "Serve. *Duvaḥ* means service;
[the meaning is] "desiring that."
The suffix *kyac* follows a verbal root ending in *sup*. The form of that [derivative] root in the imperative (*loṭ*) is *dātā*.
The root *ḍudāñ* means "to give.
The suffix *tṛn* is used here in the sense of habit (*tācchīlika*). By virtue of the rule "the first syllable of a word ending in *tṛn* is udātta," it is udātta.
May Agni grant us most auspicious protection for our enjoyment,
from which [protection] he may deliver us in the speckled [clouds], in heaven, among the dwellers on earth, or in the waters.
May Agni grant us most auspicious protection for our enjoyment, from which he may bestow upon us wealth—whether in heaven or in the waters—for our dwelling places. 4.

1. Not by being the giver of oblations (*na-haviṣ-pradātṛtvena*); *la*: by being the giver of oblations (*haviṣāṃ pradātṛtvena*). 2. *ca-sa*: the vowel *kyac*. 3. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa*: by the obstruction of the time (*kālo-parodhena*). 4. *gha*: by the perception of action (*karmadarśanena*). 5. *pa*: that very fire (*eva sa agniḥ*). 6. *ca-la*: worthy of praise (*mahanīyam*). 7. *ca*: the word "hi" is not present. Ka. 2-31:
That Agni, for us who give oblations, [bestows] most peaceful things (*śaṃtamā*)—those which cause supreme happiness through abundance in cattle, sons, and so forth.
The word *śama* denotes a house, because it is listed among the words for "house" in the Nirukta (3.4.21): "Shadow, *śama*, armor."

May he grant such houses for our enjoyment—that is, for the performance of rites such as the *agnihotra*—since from that Agni there comes forth, in every direction, wealth (*vasu*) produced in heaven, on earth, and in the waters; wealth that is abundant and increases even while being spent through gifts, enjoyments, and the like, existing uniquely in each respective world.
The connection with the preceding [sentence] is as follows: "That fire by whose grace the wealth existing in the three worlds comes to us, that is Agni."
For the sake of departure (*vītaye*).
The root *vī* is used in the sense of "motion," "beauty," and so forth.
The suffix *ktin* is applied according to the rule beginning with "after *mantra*, *vṛṣa*, *paśu*, etc. (Pāṇini 3.3.96).
It is accented acute because it is an indeclinable (nipāta) by virtue of being acute (udātta). [The form] *yacchatu* [is derived from] the root *yama*, meaning "to cease" (*uparame*).

*ipagamimayāṃ cha:*—thus, *cha* replaces the *m* of *mi*. The root *pṛṣ* is used in the senses of moistening, sprinkling, and filling. From this root, the suffix *nak* is added according to the *īṇādika* group.
The suffix *mat* [is applied] in the sense of "this belongs to him";
its lack of the acute accent (*udātta*) is a Vedic peculiarity (*chāndasa*).
The chanters kindle Agni—the ancient, shining one—with the prayers of the possessor of goodly wealth; they enkindle him as the Hotṛ-priest, the lord of the people.
The chanters kindle Agni, who shines brightly, the unprecedented one, with his excellent thoughts—Agni, the Hotṛ-priest, the lord of the people. 5.

The *ṛkvāṇaḥ* (those chanting verses), the *śakviṇaḥ* (the capable Hotṛ-priests and others), praise him—the shining one, the one being offered, the unprecedented, who is ever-new at every moment due to his brilliance; the invoker (*hotā*) of the gods, the lord of the people (*viśāṃ viśpatiḥ*), the supreme protector of creatures—they praise that Agni with "good" (*vasvībhiḥ*) and praiseworthy hymns (*dhītibhiḥ*), characterized by devotion toward Agni.
Or rather, they kindle him with "good" and wealthy words, and with the mental efforts (*dhītibhiḥ*) consisting of rites performed for his sake.
They bring about prosperity through activities such as composing hymns and offering oblations.
*Dīdivāṃsam*:
this is the form of the root *div*, meaning "to play" and so forth, in the *kvasu* suffix.
By the rule *tujādīnām*, there is lengthening of the reduplication;
by the rule *lopo vyor vali*, there is elision of the *v* and *y*; thus:
*vasvībhiḥ*.
From the word *vasu*, by means of the suffix *ḍīn* according to the rule *dhyāy-atha*, [the form] *vasavya* is derived; it is unaccented. [The word] *dhītibhiḥ*.
The root *dhā* is used in the sense of "drinking. The suffix *ktic* is applied by the rule *kticktau ca saṃjñāyām*.
Due to its *k*-marker, the substitution of *i* for *ā* occurs according to the rule *ghumāsthāgāpājahātisām hrasvaḥ*.
*citsvara*:
*ṛkvāṇaḥ*. The suffix *vanip* is applied after the word *ṛc* in the sense of the suffix *tup*.
Because [the root] *indh* is known to belong to the *ayasmaya*-class, there is the substitution of *k* for *t*. Due to its status as a verbal base (*pada*), the *jha*-substitution does not occur.
Thus: *indhate*.
The root *indh* means "to kindle" or "to shine.
Regarding the word *vispatim*: according to the rule *parādiś chandasi bahulam*, the acute accent (*udātta*) falls on the first syllable of the second member of the compound.
[The word] *viśām* [is used]; the acute accent (*udātta*) of the case ending is due to the rule *sāvekācaḥ*.
And may you, O Agni, invoked by the gods at our prayers and hymns,
shine auspiciously for us as the most bountiful bestower of thousands.
And so, O Brahman, protect us; be present at our hymns, O God-invoker. Shine auspiciously for us, O Agni, strengthened by the Maruts, as the greatest winner of thousands. 6.

1. *ta-na*: "to the givers"; *na-no* means "to us, the givers of oblations. 2. *ta-ṛddhimat*. 3. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-bha-no*: "it comes to us"; *ta-na-sa*: "wealth comes to us. 4. *ta-gatyādiṣu*. 5. *ta-chakāraḥ*. 6. *ta-pratikṣaṇamabhinavam*. 7. *ta-bhyoḥ*.

Furthermore, O Agni, protect us, the performers of sacrifice (*yajñakāriṇaḥ*), in the sacred word (*brahmaṇi*)—that is, in the hymn being recited by us—so that no defect of deficiency or excess regarding the subject matter of the hymn (*stotraviṣaya*) may occur.
Furthermore, O most excellent invoker of the gods (*devahūtamā*), protect us while we recite the hymns (*uktha*) consisting of the *prauga* and other such portions;
furthermore, O you who are strengthened by the Maruts (*marudvṛdh*).

*sabbahuḷam* (sabbahuḷam): known as *sip*. Because of its being *ādhyātukatva*, there is elision (*lāpa*) from here; the elision of the vowel *ikāra* is known as *sap*. By the rule *leṭo’ḍāṭau*, there is the augment *aṭ*. There is *nighāta* (elision of accent). *ukthedhu*. From the root *vaca* in the sense of "speaking," the suffix *thak* is applied in the passive sense by the rule *pātṛnudi-vacirica*, etc. Due to its being *kittva*, there is *saṃprasāraṇa*. The accent is that of the suffix. *devahutamaḥ*: from the root *hū* (to sacrifice), there is the suffix *kip*. By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, there is *saṃprasāraṇa* and the subsequent form (*pararūpatva*). By the rule *halaḥ*, there is lengthening (*dīrgha*). The accent is the original accent of the second member of the compound (*kruduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*). *śoca*: from the root *śuca* in the sense of "shining. This [root] has the causative sense (*antarbhāvitaṇyartha*) included within it. There is *nighāta*. *marudvṛdhaḥ*: from the root *tṛdha* in the sense of "increasing. The suffix *ka* is applied by the rule *igupadhalakṣaṇaḥ kaḥ*. Due to being in the *marudvṛdhādi* group, there is acute accent on the final syllable of the first member (*pūrvapadāntodāttatvam*). *sahasrasātamaḥ*: from the root *paṇa* in the sense of "giving. The suffix *viṭ* is applied by the rule *janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ*. By the rule *viḍnoranunāsikasya*, etc., there is the substitution of *ā*. The accent is the original accent of the second member of the compound (*kruduttarapadaprakṛtisvaraḥ*).
Now, O Agni, grant us wealth consisting of thousands, offspring, and nourishment— splendid,
full of heroic vigor, most excellent, and undecaying.
Now, O Agni, grant us wealth accompanied by a thousandfold, by offspring, by prosperity, by splendor, and by heroic strength—wealth that is most excellent and inexhaustible. 7.

O Agni, being praised in this hymn, [grant us] that which is "thousandfold" (sahasravat), meaning endowed with the number one thousand; "possessing offspring" (tokavat), meaning accompanied by sons, grandsons, and so forth; "prosperous" (puṣṭimat), meaning providing nourishment—by this, cattle and the like are indicated, which bestow strength and health upon the body through milk and other products;
and "radiant" (ghumat), meaning possessed of light.
By this term, gems, gold, and so forth are included.

*Suvīryam* means endowed with excellent capacity, suitable for use in its intended purposes. *Varṣiṣṭham* means most increased, that is, abundant; therefore, it is *anupakṣitam*, meaning undiminished even when expenditure is being made. Such *vasu*—wealth characterized by gems, gold, cattle, and the like—give (*rāsva*) to us (*naḥ*), that is, bestow upon us quickly (*anu*) without delay.

rāsva.
This is the form of the root *dā* (in the sense of "giving") in the imperative (*loṭ*),
with the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) due to its being included in the *vyāpya* group;
the suffix *śap* is elided because it belongs to the *adādi* class.
The elision [of the final vowel] by *nighāta*. [The form] *sahasravat* [is derived] with the suffix *matup*, where the *v* is substituted for *m* according to the rule "mādupadhāyāḥ".
The word *sahasra* is placed in the middle because it begins with the letter *sa*.

from the root *puṣ* meaning "to nourish."
From this [suffix], *kic* is added.

By the rule "after a short vowel and *ṅe*, [the suffix] *matup* is acute," *matup* receives the acute accent.
*varṣiṣṭham*:
By the rule "priyasthira" and so forth, *vṛddha* is replaced by *varṣa*. It is unaccented (*nisvara*).
*Anupakṣitam*:
Since the root *kṣi* in the sense of "to perish" lacks a long vowel, the suffix *triṇac* does not apply.
Because it is a *tatpuruṣa* compound with an indeclinable as the first member, it bears the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member.
13. "Ā hotā" is the seventh hymn, the second [in this section].
"Ā hotā" is the entry in the Anukramaṇikā.
Regarding the phrase "But Ṛṣabha," the use of the word "but" (tu) indicates that Ṛṣabha is the seer (ṛṣi) of this hymn.
Since [the meter] has not been explicitly stated, it is Triṣṭubh. Agni is the deity.
These ten hymns, beginning with this one and excluding those belonging to the third Aṣṭaka, are prescribed for the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina Śastra in the Triṣṭubh metre.
1. In manuscript *pha*, the phrase "aihikamāmuṣmikaṃ ca" is absent. 2. In manuscript *kha*, the rule "sibbahulaṃ leṭi" is found.
3. *ta* [is derived] from that; 4. *la* from this; 5. *tala* from this.
6. In the manuscripts Kha, Ga, Ca, Ja, and Ṅa, the phrase "praised in this hymn" (*asmin sūkte stūyamāna*) is absent. 7. In the manuscript Ta, [the term] is *poṣaṇakṛt* (the provider of nourishment).

8. In the manuscripts Kha, Ga, Ca, Ja, and Ṅa, it refers to the state of being free from physical defects due to the strengthening of the body through the flow of milk and other substances; in the manuscript Ta, it refers to cows and the like, which bestow strength and health upon the body by means of milk and other such products.

In the section beginning with "Now, of this," it is stated in the Sūtra: "'Ā hotā' [is the refrain] for ten verses; the third and eighth [verses] are in the Triṣṭubh meter" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 4.13).

The delightful Hotṛ has taken his place at the assemblies; he is the true sacrificer, the most wise, the ordainer. Agni, whose chariot is lightning, who has a thousand sons, whose hair is flame—He has spread His splendor over the earth. 1. The delightful Hotṛ has taken his place at the assemblies; he is the true sacrificer, the most wise, the ordainer. Agni, whose chariot is lightning, who has a thousand sons, whose hair is flame—He has spread His splendor over the earth.
He praises Agni: "The Hotṛ, the invoker of the gods;

the delightful one, the inspirer of the singer; the true one, whose actions are real; the most wise, exceedingly intelligent; the sacrificer, the worshipper of the gods; the ordainer, the creator of the entire world.
Endowed with such greatness, that Agni has occupied—indeed, reaches—the *vidathas*, the sacrifices being performed by us.
Furthermore: "Vidhudrathaḥ" means one who possesses flashing lightning as his chariot; "Śociṣkeśaḥ" means one whose hair consists of flames—that is, he is endowed with hair made of fire;

"Sahasraputraḥ" means the son of Bala. Being such, that "Agni" "on the earth"—that is, in the vast intermediate space—"aśret" (from √śri) his "pājaḥ," meaning his own radiance or splendor; he extends it.
Alternatively, existing on the "pṛthivī," the earth, he "seeks" or "possesses" "pājaḥ," meaning strength.

*Mandra*: [derived from] the root *madi*, meaning "to praise, to rejoice, to intoxicate, to sleep, and to move. From this root, the suffix *rak* is applied according to the rule beginning with "sphāyitañca" (Pāṇini 6.1.27).
The augment *num* occurs because of the rule *idi ca*. [Thus:
*asthāt*.
[From the root] *sthā*, "to stop moving."
The *luṅ* suffix is applied while the rule "in Vedic usage, *luṅ*, *laṅ*, and *liṭ* [are used for all tenses]" is in force. By the rule "for *gati*, *sthā*, etc.," there is the elision of *sic*.
There is the *nighāta* (elision of accent).
A sacrificer (*yajvā*).
[The root] *yaja* is used in the senses of "worshiping the gods," "forming an alliance," and "giving. The suffix *ṅīn* is applied according to the rule "after *su-yaj*, the suffix *ṅīn* [is added]."
Because it is a root (pittva), it has the anudātta accent; thus, the accent of the root prevails:
*kavitamaḥ*.
[The root] *ku* means "to sound."
It is derived from the roots *ku* (to sound) or *kū* (to cry out).

According to the rule *aca haḥ*, the suffix *ip* is applied in the sense of either the agent (*kartari*) or the action/state (*bhāve*). Since the suffix *tamap* is marked with *p*, it is unaccented (*anudātta*), and thus the accent falls on the suffix itself.

*Śociṣkeśaḥ*: [The root] *śuci* means "to shine. The suffix *isi* is applied according to the rule: "The suffix *isi* is added after the roots *arc*, *śuci*, *husṛp*, *chad*, and *chard*. Thus, *śociḥ*. [The word *śociṣkeśaḥ* is formed by adding *keśa* to this.]
It is accented on the final syllable by the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the original accent of the first member (*pūrvapadaprakṛtisvara*) applies. [The form] is *aśret*.
The root *śri* in the sense of "service" (*sevā*) takes the *laṅ* suffix when occurring in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
By the rule "the *śap* [augment] is frequently elided in the Veda," there is the elision (*luk*) of *śap*.
Then, the *guṇa* substitution applies as a *sārvadhātuka* [suffix].

The suppression (of the accent). An utterance of homage has been offered to you; accept it, O upholder of *ṛta*, for you who are mindful, O powerful one! As a knower, bring hither the knowers; sit down in their midst upon the sacred grass (*barhis*) for our protection, O worshipful one. *ayāmi te namauktiṃ juṣasva ṛtāvastubhyaṃ cetate sahasvaḥ | vidvān ā vakṣi viduṣo ni ṣatsi madhye ā barhirūtaye yajatra || 2 ||* An utterance of homage has been offered to you; accept it, O upholder of *ṛta*, for you who are mindful, O powerful one! As a knower, bring hither the knowers; sit down in their midst upon the sacred grass for our protection, O worshipful one.
"O you who abide in the *ṛta*! The *yajña* is the *ṛta*, that which has become truth. O Agni, desiring that, I offer—to you—this *namaukti*, a word of salutation; I extend it, I utter it."
"He is powerful; *sahaḥ* means strength. To you who possess that [strength], who are conscious for the sake of the conscious one—the knower of action—to you this expression of homage is made."

"Be pleased with her; resort to the words of salutation being offered by us. 1. [The reading] *madayitā* is found in manuscript *tra*. 2. [The variant] *dyotamāna* is found in manuscripts *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, and *sa*. 3. In manuscript *gha* and *sa*, because the root is *pitta* (anudātta), the accent of the suffix prevails. 4. The particle *ḍā* is absent in manuscripts *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, and *la*. 5. The word *aham* (I) is absent in manuscripts *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *bha*, and *la*.

Furthermore, O wise one, you who are cognizant of the sequence of the gods, bring hither—that is, summon—the wise ones who are cognizant of ritual action. Moreover, O Agni, worthy of sacrifice, for our protection (*utaye*), sit down completely (*ā ni ṣatsva*) in the midst of the strewn sacrificial grass (*barhiṣaḥ*). *Ayāmi*: from the root *iṇ* (to go), belonging to the *bhvādi* class; it is unaccented because it begins the foot of the verse. *Jupasva*: from the root *juṣ* (to enjoy/to serve), belonging to the *tudādi* class; this is the form in the imperative (*loṭ*); it is unaccented. *Vidathe*: from the root *cit* (to perceive/to know) with the suffix *śatṛ*; since the *śatṛ* suffix has an anudātta accent by the rule of *sārvadhātuka* accents, and because the word would otherwise be oxytone, the suffix *śatṛ* causes the case ending to be udātta according to the rule *śataranumaḥ*. The original root accent remains. *Sahasvaḥ*: "possessing strength" (*sahaḥ*); formed with the possessive suffix *matup*. Because the *sakāra* is part of the technical term *bha* by the rule *tasau matvarthe*, the substitution of *ru* does not occur. By the rule *mātupadhāyāḥ*, the *ma* of *matup* becomes *va*. The augment *num* is added by the rule *ugidacām*. After the elision of the *hal* and *ad* vowels, the *nakāra* becomes *ru* by the rule *matuvaso ruḥ*. It is unaccented by the rule of *āmantrita-nighāta* (the vocative is unaccented). *Viduṣaḥ*: from the root *vid* (to know), the following *śatṛ* suffix undergoes the substitution of *vas* by the rule *videḥ śaturvasuḥ*. In the state of being a *bha* stem, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the *vas* by the rule *vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam*. The accent is that of the suffix. *Sasi*: from the root *sad* (to perish, etc.); in the present tense (*laṭ*), the *śap* suffix is elided by the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*. Because the suffix *śi* does not follow immediately, the substitution of *sīd* does not occur. The substitution of *va* occurs by the rule *sadir aprateḥ*. *Yajatra*: from the root *yaj* (to worship/deity); the suffix *atranc* is added by the rule *aminakṣiyajirājivrajīṇaḥ ktraḥ*. It is unaccented by the rule of *āmantrita-nighāta*.
O Agni, may those two Dawns, seeking strength, flow toward you with the ridges of the wind;
when they groom you, the ancient one, with oblations, they stand upon the chariot-seat as if in a dwelling.

Let them two flow forth, O Agni, as they strive for booty with the Dawns, along the ridges of the wind. When they anoint the ancient one with oblations, the two have taken their stand in the dwelling like two chariot-seats.
O Agni, may the two Dawns—the Night and Day, which bring forth food and seek strength—approach you swiftly.

You too, by the paths of Vāta (the Wind), go quickly toward those two, Day and Night. Because Day and Night are mutually bound by their mutual approach, therefore at the evening and morning times, the priests anoint you, the ancient one, on all sides with oblations such as clarified butter.

Furthermore, just as two poles at the front of a chariot are joined together by mutual contact, so may these two great ones—day and night—stand encompassing us within our own home (*duroṇe*) for the sake of accomplishing our rites such as the Agnihotra, returning again and again. May they remain thus.
"Let them flow.
This is the form of the root *du* (to go) in the imperative (*loṭ*). "With the paths."
In the sense of "those who are proficient in paths," the suffix *yat* is applied according to Pāṇini’s rule 4.4.98 (*tatra sādhuḥ*).
By the rule *naḥ taddhite*, there is elision of the *ṭi* portion.
By the rule *tisr̥svaritaḥ*, the vowel becomes svarita.
*tasthatuḥ*. This is the form of the root *sthā* in the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*) with the suffix *atus*.
There is elision of the accent (*nighāta*).
May Mitra and Varuṇa, O powerful Agni, and all the Maruts grant you their favor;
when you stand with your flame, O son of strength, like the Sun, spreading yourself abroad over the dwellings of men.
Mitra and Varuṇa, O powerful Agni, and all the Maruts sing your praise for your favor, when you, O son of strength, stand with your flame like Sūrya, spreading yourself over the peoples, O hero. 4.

1. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-he* [is used] for *yajatra*; 2. *ta-aya*; 3. *ta-kṛto*; *la-kṛte*; 4. *ca-la-ityasmāt*; 5. *la-sa-saderapateḥ*; 6. *ta-uṣasā* does not exist; 7. *ca-ta-upasānakte*; 8. *ta-ahorātre*; 9. *ta-ahorātrayoḥ*.

"O powerful (*sahasvaḥ*) and mighty (*balavān*) Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa (*mitrāvaruṇau*), and all the Maruts (*viśve marutaḥ*), that is, all the gods (*sarve devāḥ*), bring forth (*vahanti*) a beautiful hymn (*suṣṭhu stotram*) for you (*tubhyam*), for your sake (*tvadartham*).
Or rather, all the gods bring forth—that is, they worship (*pūjayanti*)—you (*tvām*) beautifully and with ease (*sukhena*)."
"Because, O Agni, you who have a thousand sons, you are the *asurya*—
the excellent master (*su-artha*),
or alternatively, the excellent impeller (*su-preraka*) by virtue of being the inner controller (*antaryāmin*) of all."
Or rather, Sūrya is one of beautiful prowess;
"toward the *kṣitīḥ*.
The word *kṣiti* denotes human beings, as it is listed among their names in the Nirukta (2.3.6): "The clans (*viśaḥ*) are the *kṣitayaḥ*."
Aiming toward human beings—meaning, spreading out and extending your rays as leaders who show the path to men—you stand, shining with your luster;
therefore, these gods worship you.
*Archan*:
This is the form of the root *arca* (meaning "to worship") in the present indicative (*laṭ*),
with the absence of the augment *aṭ* being Vedic (*chāndasa*).
"tiṣṭhaḥ" is the form of the root "ṣṭhā" in the sense of "ceasing from motion" (gatinivṛtti) in the leṭ mood;
and because it is [part of] the *yuj* class, there is no *nighāta*.

By the rule beginning with *pādhā0*, the substitute *tiṣṭha* is prescribed as having the acute accent on the first syllable (*ādyudātta*) by means of a specific grammatical derivation (*nipātana*); thus, *sūryaḥ* is ādyudātta.
By the rule *rājasūyasūrya0*, because of its derivation from the suffix *kyap*, all meanings are established as correct.
We have indeed fulfilled your desire today, approaching you with uplifted hands and homage;
O Agni, as a sage, worship the gods with sacrifice and with a focused mind, with a prayer that brings success.

We have indeed granted your desire today, having approached you with outstretched hands and with homage. O Agni, as a sage, worship the gods with sacrifice, with mind, and with an unwearied prayer. 5.

"O Agni, we—having raised our hands (that is, having extended our palms) for the acceptance of the oblation—offer (*rarima*) to you today, at this very moment in this rite, the desirable oblation consisting of the *puroḍāśa* and other offerings.

Having approached with reverence (*namasā*), that is, with prostration, and being well-disposed, worship (*yakṣi*) the gods who are worthy of sacrifice; honor the gods with the sacrifice (*yajñena*), that is, with the sacrificial state, by means of a mind (*manasā*) desiring the ritual, that is, by the internal organ."
Furthermore: "O wise one, skilled in ritual action, you—by means of abundant, undiminished *manmana*, that is, a hymn worthy of contemplation—worship the gods."
*Adya* is derived as an irregularly formed word (*nipātita*) by the rule "sadyaḥ-parut-parāryeṣamaḥ... and so forth;
it is also oxytone (having the acute accent on the final syllable).
*rarima*: from the root *rā* in the sense of "giving," in the present tense, with the *liṭ* suffix; by the rule *parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatuḥ* (Pāṇini 3.4.82), there is the substitution of *mā* for *mas*;
and by the rule regarding roots beginning with *krī*, there is the augment *iṭ*.
There is elision of the vowel *ā* by the rule "āto lopa iṭi ca" (Pāṇini 6.4.64).
Due to its connection with the particle *hi*, there is no *nighāta* (elision of accent).
Since the augment *iṭ* is unaccented according to the rule "āgamā anudāttāḥ" (Pāṇini 3.1.3), the accent belongs to the suffix.
Having approached [the root] *pad*—
which [is used] in the senses of "falling," "going," and "sinking"— [one forms the gerund] *upasadya* by means of the suffix *ktvā*.
In the compound, because it is not preceded by the negative particle *nañ*, the suffix *ktvā* is replaced by *lyap*. The accent is that of the *liṭ* suffix. [The form is] *yakṣi*.
The root *yaja* is used in the senses of "worshiping the gods," "forming a connection," and "giving.

In the imperative (*loṭ*), there is elision of the *śap* suffix according to the rule "there is frequent elision in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*). [Then] the substitution of *patva* (the change of *j* to *k*) occurs.
The substitution of *si* for *as* is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*) due to the absence of a prescribed rule;
[the form] is *asaidhat*. The root *sidh* has the meaning of "decay" (*kṣaya*).
In the case of a *tatpuruṣa* compound, the accent is that of the negative particle (*nañ*).
From you, O Son of Strength, many are the succors of the god that go forth, as well as the spoils of war;
grant us thousandfold wealth with unfailing splendor, O Agni, according to the truth.
For from you indeed, O Son of Strength, the many aids of the god go forth; from you come the spoils of war. Grant us thousandfold wealth with guileless splendor—truly so, O Agni! 6.

1. Different from that (ta-bhinnaḥ). 2. In the *tala* and *mataramātta* [metres] (ta-la-ma-taramātte). 3. Due to the connection with *layadgṛta* (la-yadgṛtayogān). 4. All objects (*sarve'rthāḥ*) consist of *ta*, *la*, and *sa* (ta-la-sa). 5. Those to be sacrificed (*ca-yajanīyān*); in the variants *ta-na-ayajanīyān devān*, the word "devān" is absent. 6. In the variants *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa*, the word "yaja" is absent. 7. In the variants *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-bha*, read "pūjaya hi" (worship indeed). 8. Of this (ityasya) according to variant *ta*. 9. Also in that (tyapi) according to variant *ta*.

O Agni, son of strength, son of power! From the presence of the sacrificer—who is himself a god, characterized by divine play, and engaged in the performance of ritual acts—his many previously offered aids, consisting of protections such as the removal of obstacles and the preservation of the rite, indeed go forth;
that is, they surely proceed in various ways toward this sacrificer.
Likewise, the strengths (vāja), meaning foods, go forth.
They reach this sacrificer.
Furthermore, O Agni, grant us wealth consisting of a thousandfold;
likewise, grant us a son who is truthful in character, one who abides in the path of righteousness, and who is endowed with speech that is free from malice and devoid of sin.
From *svata*:
the substitute *tvā* occurs for the word *yuṣmad* in the singular ablative case;
and by Pāṇini Sūtra 7.1.32 (*iseḥ ekavacanasya ca*), the substitute *āt* occurs [for the final vowel].

The single substitute vowel [is unaccented]. In *putra-maham*, because of the rule "also in the Veda" (*chandasi*), which causes it to behave as part of the subsequent member, both vowels are entirely unaccented (*sarvānudātta*).
Give! Huda 248.
Flashing forth with your broad radiance, drive away our enemies, the Rākṣasas, and diseases.
May we abide in the protection of you, the great one who provides excellent refuge, under the guidance of you, the one easily invoked.

O Agni, shining with your broad radiance, drive away our enemies, the Rākṣasas, and all maladies. May we abide in the protection of you, the great one who grants secure refuge; may I be under the guidance of you, the one easily invoked, at the very beginning. 1.

The reciter of hymns (*ukthīlaḥ*) praises: "O Agni, shining intensely with your broad and expansive *pārjasa* (splendor/energy), do you utterly drive away (*vi bādhasva*) the *dvipaḥ*—the enemies who create obstacles to the performance of rites—and likewise the *amīvāḥ*, the *rakṣasaḥ* (demons) that have approached me. [Note: There is a transposition of *su-* in both instances. Drive away those demons; dispel those who cause obstacles to the ritual. Or rather, drive away the *piśācikāḥ* (female goblins) who are intent on coming toward and going away from us. O Agni, in your protection (*śarmaṇi*)—which is the cause of excellent happiness (*suśarmaṇaḥ*) characterized by heaven and the like, which is great (*bṛhataḥ*) having attained majesty through victory over enemies, and which is possessed of being well-invoked (*suhavasya*)—may I be present during your leading forward (*praṇaye*), which is the cause of our happiness, in the places such as the *uttaravedi* (northern altar), where there is a leading forward (*praṇīti*). Leading forward (*praṇayana*) means bringing and depositing here and there. May I thus exist during your leading forward, preceded by the invocation for the performance of the sacrifice. Grammatical notes: * **Pārjasā**: From the root *pā* (to protect). With the suffix *asun* (occurring in the context of the rule *pāter bale juṭ ca*), the augment *juṭ* is added. It is acutely accented on the first syllable because of the *nit*-suffix. * **Pṛthunā**: From the root *prath* (to expand). With the suffix *upa* (occurring in the context of the rule *prathin-dhra-dibhrajāṃ saṃprasāraṇam*), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). The accent is that of the suffix. * **Śośucānaḥ**: From the root *śuc* (to shine) in the *yaṅluk* (intensive without *yaṅ*). By the rule *guṇo yaṅ-lukoḥ*, there is *guṇa* of the reduplicative syllable. The suffix *śānac* is used by transposition (*vyatyaya*). Since the *carkarīta* (intensive) is treated like the *adādi* class, there is elision of *śap*. When the acute accent on the final syllable would otherwise apply due to the *cit* suffix, the rule *abhyastānām ādiḥ* applies, resulting in acute accent on the first syllable. * **Bādhasva**: From the root *bādh* (to press/drive away) in the imperative (*loṭ*). This form is not subject to the *nighāta* (elision of accent) because it begins a new *pāda* (verse-quarter). * **Suśarmaṇaḥ**: From the root *śṛ* (to injure). The suffix *manin* is added according to the *Uṇādi* rules to form *śarman* (protection), meaning "that which wards off suffering. By the rule *sormanasī*, the first syllable of the second member of the compound is acute. * **Syāma**: From the root *as* (to be) in the optative (*liṅ*). The suffix *yāsuṭ* is added according to the rule *yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣu*. There is elision of *s* by the rule *liṅaḥ salopaḥ*. Because of the *it* marker in *yāsuṭ*, there is elision of the *kṣa* and *as* suffixes. There is *nighāta* (elision of accent).
May you be our foremost protector at the breaking of this dawn; may you be our guardian when the sun has risen.
Like a father his own son, O Agni, well-born in body, ever accept my hymn of praise.

You [are] ours; at the dawning of this dawn, you who have unyoked [your horses], you, O wise one, be awake as our protector when it has risen. Like a father his own constant offspring, accept my hymn with your body, O Agni, well-born one. 2.

O Agni, today at the dawning of this present *uṣas*, at its breaking forth and upon the rising of the sun, become our protector—be mindful that "I shall be the guardian of us who have set out in the performance of the *agnihotra*. Some offer the *agnihotra* before sunrise, while others offer it once the sun has risen;
the meaning is: "Be the protector of both these groups."
O thou well-born with a body encircled by flames— meaning, O thou who art well-born or resplendent,
or alternatively, O thou who art well-born by thy own self,
i.e., self-existent— such as thou art, [accept] my hymn, characterized by the *trivṛt*, *pañcadaśa*, and other such forms of praise.
1. The enemies [consisting of] the letters sa, ga, ja, ṇa, and tā;
2. the leading forth (praṇayana) of ja and ṇa; 3. the churning (viloḍana) of ta.

"Accept this [offering]. Regarding this, there is an illustration: "Just as birth [itself]" and so forth. Just as a father, the progenitor, attends to his own legitimate son with embraces and other such acts, so too do you accept this which is being performed by us. [Grammatical derivation: From the root *ucchī* in the sense of "to dispel. In the sense of the instrument (*karaṇe*), the suffix *kin* is applied because darkness is dispelled by it. By the rule beginning with *vaśādi*, the word-form is established. By the rule *tādau ca niti kṛtyatau*, the root accent remains for the prefix *pra*. *Gopāḥ*: From the root *gupū* in the sense of "protection. By the rule *gupū-dhūpa-vicchi-paṇi-panibhya āyaḥ*, the suffix *āya* is added. From that stem ending in *āya*, the suffix *kvip* is applied. By the rule *ato lopaḥ*, the vowel *a* is elided. By the rule *lopo vyoḥ*, the *y* is elided. The accent is that of the root. *Juṣasva*: This is the form of the root *juṣī* in the sense of "affection" and "service" in the imperative (*loṭ*). It receives the *nighāta* (suppression) of accent.
O bull, you who see clearly, shine forth upon the many dark nights as the ruddy one.
O Vasu, lead us and carry us across beyond distress; O youngest god, grant us wealth according to our desire.
O Bull, you are the one who sees; shine forth, O Agni, the ruddy one among the many dark nights. O Vasu, lead us and carry us across the days. O Most Youthful One, make us eager for wealth. 3.

O Bull (*vṛṣabha*) among those who shower down desires, O Agni, you who are the beholder (*anucakṣāḥ*) of the good and evil deeds of men, shining (*ārupaḥ*) in the dark nights, do you shine forth (*vi bhāhi*) in succession through many flames, illuminating them especially. O Vasu, bestower of light upon all and dweller in your own abodes, lead us (*neriṣi*) to the fruits corresponding to our actions; and carry us across (*ati parṣi*), that is, ward off, the distress (*aṃhaḥ*) characterized by our poverty. Furthermore, O youngest (*yaviṣṭha*) Agni, make us desirous (*uśijaḥ*) for wealth (*rāye*); that is to say, fulfill our longings by granting the desired fruits. Regarding the word *anucakṣāḥ*: the root *cakṣiṅ* means "to speak clearly," but here it functions in the sense of "seeing. Following the rule *asun*, and with the addition of the suffix *asun* to *cakṣ* frequently, the suffix *śit* (indicative of present tense) applies, which prevents the substitution of *ly* for *ya*. The accent is on the first syllable of the second member of the compound. Regarding *vṛṣabha*: the root *vṛṣu* means "to serve" or "to rain. Following the rule *abhac*, and with *ṛṣi-vṛṣibhyāṃ kit*, the suffix *abhac* is added. Due to the *kit* designation, there is no *guṇa* strengthening. Because it is not at the beginning of a *pāda*, it does not lose its accent. Regarding *pūrvīḥ*: from the word *puru*, the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is added according to the rule *voto guṇavacanāt*. The lengthening of the initial *u* is Vedic (*chāndasa*). By the accent of the suffix, it is oxytone. Regarding *bhāhi*: the root *bhā* means "to shine. It has an implied causative sense (*antarbhāvitaṇyartha*). This is the form in the imperative (*loṭ*). Regarding *vaso*: the root *vas* means "to dwell. Following the rule *uḥ*, the suffix *upratyaya* is added to *śvasṛ-śvihitṛpyasivasi-* etc. Because it is at the beginning of a *pāda*, it does not lose its accent; optionally, it may have the acute accent on the first syllable. Regarding *neriṣi*: the root *ṇīñ* means "to lead. In the Veda, the present tense (*laṭ*) is used in the sense of the imperative. By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, the suffix *śap* is elided. Since the vocative preceding it is treated as non-existent (*avidyamānavat*), it does not lose its accent because it is at the beginning of a *pāda*. Regarding *parṣi*: the root *pṛ* means "to protect" or "to fill. Because it is in the list of particles (*cādiṣu*), it does not lose its accent. Regarding *kṛdhi*: this is the imperative of the root *ḍukṛñ* "to do. By the rule *ser hapi ca*, *hi* is substituted for *si*; then by *śruśṛpṛkṛvṛbhyaśchandasi*, *dhi* is substituted for *hi*. By *bahulaṃ chandasi*, the suffix *upratyaya* is elided. Because it is at the beginning of a *pāda*, it does not lose its accent. Regarding *rāye*: the root *rā* means "to give. The suffix *ḍai* is added by the rule *rāterḍaiḥ*. By the rule *aḍiḍam* etc., the case ending is acute. Regarding *uśijaḥ*: the root *vaś* means "to desire. The suffix *kip* is added by the rule *vaśaḥ kicca*. Due to the *kit* designation, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). The accent is that of the suffix. Regarding *yaviṣṭha*: from the word *yuvan*, the comparative suffix *iṣṭhan* is added. By the rule *sthūladbṛhad-yuva-*, the subsequent portion is elided and the preceding part undergoes *guṇa*. Because it is a vocative, it loses its accent.

1. *ja*, *ṇa*, *pa* [are used] for the fruits of action (*karmaphala*). 2. *gha* [is used] for the bestowing of desired fruits (*abhimatphalapradāna*). 3. *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *ma*, *bhā* do not exist in the sense of "shining" (*dīpti*). 4. *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *ma*, *rā* do not exist in the sense of "giving" (*dāna*). 5. [The rule applies] when followed by *ta*, *ya*, *ṇa*, etc. Maṇḍala 2.32:
O Apālā, shine forth before us like a bull, having conquered all auspicious fortunes.
O Jātavedas, you are the leader of the first sacrifice; [shine] well-guided in the great [sacrifice].
Invincible, preeminent, the bull, shine forth! Having conquered all blessings, as the leader of the sacrifice, O Jātavedas, drink first of the great draught, O excellent guide. 4.

He who is "unassailable" (*apāḷhaḥ*)— meaning unvanquished and unconquerable by enemies— and who himself conquers the enemy; such as you, the "bull" (*vṛṣabhaḥ*), the showerer of desires— "having completely conquered" (*saṃjigīvān*) all the "forts" (*puraḥ*) of the enemies and the "splendid riches" (*saubhagā*) located therein, shine forth, blazing with flames on every side.

"O *Ajātavedas*—O Agni whose wisdom is born—[be] the leader of such a sacrifice as the *Jyotiṣṭoma*, which is 'well-guided' (*supraṇīta*) because it is beautifully directed, 'great' (*bṛhat*) because it possesses the entire collection of prescribed procedures and rituals, 'protective' (*pāyu*) because it bestows its fruits, and 'first' (*prathama*) because it is performed primarily as the foremost [sacrifice], according to the Vedic scripture: 'This indeed is the first of sacrifices, namely the *Jyotiṣṭoma*. Be the leader of that sacrifice, the one who carries out the performance of the rites such as carrying the oblations and invoking the deities."

*Apāḍhaḥ*. In the sense of "endurance" (*marṣaṇe*), the root *pāḍh* takes the suffix *niṣṭhā*; by the rule "ho ḍhaḥ," the letter *ḍha* is substituted for *ha*, and by the rule "jhapastathordho'dhaḥ," the letter *dha* is substituted for that [ḍha].
By the rule "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ," [the ṣṭu-substitution occurs].

When the ḍha has been elided, the long vowel is applied by the rule "when there is elision of a ḍ-letter, the preceding [vowel] becomes long. The absence of the substitution of *o* for *au* is due to Vedic usage (*chāndasa*).
By the rule *saheḥ sāḍaḥ saḥ*, the sibilant (s) is replaced by a retroflex (mūrdhanya). In the case of *adhyaya-pūrvapada-prakṛtisvara*, the accent falls on the suffix *nam*. [Thus,] *vṛṣabhaḥ*.
The root *vṛṣ* means "to sprinkle.
By the rule *ṛtvigdadhṛk...* [Pāṇini 3.2.59], the suffix *kvip* is applied; thus, by the accent rule for items marked with the *cit* designation, the acute accent falls on the final syllable.

*didīhi*: This is derived from the root *div* (meaning "to play," etc. in its *yaṅluk* (intensive without the suffix) form, in the second person singular imperative (*loṭ*). Due to the rule "a grammatical operation not preceded by a technical designation (*saṃjñā*) is not mandatory," there is no *guṇa* strengthening of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*). Furthermore, because of the principle "all rules are optional in the Veda" (*sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante*), the rule "that which precedes is as if non-existent" (*pūrvatrāsiddham*) does not apply; consequently, by virtue of its subsequent position, the lengthening of the vowel occurs according to the rule "also before a consonant" (*hali ca*).
Subsequently, there is the elision of the *val* (the consonant *v*).
[The form] is *saubhagā*.

Because [the word] *subhaga* is listed among those beginning with the udātta accent in the rule "in the case of the mantra *subhagā*," the suffix *añ* is applied in the sense of "belonging to" (*tasyedam*).
In the phrase "hragasinnacvante," there is a vṛddhi strengthening of the preceding member.

The vṛddhi of the subsequent member occurs because, in the Vedic language (chandas), all grammatical rules are optional. Furthermore, the substitution of "ḍā" for the case-ending (sup) follows the rule "supāṃ suluk."
And by that good fortune, riches are indicated.
Because it ends in *jit*, it is udātta on the first syllable.
Thus: *saṃjigīvān*.
"ji jaye. In Vedic usage, there is the *liṭ* suffix; for that, there is the *kasu* suffix.
By the rule "sanvilaṭojeḥ," there is the substitution of the *kavarga* [the velar stops].
The accent is *prathayasvara*.
The lengthening is Vedic (*chāndasa*).
Regarding *pāyu*: [it is derived from] the root *pā* in the sense of "to protect.
By the rule beginning with *kṛ-vā-pā-ji-mi*, etc., the suffix *uṇ* is applied.
The augment *yuk* is applied by the rule "āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ";
it bears the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
O singer, you who are wise, shining toward the gods, provide many flawless shelters;
like a well-seated chariot, bring us strength, O Agni, for we have the two well-established worlds at our disposal.

O singer, bring us many flawless shelters; shining toward the gods, you of noble wisdom, like a well-yoked chariot, carry us to strength, O Agni, you who are well-established between the two worlds for us. 5.

O singer, you who are faultless, a refuge, and highly wise, shining toward the many gods, bring us strength like a well-yoked chariot; O Agni, bring us both world-halves, which are well-established for us. 5.

1. [The reading] *kartavyakalāpena* is found in manuscripts Kha, Ga, Ca, Ja, and Ṇa. 2. [The reading] *jyotiṣṭomasya* is found in manuscripts Kha, Ga, Ca, Ja, Ṇa, Na, and Bha. 3. [The reading] *ta-dhaḥ* is found in manuscript Ta. 4. [The reading] *lopamadhyamaikavacane* is found in manuscript Ta. 5. [The reading] *subhagamantre* is found in manuscripts Ta and Na-Bha. 6. [The reading] *uttarapadasya ca* is found in manuscripts Kha, Ga, Ca, Ja, Ṇa, and Pha.

O Agni, you who have consumed all at the time of the world's end, you who cause all to decay, you who are possessed of excellent wisdom (*asu-medhāḥ*), and you who shine with your own splendor (*dīdhyānaḥ*), perform for the sake of the gods—the deities worthy of sacrifice—many protections (*puruṇa śarma*): that is, make the rituals such as the *agnihotra*, which are the means to attaining happiness such as heaven, flawless (*acchidrā*).
Make them complete, free from any deficiency in agent, action, or instrument.

Furthermore, O Agni, you who are *satsiḥ*—having restrained your own constant motion and remaining here until the oblation is cast—you must *vakṣi*, that is, carry and bring *vājam*—the food characterized by the oblation offered by us—to the gods.
Therein lies the illustration:
like a chariot (*ratho na*).
Just as a chariot, having carried grain and other goods, brings them to the owner, so it is here.
Furthermore, O Agni, make the two worlds, heaven and earth (*rodasī*), well-united (*sumeke*)—that is, endowed with beautiful forms—as they are illuminated by your own splendors.
*Dīghānaḥ*:
*dīdreti* is a verb meaning "to shine";
from it, the suffix *śānac* [is applied].
In *abhyamānāmādiḥ*, there is the acute accent on the first syllable.
In *sumedhāḥ*,
the suffix *asic* is applied according to the rule "the suffix *asic* is always used after *prajā* and *medhā*."
In the case of a *bahuvrīhi* compound, by the rule "anansubhyām," there is acute accent on the final syllable of the final member. [The form] *satsiḥ* [is derived from] *sadas* with the suffix *si*.
[The root] *sad* means "to sit."
From this [root], the suffix *nin* is applied according to the *Auṇādika* rules; due to the presence of *ni*, there is udātta accent on the first syllable. *Vakṣa*.

In the case of the root *vah* (meaning "to carry") in its imperative (*loṭ*) second person singular (*sip*), there is an elision (*luk*) of the suffix *śap* according to the rule "there is diversely [elision] in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*). Due to the Vedic nature of the text, the substitution of *hi* for the imperative marker occurs even when the sense is not that of command (*ḍhavaktve*). Thus, the form *vahā hi* is established.
The elision of the accent.

O Bull, cause us to swell and quicken our strengths; may you, before whom the two worlds yield milk easily for us, O God, shine with a brilliant luster together with the gods. Let not the ill-will of a mortal encompass us.

Make us swell, O Bull; quicken our strengths. O Agni, you [make] the two worlds yield milk well for us. O God, shining with a beautiful luster together with the gods, let not the ill-will of a mortal encompass us. ||6||
O Agni, you who are the showerer of desires, like a bull (*vṛṣabha*), cause our longings to swell—that is, increase the fruits we desire. Bestow upon us strength (*vāja*) and food; grant them to us.

Furthermore, O radiant God Agni, shining with beautiful luster, together with the gods who are worthy of sacrifice, make these two worlds, Heaven and Earth, well-yielding for us—making them flow abundantly with rain and the granting of desired fruits.
Likewise, may the "evil-mindedness"—the assault instigated by a wicked intellect—of the "immortal enemy" not "surround" us; may it not come upon us from all sides.
*pīpaya*:
from the causative (*ṇyanta*) of the root *pā* "to drink," in the aorist (*luṅ*) with the *caṅ* suffix, there is reduplication and lengthening of the penultimate vowel;
the elision of the *sip* suffix is Vedic (*chāndasa*).
*Jinva*. The roots *ivi*, *jivi*, and *dhivi* have the meaning "to please.
In the *loṭ* (imperative) mood, *num* is added to this root because it is marked with the *it* indicatory letter.

[The suffix] *ṣāp*. By the rule "ano heḥ," there is elision (*luk*) of the imperative suffix *hi*. Since the vocative is treated as non-existent (*avidyamānavat*), it does not follow after a finite verb (*atiṅ*); therefore, there is no *nighāta* (anudātta accentuation).
*sudugdhe* [is derived as follows]: *dohanaṃ* (the act of milking) is *dogdhaḥ* (the milk).
The suffix *ghañ* is used in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāve*).

The form *kutvám* is Vedic (*chāndasa*). According to the rule "that which is [Vedic] has the acute accent on the first syllable" (*ādyudāttaṃ yac chandasi*), the latter member of the compound bears the acute accent. *Durmatiḥ*.
The root *man* means "to understand.
That which thinks (*manyate*) is *mati*, meaning "intellect" (*buddhi*). The suffix *kvi* is applied in the sense of the agent.

The word *duṣṭā* is a compound meaning "corrupted intellect.
