Although the original accentuation of the first member (*pūrvapada*) would have applied by the rule for *avyaya* compounds, the accentuation of the final member (*uttarapada*) as the original accent is applied instead by the rule for *ku*-compounds.

1. *Ta-satsiḥ* means "one who shares" or "one who should be threatened"; alternatively, *satsiḥ* means "you who are a protector. 2. *Ta-gandhyādikaḥ* means "having carried wealth and so forth. 3. *Ta-ime*. 4. *Ta-satsiḥ*: from the root *sanati* or *jñāti*, with the suffix *kin*; because it functions like a *liṅ* (optative), there is reduplication. 5. *Sa-ṣca samavāye*. 6. *Ta-niśvādādyudāttaḥ*. 7. *Sva-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-na-bha-sa-*—there is no *nighāta* (elision of accent). 8. *Ta-pravardhaya*. 9. *Ta-manuṣyasyāsya*. 10. *Sva-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-*—due to the absence of anything following [it]. 252
O Maruts, this man is ever-increasing, in whom you, the increasers of bliss, take delight;
you who overcome the malicious foe in battles and subdue the enemy forever.
O Maruts, men shall attend upon this prospering one, in whom riches have increased, who in battles overcomes the evil-minded, and who day by day strikes down the enemy.

O Maruts, O gods, you who are the leaders of men’s actions, attend upon this Agni—who is being praised by us—as one who increases prosperity through cattle, sons, and other blessings, for the purpose of bringing the oblations.

In response to the question "Of what nature is this Agni?", he says: he is that god in whom riches (*rāyaḥ*) are present on all sides—riches which are *śevṛdhāsaḥ*, meaning they increase happiness through their utility for giving, enjoyment, and so forth.

And those gods who, in battles, in armies, and in the conflicts characterized by them, overcome—that is, they assail—the *dudhyaḥ*, the malicious-minded, harmful enemies; and who, throughout all days (*viśvāhā*), at every moment of that uninterrupted time, [protect] the enemy from themselves—O Agni, make us related to such a one as this: to one who is *varṣapasya* (belonging to the most excellent), *vṛddhatamasya* (most grown), *prabhūtasya* (abundant), *prajāvataḥ* (possessed of offspring), *anamīvasya* (free from disease) for the sake of health, and therefore *śuṣmiṇaḥ* (vigorous) for the sake of strength, and *suvīryasya* (of noble heroism) endowed with excellent capability. Make us connected to such a person.
Alternatively,
this [word *etad*] should be construed as a qualifier of *saṃvat*;
these [words] are used in the sense of the third case (*tṛtīyārthe*).
This is what is meant:
"By means of wealth, by offspring, by health, and by a body endowed with strength—by this fire, make us prosperous."
*Śiśīhi*. This is the imperative (*loṭ*) of the root *śiṣ* (meaning "to sharpen"), where by the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, the suffixal augment (*vikaraṇa*) is replaced by *śnu*.
Because of the optional *ṅit*-character (*ṅittva*) by the rule *vā chandasi*, the substitution of *dhi* for *hi* by the rule *aditaśca* does not take place.
The lengthening is Vedic;
[there is] the *nighāta* accent;
[the form] *mīdaḥ*.
From the root *miha* in the sense of "sprinkling," with the suffix *kasu*, there is the substitution of *ḍha* by the rule *dāśvānsāhānmīḍhuṣca*, as well as the lengthening of the penultimate vowel.

When the vocative suffix *su* is applied, after the elision of the *hal-ādi* (consonant-initial) portion and the elision of the final consonant cluster (*saṃyogāntalopa*), the substitution of *ru* occurs by the rule *matubamo ruḥ saṃbuddhau chandasi*.
Because it begins the quarter-verse (*pādādi*), it is unaccented (*anudātta*).

The maker, who overcomes all worlds, has established his dwelling among the gods; he strives for the gods, for heroic strength, and for the praises of men. 4. The maker—He who overcomes all worlds, the maker who has established his dwelling among the gods; he strives for the gods, for heroic strength, and for the praises of men. 4.

This Agni, the maker (*cakri*) and creator of the entire world, pervades all beings (*viśvā bhuvanā*). According to the Vedic scripture, "Having created that, he entered into it" (*tatsṛṣṭā tadevānuprāviśat*, Taittirīya Upaniṣad 2.6).

That Agni, the maker and the victorious one (*sāsahiḥ*), being capable of bearing the weight of the sacrificial offerings such as the *puroḍāśa* cake, brings the oblation (*duvaḥ*) given by us among the gods, the deities worthy of worship.
And this [Indra] exerts himself toward, or approaches, the gods—those who delight in divine play and who offer praise;
or else, he is one whose nature is to overcome all worlds as he creates them.
The prefix *ā* is used here in the sense of "toward" (*arthe*).
And among the gods, he has performed service and worship;
he who is such as this extends [his life], and so forth, as before.
Moreover, he [is the one] to be praised in the praise of men—the leaders of sacrifice and the reciters.
*Śaṃsa* means praise; it is the *śastra*.
Into that [praise], that Agni comes.
Likewise, for the sake of protecting men—human beings—endowed with excellent heroism (*suvīrya*), he comes.
By this, the all-pervasiveness of fire is established.

The word *cakriḥ* is derived from the root *ḍukṛñ* in the sense of "making" (*karaṇe*). The suffix *kin* is applied according to the rule: "After the roots *āp*, *gam*, *han*, and *jan*, the suffixes *kikin* and *kin* also [occur]. Thus, it is formed with the suffix *kin*.
The dual number is absent due to the lack of a grammatical marker (*liṅga*). Due to the *kit* suffix, there is an absence of *guṇa*.
It is without accent (*nissvara*).

*Sāsahiḥ*: from the root *ṣaha* in the sense of "enduring" (*marṣaṇe*), with the suffix *yah*, and then the suffix *ki* added according to Pāṇini 3.2.171, which states: "The suffixes *kikin* [and *kvip*] are applied after the roots *saha*, *vaha*, *cala*, and *pathi* ending in *yan*. The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
He exerts himself; [the root] *yat* means "exertion. Due to its connection with the word *yat*, there is no loss of accent (*anighāta*).
The suffix *ghañ* is applied in the sense of the abstract action (*bhāva*);
it has the accent on the first syllable (*jisvara*).
In the word *nṛṇām*,
there is optionally no lengthening due to the rule *nṛ ca*;
furthermore, the acute accent (*udātta*) of the case ending is applied by the rule *nāmnyatarasyām*.
In the case of *viśva* and others [in compounds], there is a prohibition of the genitive case by the rule "na lokāvyaya" (Pāṇini 2.3.69).
1. For the sake of health for Kha, Ga, Ja, Ṇa, and A; for the sake of health for La and Ā. 2. [For the sake of] Gha, Ta, and that which is joined with Ajaya.
3. By way of being a qualifier for La; by way of being a qualifier for Ma and Rāya.
4. In the Ta manuscript, "agnena" is absent.
5. In the Ca and Vā manuscripts, "ca" is absent; in the La manuscript, both "ca" and [the following] are absent.
6. In the Kha, Ga, Ja, Na, and Bha manuscripts, there is a doubling [of the consonant].
7. *ta-* [is] capable of enduring the portion of the oblation.

8. *kha-ga-ja-ṇa-na-pa-pha-bha-sa-* or "...... as before" does not exist. 9. *ta-sa* [means that he] extends toward the gods among the gods—that is, toward the singers who delight in the divine—and furthermore (*uta*).

10. There is no [application of the] genitive for those ending in *ta*. 11. It is joined with *śobhana*, *vīrya*, and *īpita*. 12. Regarding *kha*, *ga*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *pha*, *ma*, *la*, and *sa*—in words beginning with *viśva* and others—there is no prohibition of the genitive (*ṣaṣṭhī-pratiṣedha*).
Do not deliver us over to thoughtlessness at the outset, nor to lack of heroes, nor to lack of singers, O son of strength; do not hand us over to reproach, and drive away those who hate us.
Do not deliver us over to indigence at the outset, nor to lack of heroes, nor to lack of cattle, O Lord of Might! Nor to reproach; drive away those things that are hateful. 5.

O Son of Force, Son of Power, O Agni! Do not deliver us over to *amati*—to poverty that has become an enemy; do not make us objects for its possession. Likewise, do not [deliver us] to *avīratā* (lack of heroism) or *aputratā* (childlessness). By the word *vīra*, one who possesses such a quality is indicated. The state of being a *vīra* is *vīratā*. The absence of *vīratā* is *avīratā*; to that [state]. [Do not make us] objects for childlessness. Likewise, do not make us objects for *agotā*—the absence of the abundance of cattle and other livestock. Furthermore, do not make us objects for *nida*—for censure; do not ordain it. Likewise, do you drive away (*apa kṛdhi*) and remove those hateful things caused by the transgression of our actions. Regarding *avīratā*: one who has *vīras* (heroes/sons) is a *vīra*. From the class beginning with *arśas*, the suffix *yac* is applied. The state of that is *vīratā*. For "the state of that," the suffixes *tva* and *tal* are used; here *tal* is used. The absence of *vīratā* is *avīratā*. Regarding the accent of the negative particle (*nañ*), although an acute accent would normally apply, by the rule "in the Veda, the accentuation of words following *nañ* is frequently varied," the subsequent syllable becomes udātta. Regarding *riradhaḥ*: from the root *rādha* (or *sādha*) meaning "accomplishment," in the *luṅ* (aorist) after the causative suffix (*ṇic*), by the rule "after *ṇi*, *śri*, *du*, and *su*," there is the substitution of *caṅ* for *cli*. By the rule "there is elision of *ṇi* before an affix beginning with *an* and not having *i*," the *ṇi* is elided. By the rule "when *caṅ* follows, the penultimate vowel is shortened," the penultimate vowel is shortened. By the rule "doubling occurs when *caṅ* follows," there is reduplication. By the rule "like *san* when followed by a light vowel and *caṅ*," there is the *san*-like behavior. By the rule "the vowel of the reduplicated syllable is long," there is lengthening. Because of the connection with *māṅ*, there is no *aṭ* augment. There is the *nighāta* (suppression of accent). Regarding *agotāyai*: by the word *go*, one who possesses cows is indicated. One who is not a *go* is *ago*. The state of that is *agotā*. The suffix *tal* is added by the rule "the state of that. It takes the accent of the suffix (*lisvara*). Regarding *sahasaputra*: because of the rule "vocatives preceded by a case-ending are treated as *parāṅ* when followed by another vocative," both *sahasaputra* and the following word take the grave accent (*sarvānudātta*). Regarding *nide*: from the root *ṇidi* meaning "censure," the suffix *kvip* is applied in the sense of "that which is produced" (*sapadādvidvābhāve*). By the rule "there is no *num* when the suffix is not prescribed," there is no *num*. By the rule "the case-ending of a monosyllabic word ending in *mā* is udātta," the case-ending is udātta.
O fortunate one, accept graciously at this great sacrifice the food accompanied by offspring;
O Turvidyumna, endow us with greater wealth that brings joy and is full of glory.
Be gracious, O fortunate one, at the beginning of this great sacrifice; bestow upon us abundant wealth that brings joy and glory, O Turvidyumna! 6.

O fortunate one, endowed with beautiful wealth, O Agni, you are the master (īśiṣe) of abundant, great, and plentiful food (vāja) accompanied by progeny; therefore, grant us such [food] in this sacrifice (adhvara) being performed by us, namely in this ritual such as the Agniṣṭoma. [Note:
1. ga-ca-ja-ṇa-na-la-śatrubhūtāya]
By the word *avīra* [is meant] *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-bha-sa*. 2. By the word *vīra* [is meant] *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-pa-pha-bha*. ... There is no [object] that has become an object (*viṣayabhūta*).
+*ta-la-asmāt*... there is no *asmāt*.
3. Do not do that; it does not exist. 4. [It is] due to the faults of actions involving *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *bha*, *sa*.
5. And those who are hateful: *kha*, *ga*, *gha*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *bha*, *dveṣyān*; *ta*, *na*, *dveṣyān*.

6. After *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *bha*, and *ta*, the suffix *tal* occurs in the sense of state (*bhāva*). 7. After *kha*, *ga*, *ta*, *na*, *bha*, and *nañ*, [the suffix *tal* occurs] after the following [word].
8. There is no [suffix *tal*] after *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, *sa*, *para*, *aṅka*, and *ambare*.

Grant us [wealth] in this sacrifice. Furthermore, O Agni of abundant splendor (*tuvidyumna*), rich in much wealth, [grant it] with joy (*mayobhūnā*). "Joy" (*maya*) is a name for happiness, as it is listed among those names in *Nirukta* 3.6.7: "joy is a name for happiness. Being possessed of that [joy], through the cause of providing food and sustenance, and therefore through that which is glorious—possessing fame—with exceedingly abundant wealth, unite us; join us with such riches. [The word] *śagdhi*: from the root *śaklṛ* (to be able) in the imperative (*loṭ*), there is the elision of the suffixal augment (*vikaraṇa*) by the rule "frequently in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*). By the rule "for *hu*, *jhal*, and *ya*, *dhi* is substituted for *hi*" (*hujhalyo hedhiḥ*), there is the substitution of *dhi* for *hi*. Because *dhi* follows a vowel (*api*), it is udātta-accented. [The word] *rāyā*: the case-ending is udātta by the rule "the *u* of *idam* [is udātta]" (*udidam*). [The word] *bhūyasā*: from the word *bahu*, the suffix *īyasun* is added by the rule "when a dual or a distributive word is the upapada" (*dvivacanavibhajyopapade*). When the entire suffix *īyasun* is liable to elision by the rule "elision of *bahu* before *īyasun* and the substitution of *bhū* for *bahu*" (*bahorlopo bhū ca bahoḥ*), the elision applies to the beginning of the suffix by the rule "of the subsequent, the first" (*ādeḥ parasya*, Pāṇini 1.1.54), and *bhū* is the substitute for *bahu*. It is unaccented (*nissvara*). [The word] *sṛja*: from the root *sṛj* (to emit/creatively produce), belonging to the *tud*-class; this is the form in the imperative. There is the *nighāta* (suppression of accent). [The word] *mayobhūnā*: from the root *bhū* (to exist/be) comes the *auṇādika* suffix *ḍup*. [The word] *tuvidyumna*: because it begins a quarter-verse (*pāda*), there is no *nighāta*. || 16 ||
The fifth hymn, beginning with "samidhyamānaḥ," consists of five verses; it is in the Triṣṭubh meter and was composed by Kavaṣa Vaiśvāmitra.

As it has been stated: "The five [verses] beginning with 'samidhyamānaḥ' belong to Kavaṣa Vaiśvāmitra. Furthermore, the application of the ten-hymn collection beginning with "ā hotā" has been specified for the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina Śastra.

In this regard, the following is the fourth [point]: at the Vājapeya sacrifice, for the sacrificial porridge (*caru*) dedicated to Bṛhaspati, "Agni sudītim" is the *yājyā* verse for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.
This is prescribed in the section beginning with "By means of the Vājapeya" in the sūtra: "'Agniṃ sudītiṃ sudaṃśaṃ gṛṇantaḥ' are the two *saṃyājyā* verses" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 9.1).
Being kindled according to the first ordinances, he goes forth, possessing all boons, with his offerings;
he whose hair is flame, whose garment is clarified butter, the purifier, is yoked for the worship of the gods.

Being kindled according to the first law, he is anointed with the hands; he who possesses all boons, whose hair is flame, whose robe is clarified butter, the purifier, the excellent sacrificer—Agni, for the sacrifice of the gods. 1.
He praises it, saying:
"Dharma! Dharma is so called because of its capacity for upholding."
Agni is so called because he is the conductor of the sacrifice or because he is its instrument;
thus says the mantra: "The upholder of dharma, Agni, the accomplisher of the assembly" (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10.92.2).
Such an Agni is first known at the commencement of the sacrifice, being kindled in due order and properly inflamed.
Or alternatively:

being first kindled among the *dharmas*—that is, among the sacrifices which are the means for accomplishing *dharma*—he is the one who possesses all desirable things (*viśvavāraḥ*), meaning he is to be chosen as the object of sacrifice by all (*viśvaiḥ*) sacrificers; and he is the one whose hair consists of flames (*śociṣkeśaḥ*), so called because his "hair" (*keśāḥ*) are the "flames" (*śocīṃṣi*).
He whose purification is through clarified butter—that is, the purifier by means of melting [the butter] through heating;
he who is the purifier (*pāvaka*) of our sins;
he who is possessed of a beautiful sacrifice (*suyajña*).

Agni, being thus, is thoroughly consecrated—that is, properly prepared—with *aktubhiḥ*, meaning with clarified butter and other substances used as means of anointing, for the sake of sacrificing (*yajathāya*), that is, for the purpose of worshipping the gods who are to be worshipped by us.
[Grammatical note: In the first word, the case-ending (*sup*) is replaced by *ḍā* according to the rule *supāṃ suluk*.

Dharma: from the root *dhṛñ* in the sense of "holding" (*dhāraṇe*), the suffix *manin* is applied according to the rule "it is seen [to occur] even after roots other than those ending in *a*. The shortening of the vowel is Vedic (*chāndasa*).
Nissvaraḥ; akkubhiḥ; the root *añj* is used in the senses of manifestation, motion, and eating.
The suffix *ku* is added in the sense of "instrument" (*karaṇa*) by virtue of its frequent occurrence (*bāhulaka*) in the rule "from other [roots] than these" (*añyata ebhiḥ*).
Due to the *kit* designation, there is elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhālopa*). The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
It is being anointed;
that very same root [is used here]; the suffix *yak* is applied in the sense of the object (*karman*).
By the rule "aniditām," there is elision of the penultimate vowel. Thus, *viśvavāraḥ*.

In the sense of "one whose choosing (*vāraṇa*)—that is, selection—is by all the sacrificers (*viśvaiḥ yajamānaiḥ*) through the medium of a cause," the word *vāraḥ* is a form of the root *vṛñ* (meaning "to choose") with the suffix *pyant*.
In the compound *bahuvrīhi*, by the rule "when it is a name (*saṃjñā*), *viśva* [has] acute accent on the first syllable," there is acute accent on the first member of the word. *Ghṛtanirṇik*:
from the root *ṇijir* in the sense of "purification" and "nourishing."
Kip [is applied] because of the *dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa* compound in the sense of "he cleanses the ghee" (*ghṛtaṃ nenektīti*).

1. The substitution of *ta-dāna* etc.; 2. the substitute *bhū*; 3. from the root *bhavati*; 4. *agni*; 5. the nominative case (as found in the recensions kha, ga, ca, ja, ṇa); 6. by means of melting (*vilayanena*); 7. due to the rule of diversity (*bāhulakāt*).

The accent is on the first member of the compound. [The word] *yajathāya* [is derived as follows]: from the root *yaja*, meaning "to worship a deity," "to associate," or "to give"; it takes the suffix *atha* belonging to the *am-ādi* group. The dative case is used in the sense of purpose (*tādarthye*). The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).

As you have performed the office of the Hotṛ for the earth, O Agni, and as you, Jātavedas, being wise, have done so for heaven—so with this oblation do you worship the gods; and, following the human way, further extend this wealth.

As you [performed] the priestly office for Aryaman, O Agni, as for the Earth, as for Heaven, O Jātavedas, being wise—so with this oblation do thou worship the gods, O lord of men; further this sacrifice of ours here. 2.

O Agni, just as you, being the ancient Hotṛ-priest, performed the sacrifice—offered the oblation that is the means of the *hotra*—for the Earth when she was the sacrificer, O Jātavedas, O Agni possessed of born wisdom and knowledge regarding ritual acts; and just as you, having become the Hotṛ for Heaven when it was the sacrificer, offered the oblation—even so, being the Hotṛ in this rite, worship the gods with this oblation being offered by us.
Furthermore, do you now extend this sacrifice being performed by us; that is, lead it to its completion through the fulfillment of its performance.
In this regard, there is an illustration: "like Manu's.
The meaning is: just as you led Manu’s sacrifice to its conclusion through the fulfillment of its performance, so lead this sacrifice to its end.
For example: by the rule *prakāravacane thāl*, the suffix *thāl* is applied;
and by the rule *liti*, the vowel preceding the suffix receives the udātta accent.
*ayajaḥ*: This is the form of the root *yaj* in the *laṅ* (imperfect) tense;
it does not undergo the loss of accent (*anighāta*) because of its connection with the word *yat*.
*hotram*: [derived from] the root *hu*, meaning "to give" or "to eat. By the rule *huyāmāśubhasibhyo 'n*, it takes the suffix *an*, and thus the word is oxytone (accented on the final syllable).
From heaven; the acute accent on the case-ending is by the rule "uḍidam. [The word] cikitvān.
The form *jñāne* is derived from the root *jñā* with the suffix *kasu*;
it has the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
By this [rule].
In the third person singular of the instrumental case for the word *idam*, there is the substitution *an* according to Pāṇini Sūtra 7.2.112 (*anāpyakaḥ*).
*Yakṣi* is the form of the root *yaj* in the *leṭ* mood.
The word *manuṣvat* [is formed as follows]: the suffix *vati* is applied by the rule *tatra tasyeva*.
Since it is not a technical name (*asaṃjñā*), the substitution of *ru* does not occur, according to the supplementary rule *nabho'ñjiromanuṣāṃ vatyupasaṃkhyānam*.
The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
[The form] *tira* [is derived from] the root *tṛ* (to cross) in the imperative (*loṭ*), with the substitution of *śa* by way of irregularity (*vyatyaya*).
In the word *ṛteddhātoḥ*, the substitution of *i* for *e* (itvam) occurs,
and there is the nighāta (anudātta accent).

O Jātavedas, you have three lifespans; O Agni, you have three births from the kindling-sticks. As such, being wise, perform the sacrifice for the gods with them, and be one who brings peace and prosperity to the sacrificer.

Three are the lifespans; three, O Jātavedas, are your births; three are the dawns for you, O Agni. With these, as the one who knows, sacrifice for the protection of the gods; and then become a source of well-being and security for the sacrificer. 3.

O Jātavedas, whose wisdom is born, you have three kinds of life-sustaining forces—consisting of clarified butter, herbs, and Soma—which are ordained as your various types of food. O Agni, there are three Upas (Dawns), comprising the one-day sacrifices and the multi-day sessions; these are the three presiding deities who are your *ajānīs*, the mothers who give birth to you, or rather, the three deities presiding over the dawns who were born after you.

1. *ta-* lacks "tvaṃ". 2. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-pha-* lack "yathā". 3. *ga-ca-tanna-* lack "tvaṃ yathā ca". 4. *ga-ca-na-* lack "divaḥ...devān". 5. *kha-sa-* read "yajñānuṣṭhānaṃ saṃpūrtyā". 6. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-pa-pha-* read "anātaprajña agne". 7. *ta-* lacks "upasaḥ". 8. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-* lack "yadvā...tisraḥ". (Ṛgveda 3.23)

The sisters [are three]. And thus there is a mantra regarding the sister: "One protects the progeny, one protects the vigor, one protects the kingdom. With those deities presiding over the [three] days, together with them, O *ugha*, bestow upon us the food characterized by the oblation (*havis*) which is being offered; [bestow it] upon the gods, that is, upon the gods who are to be sacrificed to. Then, thereafter, being wise (*vidvān*), know [this] and become a source of well-being (*śam*) for the sacrificer; and also become a mixer (*yoḥ*) of happiness. *Tava*: [The word] *yuṣmad* [becomes] *tava* by the rule "yuṣmad-asmad-bhyāṃ ṅaso 'ś" [Pāṇini 7.1.27], and it is udātta. *Tisraḥ*: In the sense of the feminine, the word *tri* undergoes the substitution *tisṛ* by the rule "tricaturor striyām" [Pāṇini 7.2.99]; then the substitution of *r* by "aci ra ṛtaḥ" [Pāṇini 7.2.100]; and the accentuation of the case-ending by "tisṛbhyo jasaḥ" [Pāṇini 6.1.166]. *Ājānīḥ*: from the root *jan* (to be born); the suffix *iṇ* is added in the sense of the agent by "janighasibhyāmiṇ" [Uṇādi Sūtra 2.102]; due to the *ṇit*-nature, there is vṛddhi of the penultimate vowel; the long vowel by "vā chandasi" [Pāṇini 6.1.106]; and the original accent of the final member of the compound. *Avaḥ*: from the root *av* (to protect); the suffix *asun*; it has the *nisvara* (anudātta) accent. *Yakṣa*: this is the form of the root *yaj* (to sacrifice) in the *leṭ* mood. *Yajamānāya*: the suffix *śānan* is added to *yaj* by "pūṅyajoḥ śānan" [Pāṇini 3.2.128]; it has the *nisvara* accent. *Yoḥ*: from the root *yu* (to mix), the suffix *vic* is added by "anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante"; there is guṇa by the rules governing *ārdhadhātuka* suffixes; and it has the original accent of the final member of the compound.

Praising Agni, who is of beautiful luster and fair to behold, we pay homage to you, O Jātavedas, whose will is irresistible. The gods have made you their messenger, their thought, and the bearer of oblations—the navel of immortality.

Praising Agni, the brightly shining, the fair-looking, we pay homage to you, O Jātavedas, who are worthy of praise. The gods have made you their messenger, their steward, and the bearer of oblations—the navel of immortality. ||4||

O Jātavedas, O Agni, knower of everything that has been born—we who are praising you, offering hymns concerning your domain—[we worship] Agni, who is endowed with qualities such as providing food, who possesses beautiful radiance (sudīti), and for that very reason is beautiful to behold (sudṛśa) by all; [we worship] you, who are thus worthy of praise (īḍya), with obeisances and honor you with oblations. Furthermore, O gods—the deities such as Indra and others who are to be worshipped by us—you are "Arati," one in whom there is no delight (rati) or pleasure in sense objects.

Therefore, they made you—who were thus devoted to the *amṛta*, the nectar that is the food of the gods—the navel, the central seat; they made you such a bearer of oblations (*havyavāha*), a messenger (*dūta*). They made you the carrier of sacrificial offerings and the messenger.
For a messenger is indeed of two kinds: the bearer of news and the executor of a task.
The sense is that they have appointed you as a messenger who will accomplish their task.

*Sudītim*: from the root *dīṅ* in the sense of "perishing" (*kṣaye*). It is derived with the suffix *ktin* in the instrumental sense (*karaṇe*), meaning "that by which darkness is destroyed or dispelled."
*dītayaḥ* [is the nominative plural of] *dīptayaḥ*.
In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, by the rule "nañsubhyām," the final syllable of the second member (*uttarapada*) is udātta. *sudṛśam*.
The root *dṛś* is used in the sense of "seeing. From it, the suffix *khal* is applied in the sense of capability (*śakya*).
By the rule "A grammatical operation conditioned by a technical name (*saṃjñā*) is not invariably valid," there is an absence of *guṇa* substitution.
In the word *liti*, the vowel preceding the suffix is acute (*udātta*). *Gṛṇantaḥ*: the root *gṛ* denotes the act of praising.
We pay homage (*namasyāmaḥ*).
Regarding *namas* in the sense of worship, the suffix *kyac* is applied by the rule "namo varivaścitraṅaḥ kyac. The form is derived from that [stem] in the present tense (*laṭ*).
Because it begins with *pāda*, there is no *nighāta* (anudātta accent).
*Dūtam*.
[The root] *dudu* [is used] in the sense of "affliction."
The suffix *kta* is applied by the rule *dutanibhyāṃ dīrghaśca* (Uṇādi Sūtra 3.370). By virtue of that [suffix], there is lengthening of the root vowel. *Dūtaḥ* means one who moves here and there.
The vowel is *pratyaya*.
[It is] *bharati*.
[The root is] *ram*, meaning "in play."
The suffix *ktin* is used in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*).

Regarding the form *akṛṇvan*: from the root *kṛvī*, meaning "to injure" or "to do," in the *laṅ* tense, the suffix *upratyaya* is applied by the rule *dhinvikṛṇvyoracca*, resulting in the substitution of the vowel *a*.
The elision of the accent.

1. In the manuscripts kha, ga, ca, ja, and ṇa, the phrase *svasāraḥ ... iti* is absent. 2. In the manuscript kha, *ta*, and *pa*, it reads *jānānastvam*. 3. In the manuscripts kha, ga, ca, ja, and ṇa, the particle *ca* is absent. 4. In the manuscript *la*, there is the acute accent (*udātta*) on the initial syllable. 5. In the manuscripts kha, ga, ja, ṇa, bha, and pha, there is a vowel lengthening (*varṇadīrgha*). 6. In the manuscript *ta*, there is the preservation of the original accent (*prakṛtisvaratvam*). 7. In the manuscript *ta*, it reads *ratir viṣayeṣu*. 8. In the manuscripts kha, ga, ja, ṇa, pha, and bha, it reads *avajñākārī*; in *ca*, *abhakārī*; and in *sa*, *vaśakārī*. [The verse:
"O Agni, that Hotṛ priest who was before you, more skilled in sacrifice, who was established twice and was auspicious through his own power (*svadhā*)."
O wise one, sacrifice according to his law; bestow wealth upon us at this rite for the banquet of the gods.

O Agni, that Hotṛ who was before you, more skilled in sacrifice, established doubly by his own nature and bringing bliss—according to his law, O wise one, perform the sacrifice for us; establish our rite for the feast of the gods. 5.

O Agni, that Hotṛ—the performer of oblations—who was even prior to you, the first to exist, and who as a most excellent sacrificer, being established by means of *svadhā* (the food called Soma) in both places, namely the middle and the highest station, became a source of bliss (*śambhu*) for the sacrificers. Regarding the second quarter of the verse, Yāska explained it thus: "Established by means of *svadhā* in both ways;
his establishment is twofold, in the middle station and in the highest."

"Śambhu is the source of happiness" (Nirukta 5.3). O Agni, you who possess consciousness—that is, awareness regarding the domain of dharma—perform the sacrifice pre-eminently (*pra yaja*), honoring the gods in accordance with the dharma of that previously designated Hotṛ priest, observing the duties performed by him.
Then, immediately after, O Agni, ordain (*dhāḥ*) this our sacrificial rite (*adhvara*) for the "delight of the gods" (*devavīti*), for the purpose of pleasing the gods.
*Yajīyān*:
from the word *yaṣṭṛ*, the suffix *īyasun* is applied by the rule *turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu*;
in that context, the *tṛ* portion is elided by the rule *turiṣṭhemayaḥsu*.
The word *dvitā* has its first syllable accented (*udātta*). It is derived from the word *dvi* with the suffix *dhā* according to the rule *saṃkhyāyā vidhārthe dhā*.
The substitution of *t* for *dh* is a Vedic archaism (*chāndasa*). It bears the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*). Its meaning is existence (*sattā*).

The root *pad-vṛt* is used in the senses of falling apart, moving, and sinking. From this [root], the suffix *tan* is applied in the sense of habitual action (*tācchīlika*), and it is unaccented (*nisvara*).
"By *svadhā* he establishes the heavenly world for the sacrificer"— thus it is *svadhā*.
The suffix *ka* is applied according to the rule "the suffix *ka* follows a verbal root ending in *a*, when no upasarga precedes."
The word retains the original accent of the final member of the compound (kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratva).
Śambhu: [He is so called] because from him happiness (śam) arises.
The root *bhū* means "existence.

In the rule *viprasabhyo ḍvasaṃjñāyām*, the suffix *ḍu* is applied because of the inclusion of the group beginning with *mita*; due to the indicatory letter *ḍ*, there is elision of the final vowel (*ṭilopa*).
Sacrifice! This is the form of the imperative (*loṭ*) of the root *yaj*. O wise one! (*cikitvaḥ*)
The form *jñāne* is derived from the root *jñā* with the suffix *kasu*.
By the rule *matuvaso ruḥ saṃbuddhau chandasi*, the *n* of *naḥ* is replaced by *ru*. Then follows *naḥ*.
The vowel lengthening [in *dhāḥ*] occurs by the rule "nipātasya. *Dhāḥ* is a form in the Vedic *luṅ* tense from the root *ḍudhāñ*, meaning "to hold" or "to nourish."
The absence of the augment *aṭ* is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*).
Regarding *devavītau*: the *vīti* of the gods—that is, their eating or enjoyment where there is pleasure—is "pleasure for the gods" (*devavīti*).
The suffix *ktin* is applied after the root *vī* in the sense of "beauty" (*kānti*) and so forth, to form a feminine noun.
In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member is retained.
‘Bhavā no agne’ is the fifth hymn, and the sixth [is likewise]. According to the Anukramaṇikā, the phrase ‘Bhavā naḥ’ [indicates the seer];
however, because of the use of the word ‘tu’ in the statement ‘Kato Vaiśvāmitrastu’, the seer of this [hymn] is also Kata, the son of Viśvāmitra.
Agni is the deity.
The application of the hymns for the Prātaranuvāka and the Aśvina-śastra has already been stated.
In the Pravargya ritual, during the Abhiṣṭava, the two verses beginning with "bhavā no agne" are prescribed for use.
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "O Agni, being well-disposed toward us, come hither"—with these two verses (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 4.6).
O Agni, be well-disposed toward us when we approach you; be as gracious in our friendship as two fathers are to their son.
For the dwellings of men are full of guile; therefore, burn up the hostile ones as they come against us.

Be well-disposed toward us, O Agni, when we approach you for friendship—friendship as one who is kind as a father. For the settlements of men yield much; therefore, burn against the hostilities that turn back toward us. 1.

1. *te-homanipādakaḥ agniḥ*. 2. *ta-karmānulakṣya*. 3. *ta-la-ityasya*. 4. In the manuscripts *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *pha*, and *bha*, it reads *svarge loke*; [in others] *talla-ślokam*. 5. *la-kaḥ*. 6. *ta-pūrvadasvaraḥ*. 7. *ta-viniyogaḥ*.

O *agne* (Agni), you, becoming *sumanāḥ*—that is, well-disposed and having a favorable mind for the sake of the successful completion of that rite—upon our approaching toward the rite called *pravr̥jya* which is being performed by us, *sādhuḥ bhava* (be effective); that is, become the accomplisher of the rites pertaining to us.
In this regard, there are two examples.

"Like a friend to a friend, like two parents"—that is, just as a friend, being well-disposed, becomes a benefactor to a friend through the giving of wholesome advice, and just as both parents, mother and father, become helpers for their son by pointing out the right path; even so [is He].
Furthermore, "the dwellers among men," that is, human beings, are indeed "many-scheming," meaning they are possessed of various kinds of malice.
The word *hi* signifies a reason:

because in the world people exist who, through mutual envy and the like, cannot tolerate one another, therefore you, being adverse (*pratīcīḥ*), should burn up the enemies (*arātīḥ*)—those who come against us with hostility; may you, acting as our adversary, protect us. [Note:
*bhava* is derived from *bhavā* + *naḥ*, according to the rule *dyaco'tastiṅaḥ*.]

The dual ending [is applied]. Due to the *kit* designation, there is an absence of *guṇa*. Because of the *cit* designation, it is udātta on the final syllable. *Tiṣṭhantām*: from the root *ṣṭhā* meaning "to stop" (gatinivṛttau). With the prefix *vi-*, by the rule *samavapravibhyaḥ sthaḥ*, the *ātmanepada* ending is applied. There is *nighāta* (elision of accent). *Āyāsaḥ*: from the root *aya* meaning "to go. The suffix *ac* is added according to the *pacādi* group. It is udātta due to the *cit* designation.
Desiring success at the outset, I offer this oblation with fuel and clarified butter for the sake of speed and strength;
as much as I am able, praising with sacred prayer, I offer this divine hymn for the attainment of a hundredfold gain.

Desiring [your favor], O Agni, with fuel and with clarified butter, I offer this oblation for speed and for strength. As much as I am able, praising you with a sacred prayer, I offer this divine hymn for the attainment of a hundredfold wealth. 3.

O Agni, desiring wealth—that is, I, the sacrificer longing for riches—I offer the oblation (*havya*), such as the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) and other offerings suitable for the invocation, together with fuel (*idhma*)—the collection of wood used for kindling—and with clarified butter (*ghṛta*). For what purpose? For *tarasa*, meaning for speed, so that your constant movement may be accomplished; for *bala*, meaning for strength, so that you may have the capacity to bear the burden of the sacrificial cake and other offerings. I cast the oblation into you. Furthermore, praising you with *brahma*—that is, extolling you with hymns—I offer as much as I am able to bear, as much wealth as I can carry. And you, make this *dhi*—this praise directed toward you—which we are performing, divine (*devī*), radiant, and exceedingly abundant, for the sake of attaining immeasurable wealth (*śataseyāya*). Regarding the words: *Idhman*: from the root *indh* (to kindle). That by which fire is kindled is *idhma*, a specific type of wood. By the rule "from *iṣ*, *yudh*, *indh*, *das*, and *sṛ*, the suffix *mak* [is added] in the sense of an instrument," the suffix *mak* is applied. Due to its being a *kit* suffix, there is the elision of the nasal (*n*). It has the accent of the first member (*prāyayasvara*). *Icchamānaḥ*: from the root *iṣ* (to desire). There is an irregularity in the application of the suffix *śānac*. By the rule "for *iṣ*, *gam*, and *mā*, the substitute *cha*" [is applied], the letter *cha* is substituted. *Juhomi*: this is the form of the root *hu* (to give/to eat) in the present tense (*laṭ*). Because it begins a quarter-verse (*pāda*), it is not subject to the *nighāta* (elision of accent). *Havyam*: that which deserves to be invoked (*havana*). By the rule "also in the Veda" (*chandasi ca*), the suffix *ya* is applied. In the designation *bha*, by the rule "of *yas*," there is elision. It has the accent of the suffix. *Yāvat*: from the word *yat*, by the rule "from *yat*, *tat*, and *etad*, the suffix *vatup* is added in the sense of measure. By the rule "of pronouns, the substitute *ā*," the vowel *ā* is substituted. It is acutely accented on the first syllable (*ādyudātta*). *Īśe*: from the root *īś* (to rule). In the present tense, third person singular, the augment *iṭ* is applied. Because it belongs to the *adādi* class, there is the elision of *śap*. *Śataseyāya*: from the root *pā* (in the sense of ending). By the rule "of *āt* in the original instruction when followed by a non-*śit* suffix," there is the substitution of *ā*. By the rule "from vowels, the suffix *yat*," the suffix *yat* is added in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*). By the rule "in *īyati*," there is the substitution of *ī*. The *guṇa* strengthening occurs because it is an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix. It has the accent of the original form of the second member of a compound (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara*).
O Son of Strength, praised with bright flames, bestow great wealth upon those who labor;
O Agni, grant prosperity and well-being to the Viśvāmitras, as you repeatedly polish your own body for our sake.

O Son of Strength, being praised with your flame, bestow great vitality upon those who labor; O Agni, grant abundant wealth, peace, and well-being to the Viśvāmitras as they repeatedly polish your body. 4.
O Agni, son of strength, blaze up with your own radiance through your light!
Praised by the mantras that serve as the means for the *stotra* and *śastra*, you [shine] among those who are *śaśamāna*.
Yāska states: "The word *śaśamānaḥ* means *śaṃsamānaḥ* (one who praises)" (*Nirukta* 6.8).

Among those born of the Viśvāmitra lineage—those who praise the subject of you (the Lord)—there is one [who is called] Viśvāmitra, because "Viśva" (the universe) is his friend (*mitra*). 1. In manuscript *pha*, "tvām" is absent. 2. In manuscripts *kha*, *ga*, *ja*, *ṇa*, and *bha*, "vandamānaḥ" appears; in manuscript *pha*, "stuvan" is absent. 3. In manuscripts *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, and *sa*, the reading is "yāvadvandanam". 4. In manuscript *ta*, it is "asya". 5. In manuscript *la*, it is "havam". 6. In manuscript *ta*, it is "upadeśe". 7. In manuscripts *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, and *la*, "viśvāmitragotrotpanneṣu" is absent; in manuscripts *gha* and *pa*, it is "sarvamitreṣu". 8. In manuscript *ta*, "ekaḥ" is absent.

The plural number is used for the singular out of respect. Grant us such wealth as this: *revat*—meaning possessed of riches; *bṛhat*—meaning abundant; *vayaḥ*. The word *vayaḥ* signifies food, because it is listed among the names for food in the passage: “*arkaḥ vayaḥ kṣatra*” (*arkas*, *vayas*, *kṣatra*). Grant us such abundant food. Furthermore, grant us *śam*—the allaying of diseases—and *yoḥ*—the warding off of fears, that is, their non-mixture with us. Yāska says: “*Śamanaṃ ca rogāṇāṃ yāvanaṃ ca bhayānām*” (*Nirukta* 4.21). May we attain *vayaḥ* (food/sustenance) through the offerings made by us, who are *śaśamāneṣu* (those who exert themselves in praise). The root *śaś* (in *śaśa plutagatau*) here has the sense of praising. The suffix *cānaś* is added according to the rule “*tācchīlyavayovacanaśaktiṣu*. By the rule “*citaḥ*,” there is acute accent on the final syllable. *Dhehi* is the form of the imperative (*loṭ*) of the root *ḍudhāñ* (to sustain and nourish). *Revat*: the suffix *matup* is added in the sense of “one who possesses this” (*rayirasyāsti*). The *matup* is accented by the rule “*hasvanḍbhyāṃ matup*. By the rule “*chandasīraḥ*,” its *t* becomes *v*. There is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule “*rayematau bahulaṃ chandasi*,” followed by the substitution of the preceding vowel (*parapūrvatva*), and then *guṇa*. In *viśvāmitreṣu*, the lengthening of the first member is by the rule “*mitre caṇau*. The acute accent on the final syllable of the first member is by the rule “*bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām*. In *marmejjam*, from the root *mṛjjū* (to purify), the third person plural present indicative (*liṭ*) ending *mas* is replaced by *mā*. There is no *it* augment because “the prescription of augments is not mandatory. The *repha* is Vedic. Since it begins the quarter-verse (*pāda*), there is no *abhinidhāna*. It bears the accent of the suffix. *Bhūri*: from the root *bhū* (to exist). The suffix *kin* is added by the rule “*adiśavibhūśubhibhyaḥ kin*. Due to being *kit*, there is no *guṇa*. It bears the accent of the root. *Kṛttvaḥ*: from the root *ḍukṛñ* (to do). The suffix *kvip* is added in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) because it belongs to the *saṃpadādi* group. The suffix *matup* is added in the sense of “this belongs to him” (*tadasyāsti*). Its *t* becomes *v* by the rule “*jhayaḥ*. The designation *bha* applies by the rule “*tasau mathvarthe*,” which prevents the change of *t* to *j*. The *t* becomes *ru* by the rule “*matuvaso ruḥ*.”

O Agni, when you are well-kindled, you become a treasure-house of jewels for those who store them well; in the sacrificial pit, you bestow wealth upon the fortunate one, and you assume wondrous forms.

O Agni, you are indeed the one who possesses a wise mind, a jewel, and the easy acquisition of riches; for when you are kindled, you bestow wealth upon the praiseworthy one. Like a fortunate man, you place within the wooden vessel beautiful forms and excellent food.
O Agni, you who are a good giver (*susanih*)—one worthy of bestowing desired wealth—place within me that most excellent treasure among riches, such as gold-winged birds and the like;
grant it to me.
When you are prosperous (*samṛddhaḥ*), perfectly kindled and blazing with Soma and other offerings, then indeed, being just such a one, you become a giver of wealth.

Furthermore, for the fortunate patron (*sūnu*)—one endowed with excellent wealth—the two arms, which are well-reaching (*suprā*) and prone to gliding (*sarpaṇaśīlau*) into the *droṇa* (the sacrificial vessel) or house, are born for the sake of performing ritual acts; they are the "knowers of deeds" (*karan-nā*), that is, the directors of actions.
Regarding this, Yāska states: "The two arms are the 'karannau,' the directors of actions" (Nirukta 6.17).
They are also "forms" (*vapuṣi*).

Since the word *vapuḥ* is listed among the names for form in the passage "vapaḥ vapuḥ" (Nirukta 3.7.4), such arms— you also hold them, O Lord, so that they are *revat*, endowed with wealth, as well as radiant lights.
Susaniḥ: [derived from] the root *paṇu* in the sense of "giving."

1. From the reading of *ta*. 2. In *kha*, *ga*, *gha*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *na*, *pha*, *bha*, and *la*, “*vidhehi*” is absent. 3. In *na* and *la*, “*śamanam*” [is present]. 4. In *ta*, “*asmāsu*” [is present]. 5. In *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *pa*, *pha*, *bha*, “*yāvanam*” is absent. 6. In *ta* and *la*, “*dhehi vidhehi*” [is present]. 7. In *ta* and *la*, “*prabhṛtibhir āhutibhiḥ*” [is present]. 8. In *ta*, due to being a *cit* (marked with an accent), it is not udātta; in *la*, due to being a *cit*, there is the state of not being udātta. 9. In *la*, “*mṛjjū*” [is present]. 10. In *kha*, *ga*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *bha*, and *la*, “*leṭi*” [is present]. 11. In *ta*, “*kanakāścanām*” [is present]. 12. In *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *na*, *pha*, and *bha*, “*dhanam*” is absent. 13. In *ta*, “*etādṛśaḥ*” [is present]. 14. In *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *pha*, and *bha*, “*bhavasi*” is absent. 15. In *na* and *la*, “*prasarpaṇaśīlau*” [is present]. 16. In *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, and *bha*, “*karannau......yāskaḥ*” is absent.

This is the form [of the verb] in the *tṛc* (third person plural). There is the *āmantrita-nighāta* (the suppression of the accent of the vocative). *Saprā*: from the root *sap* in the sense of "going," the suffix *rak* is added by the rule “*sphāyitañcivañci-etc.*”; because of its *kittva*, there is no *guṇa* substitution; the accent is that of the suffix (*pratyaya-svara*). *Karatrā*: that which produces fruit is *kara*; it is a noun ending in the *pacādyac* suffix. Those two by which there is the purification (*śodhana*) of the action (*karman*), or rather, those two by which there is the purification of actions—this is a *bahuvrīhi* compound, and thus the accent is that of the first member (*pūrvapada-svara*). *Dadhipe*: from the root *ḍudhāñ* in the sense of "holding" and "nourishing," in the present tense (*laṭ*), the suffix *thās* becomes *id* because of the rule “*chandasyubhayathā*” (in the Veda, both types of suffixes are used), as it is treated as an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix; there is the elision of the long *ā*; there is the *nighāta* (suppression of the accent). || 18 ||
The seventh hymn, consisting of five verses beginning with “Agniṃ hotāram,” is in the Triṣṭubh meter, dedicated to Agni, and has Gāthin as its seer.
Thus it is enumerated: “‘Agniṃ hotāram,’ [the seer is] Gāthin.
Its application is prescribed for the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina Śastra.
I choose Agni as the Hotṛ at the sacrifice—the skillful sage, the all-knowing, the wise one.
May he, the most excellent sacrificer, worship us among the gods; for our strength and vigor, may he win us great riches.

I choose Agni as the Hotṛ priest for this sacrificial meal—the skillful sage, the all-knowing, the unerring. May he, the most excellent sacrificer, worship for us in the assembly of the gods; may he win for us gifts for the sake of wealth and strength. 1.

Gāthin praises: O Agni, you who are *gṛtsa*—praiseworthy; a *kavi*, wise; *viśvavid*, endowed with knowledge of all objects; *amūra*, undeluded; and possessed of qualities such as *añjana* (anointing)—I choose you, such as you are, as the *hotṛ*, the performer of the oblation or the invoker of the gods, for this *miyedha*, this sacrifice being performed by us. May that Agni, being the most excellent sacrificer (*yajīyān*), worship (*yakṣat*) for us the gods who are connected to us through the state of being worthy of sacrifice (*devatātā*).
Furthermore, may that Agni accept—enjoy—the *maghāni*, the great oblations being offered by us, for the sake of *rāyaḥ* (wealth), *vājāya* (strength), and *annāya* (food).
I choose (*vṛṇe*).
[The root] *vṛṅ* means "to gather" (*saṃbhaktau*). There is a *nighāta* (elision of accent).
miyedhe | The insertion of two [letters] between the *makāra* and the *ekāra* is Vedic (*chāndasa*). Gṛtsam.
The root *gṛdh* is used in the sense of longing (*abhikāṅkṣā*).
By the rule *gṛdhipayordekau ca* (Uṇādi-sūtra 2.349), the suffix *sapratyaya* is applied, and the final letter is changed to *d*. Thus, [the form *gardabha* is derived].
The initial udātta accent occurs by way of transposition (vyatyaya).
*Amūram*:
this is the form of the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*) of the root *muh* in the sense of "bewilderment" (*vaicitye*).
The letter *repha* is Vedic;
in a compound with the negative particle *nañ*, the accent is on the *nam*;
[the verb] *yakṣat*.
In the case of *yaj* with the suffix *liṭ*, the suffix *mip* is applied by the rule "in the case of *leṭ*, [the suffixes] *sic* and *ahula*.
By the rule "for *leṭ*, there is the augment *aṭ* and *āṭ*," the augment *aṭ* is added. Then, by the rule "and after *it*, there is elision," the *ik* vowel (*i*) is elided.
*Devatātā*:
from the word *deva*, the suffix *tāti* is added in the sense of the base itself according to the rule *sarvadevatātāt-il*;
the case ending *sup* is replaced by *ḍā* according to the rule *supāṃ suluk*.

The Lord. He desires. This is the present tense (*laṭ*) of the root *vana* (or *ṣaṇa*), meaning "to desire" or "to seek," with the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) used by way of grammatical substitution (*vyatyaya*).
The elision of the accent.
O Agni, draw toward us this verse accompanied by oblations—radiant, bestowing gifts, and dripping with ghee.
Accepting this circumambulation from the right, may he unite with riches and bounties.

O Agni, I send forth toward you this oblation-laden ladle, bright-shining, bestowing gifts, and dripping with ghee. Moving clockwise and choosing the divine host, he has united with the bounties and the Vasus; he has established them. 2.

1. [The suffix] *kara* follows *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, and *bha*. 2. [The suffix] *ac* is applied after *ja* and *ṇa* according to the *pacādi* group. 3. *Gardaḥ* means "that which is desired" (*kāmyamānam*), derived from *gṛ* with the suffix *sa*. 4. *Amūram* is formed from *mṛ* with the suffix *atac* (i.e., *at*). 5. In a *tatpuruṣa* compound ending in *ta*, *la*, or *sa*, the accent falls on that [first member]. O Agni, I send forth toward you—that is, in your presence—the ladle (*juhū* or *upabhṛt*) which is well-summoned (*asuṣumṇām*), possessed of bright splendor (*sutejasam*), endowed with oblations such as the sacrificial cake (*haviṣmatīm*), the giver of offerings (*rātanīm*), dripping with clarified butter (*ghṛtācīm*). Making the host of gods (*devatātīm*) wide—that is, making them many—I impel it.

"Urāṇa means making wide," says Yāska (Nirukta 6.17). May you, being such, with the *rātābhiḥ*—the riches obtained as gifts from the *vasu*s—'pradakṣiṇit', that is, by way of circumambulation, 'sam aśret': may you fully attend to this sacrifice.
*Haviṣmatīm*: [The suffix] *matup* is applied because she possesses *havis*. By the rule "tasau matvarthe," when there is the designation *bha*, the *s* [of *matup*] becomes *r*.
The suffix *ṅīp* is applied by the rule "ugitaśca.
Because the technical rule (*paribhāṣā*) stating that "in the prescription of accent, a consonant is treated as if it were present" is not invoked here, the suffix *matup* lacks an acute accent.
[Thus,] *iyarmi*.
The root *ṛ* means "to go.
It belongs to the *juhotyādi* class.
By the rule "artipiparyośca," the reduplication (*abhyāsa*) takes the form *in*.
By the rule "abhyāsasyāsavarṇe," there is the substitution of *i* for the reduplication;
because *mip* is marked with *p*, there is *guṇa*;
[and finally] there is the *nighāta* accent.
Accha;
by the rule "nipātasya," there is a long vowel in the *saṃhitā*.
[The word is] *rātinīm*.

From the root *rā* in the sense of "giving," the suffix *kta* is applied in the neuter gender to form the abstract noun *rātam*. Since [the deity] possesses that which is given (*rātam*), the suffix *ini* is added according to the rule *ata iniṭhanau*.
The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
*Ghṛtācīm*:
from the root *dhā* preceded by *ghṛta*, the suffix *kvip* is applied according to the rule *ṛtvig-dadhṛg-...*.
The feminine suffix *ṅīp* is added according to the supplementary rule *añjeśchoṣasaṃkhyānam*.

In the term *bhasaṃjñā*, there is the elision of the vowel *a* by the rule *acaḥ*; then, by the rule *cau*, there is lengthening. Although the acute accent (*udātta*) would have applied to the suffix *ṅīp* by the rule *udāttanivṛttisvaraḥ*, the rule *cau* instead prescribes an acute accent on the final syllable of the preceding member (*pūrvapada*).
Regarding *pradakṣiṇit*:
the suffix *ṇic* is applied according to the rule *tat karoti* ("he does that") to derive *pradakṣiṇaṃ karoti* ("he performs circumambulation").

However, since the suffix *ṇic* arises only after the verb *saṃgrāmayati* when it is accompanied by a prefix (*sopasarga*), and not from any other [verb], the suffix *kvip* is applied to that [form ending in] *ṇic*.
The augment *tuk* is applied by Pāṇini’s rule 6.1.71 (*hrasvasya piti*).
The absence of the elision of the causative suffix (*ṇic*) is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*).
[Thus] there is the accent of the causative suffix (*ṇic-svara*).
Regarding *devatāti*: from the word *deva*, the suffix *tāti* is applied according to the rule "after every [word ending in] *deva*, [the suffix] *tāti* [is added].
By the rule "when *li* follows," the vowel preceding the suffix receives the acute accent (*udātta*).

*Urāṇa*: [The word *urāṇa* is derived as follows: because it makes wide (*uru karoti*), the suffix *ṇic* is applied according to the rule "he does that" (*tatkaroti*). From that which ends in *ṇic*, the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*) occurs in Vedic usage.
Because it is a *mantra*, [the suffix] *ām* does not occur. For that [suffix], there is *kānac*. There is elision of the *ṇi* by the rule "ṇer aniṭi."
The absence of the *varādeśa* (the substitution of *vṛ* for *vṛdh*) is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*). It is *udātta*-accented on the final syllable because it ends in *ci*. [The form] is *aśret*.

In the case of the root *śriñ* in the sense of "service," when the *laṅ* suffix is applied according to Vedic usage, there is the elision of *śap* by the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pāṇini 2.4.73); [the resulting form is subject to] the *nighāta* (anudātta) accent.

With a most powerful mind, O Agni, you have indeed helped us; grant us aid, O helper, for the sake of good offspring. O Agni, may we be recipients of your abundant wealth, most manly, and of your riches that are easy to win.

With a most powerful mind, I have encompassed you; therefore, O Agni, bestow upon us the gift of noble offspring, O Dispenser. May we be the ones to offer fair praises to you for the abundance of most heroic wealth. || 3 ||

O Agni, being protected by you, he becomes endowed with a mind—that is, an internal organ (antaḥkaraṇa)—that is more brilliant, exceedingly sharp, and possessed of an intellect keen toward the sphere of virtuous deeds. Moreover, "to him" (tasmai) refers to his offspring;
here the genitive case is used in the sense of the accusative.
"Bestow wealth accompanied by excellent offspring;
for you are skilled in the act of giving, as such acts of giving are taught in the case of bestowing cows and other gifts.
O Agni, may we abide in the abundant power and majesty of you, who are desirous of giving—being incapable of withholding—and who are the supreme leader and giver of the wealth of the truthful one."
Furthermore: "O Suta, may we—who possess beautiful hymns of praise concerning you—become, that is, be, 'vasvaḥ,' recipients of wealth."
*Tejīyasā*:
the suffix *īyasun* is applied to the word *tejas* in the sense of excellence (*atiśayana*), according to the rule "the *t* is elided before *iṣṭhan*, *iman*, and *īyasun*."

1. In the *pa* manuscript, "or the *upabhṛt*" does not exist. 2. In the *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *pha*, *bha*, and *sa* manuscripts, "by the Vasus" does not exist. 3. In the *ja* and *ṇa* manuscripts, it reads "by the Vasus who have attained. 4. In the *na* manuscript, it reads "dwelling with wealth"; in the *la* and *sa* manuscripts, it reads "being with wealth. 5. In the *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, and *pha* manuscripts, "who" does not exist; in the *bha* and *sa* manuscripts, it reads "he. 6. In the *ta* manuscript, it reads "employed by the intellect. 7. In the *ta* manuscript, it reads: "that which is learned (*śikṣate*) and given (*dīyate*) is *śikṣu*: wealth. 8. In the *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, and *ṇa* manuscripts, it reads "because of being desired, [it is] the bestowing of fruit. 9. In the *ta* manuscript, it reads "in greatness, in sovereignty. 10. In the *gha* and *pa* manuscripts, it reads "may we be"; in the *ca* manuscript, it reads "the filler."

The elision of the *tṛc* suffix [is applied]. It has no accent (*nisvara*). In *tvotaḥ*: the root *ava* is used in the sense of protection and so forth; with the *niṣṭhā* suffix, by the rule *jvaratvara-srivyavimavām upadhāyāḥ*, there is the substitution of *ū* for the penultimate vowel, and the elision of the preceding [vowel]. Thus, *svayā utaḥ*. The compound is formed by splitting the rule *tṛtīyā* [into two separate rules]. The elision of the final *ṭi* is Vedic (*chāndasa*). By the rule *tṛtīyā karmaṇi*, the original accent of the first member (*pūrvapada-prakṛtisvara*) is retained. In *śikṣa*: the root *śikṣ* (meaning "to take up" or "to instruct") is here used in the sense of giving. From this, in the imperative (*loṭ*), the Parasmaipada ending is used by transposition (*vyatyaya*). In *śikṣoḥ*: from the root *śakl* (meaning "to be able"), in the desiderative (*san*), there is a prohibition of the augment *it* by the rule *ekāca upadeśe*. By the rule *sani mīmādhurabhalabhaśakapatapadā haca is*, the root undergoes the substitution of *is* for the *tav* (the *k* of *śak*). There is elision of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) by the rule *atra lopo'bhyāsasya*. The suffix *u* is added by the rule *sanāśaṃsabhikṣa uḥ*. The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*). In *prabhūtau*: from the root *bhū* (meaning "existence"), the suffix *ktin* is added in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāve*). By the rule *tādau ca niti kṛtyatau*, the original accent of the prefix (*gati*) is retained. In *bhūyāma*: from the root *bhū* (meaning "existence"), in the optative of benediction (*āśīr-liṅ*), the suffix *yāsuṭ* is added by the rule *kidāśipi*. Because of the rule *chandasyubhayathā*, this is treated as a *sārvadhātuka* suffix, and thus the *vṛddhi* is elided. The accent is that of the augment (*āgamasvara*). Alternatively, in the optative of request (*prārthanā*) from that same root, *yāsuṭ* is added. By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, the *śap* suffix is elided. Since the root does not end in a long vowel (*anadanta*), the substitution of *iy* does not occur. In *suṣṭutayaḥ*: by the rule *nambubhyām*, the final syllable of the second member (*uttarapada*) is accented. In *vasvaḥ*: because the teaching regarding augments is not always mandatory (*anitya*), the augment *tum* is absent. Because a grammatical operation conditioned by a specific technical name (*saṃjñāpūrvaka*) is not always mandatory, there is an absence of *guṇa*. The *yaṇ* substitution takes place.

For the people who offer sacrifice have established your many swift flames as the foremost of the god’s aspects. O youngest one, bring hither the host of deities when you, as the sacrificer, perform the divine rite.

For the people who desire to worship thee, O Agni, have established thy many flickering faces as a god. Therefore, O youngest one, bring hither the most divine host, that thou mayst today sacrifice to the celestial assembly.

O Agni, the people— the Adhvaryus and others who perform the sacrifice— have indeed placed within you, the radiant deity, many flickering flames; these forms of light, like armies spread everywhere, have been established in you by means of the pouring of oblations.
[The meaning is] "they performed [the sacrifice].

O such as you, bring hither—that is, invoke—the deities (*devatātaṃ*), the gods to be worshipped, for this ritual act. O youngest (*yaviṣṭha*), most youthful one, because today in this rite you offer (*yarjāsi*) the divine (*divyam*)—that is, celestial, pertaining to the gods—*śardhaḥ*, which means splendor (*tejaḥ*), therefore [you are] the leader of the gods; this is the ellipsis.
*dadhire* is a form of the root *dhā* in the perfect tense (*liṭ*). Due to its connection with *hi*, it does not undergo the loss of accent (*anighāta*).
*cikhāda* is udātta at the end. *yajryavaḥ*.
The root *yaja* is used in the sense of worshiping the gods and so forth.
The suffix *yuc* is applied by the rule *yajamāna-śundhi-dasī-janibhyo yuc*.
The initial acute accent (*ādyudāttatva*) occurs by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*). [Thus we have] *devatātama*.
From the word *deva*, the suffix *tāti* is applied in the sense of the base itself by the rule "after *sarva* and *devatā*, [the suffix] *til*";
by the rule "when *l* follows," the vowel preceding the suffix is acute.
Thus: *yarjāsi*.
The suffix *leṭ* occurs after the root *yaj*;
due to its presence, there is no loss of accent (*anighāta*).
And you whom the gods, seating you here for the sacrifice, have generated as the Hotṛ priest—O Agni, as such, be our protector here; bestow glorious renown upon our bodies.

Since the gods have seated you, O Agni, as the Hotṛ priest who does not fail, for the performance of the sacrifice, therefore, O Agni, be our protector here; bestow glorious renown upon our bodies. 5.

1. *Kha-ga-bha*: elision of the *upa* (prefix); *na*: *ūṭ*; elision; *la*: elision of the penultimate (*upadhā*); *sa*: elision of the final (*uda*). 2. *ma-dha-ta-pa-phaya-cchya-devam*. 3. *kha-pa*: "born in heaven" (*divi bhava*) is not present. Ṛgveda 2.34:

O Agni, the gods—the shining officiating priests—sitting down for the sake of sacrifice (*yajathāya*), that is, for the purpose of performing the ritual, [have sat] at the *miyedha*, that is, the sacrificial feast (*medha*). Because they have anointed (*anajan*) you, the invoker (*hotṛ*) of the gods, with offerings of clarified butter (*ghṛta*).

Or rather: since the officiating priests, seating you—the Hotṛ, the performer of the oblation—upon the sacrificial grass (barhis) and sprinkling you with clarified butter (ghṛta), you have become such [a one]; therefore, in this rite, be mindful that "I shall be the protector and guardian of us.
Furthermore, bestow abundantly upon our bodies—that is, upon our offspring—the glories of food (śravāṃsi).
*anaja-n*:
the root *aṅk* is used in the senses of manifestation, movement, and destruction;
from this [root], the suffix *li* is applied because it belongs to the *rudhādi* class.
Due to its Vedic character, there is no elision [of the nasal].
By the rule *aniditām* [Pāṇini 6.4.24], there is elision of the penultimate vowel.
[Thus they are] *niṣādayantaḥ*.
The root *pal* is used in the senses of going, perishing, and sinking;
it belongs to the *curādi* (tenth) class.
According to the rule "after *sad* and *prati*," there is substitution of *pa* for *sa*.
Alternatively:
the suffix *ṇic* is applied because there is a cause [for the action].
Once the *anudātta* accent has been applied to the *śatṛ* by virtue of its being a *lasārvadhātuka*, the *ṇic* itself becomes *udātta*.
*bodhi*:
from the root *budh* in the sense of "understanding" (*avagamana*),
with the elision of the suffix *śap* by the rule *loṭi bahulaṃ chandasi*.
In *sveḥ pricca*, *si* is replaced by *hi*.
By the rule *vā chandasi*, because it is optionally treated as having the *pit* designation, there is no *guṇa* substitution.
By the rule *husṛbhyo hedhiḥ*, *hi* is replaced by *dhi*.
The elision of the letter *dhakāra* is due to Vedic license (*chāndasa*). There is a *nighāta* accent. [The form is] *dhehi*.
This is the form of the root *dadhāti* in the imperative mood (*loṭ*).
The eighth hymn, consisting of five verses beginning with "agnim upasām," is in the Triṣṭubh meter.
Regarding this, the Anukramaṇī states: "agnim upasām: [the first two verses are] addressed to Agni, while [the last three] are addressed to the Viśvedevas.
Because of the use of the particle *ha* in the phrase "gāthī ha," Gāthin is also the seer (*ṛṣi*) of this hymn.
The first and fifth [verses] have the Viśvedevas as their deity; the remaining three are addressed to Agni.
The application (viniyoga) of this hymn has been stated.
In the Marutvatīya Śastra, the verse "agninetaḥ" serves as the dhāyyā.
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "O Agni, lead them; O Soma, let them drink with the seasons; [and] 'ayāṣa' are the dhāyās" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 5.14).

At the dawning of light, the priest invokes with hymns Agni, the Aśvins, and Dadhikrā. May the gods, possessing excellent luster, hear us—may they, being well-pleased and longing for the sacrifice, listen to our call. agnim upasam aśvinā dadhikrām vyuṣṭiṣu havate vahnir ukthaiḥ | sujyotiṣo naḥ śṛṇvantu devāḥ sajoṣaso adhvaraṃ vāvaśānāḥ || 1 ||
Gāthin says:

Agni is the carrier of the oblations; at the dawns, that is, at the breakings of the night, [one approaches] Agni, the deity worthy of sacrifice, Upas (the presiding deity of the dawns), the two Aśvins, and Dadhikrā—the god named Dadhikrāvan. One approaches that Dadhikrāvan.
He invokes these gods with *ukthas*—recitations consisting of non-chanted mantras—and with *sūktas*, hymns that are the means of praise.

May all the gods, who are well-luminous (*sujyotiṣaḥ*) and shining brightly, desiring (*vāvaśanāḥ*) this sacrifice of ours, and being in harmony (*sajopasaḥ*) with one another, hear that invocation. [And may they hear] Dadhikrā.
[*Ṛ* is used in the sense of "striding" (*pādavikṣepe*).]
With *dadhi* as the upapada, the suffix *viṭ* is applied by the rule *janasanakhanakramagamah*.
The substitution of *ā* occurs by the rule *vidvanoranunāsikasyāt*,
and the accent is that of the original form of the final member of the compound (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara*).
In the case of *vyuṣṭiṣu*: the root *uc* means "to dawn";
the suffix *kin* is applied in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāve*).
The substitution of *ṣ* for *s* occurs by virtue of the rule beginning with *vaś-*.
Furthermore, because of the rule *tādau ca niti kṛtyatau*, the root vowel retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) when followed by a suffix beginning with *t* that has an indicatory *n*.
[Thus] *havate*.
In the word *hūyateḥ*, there is a *saṃprasāraṇa* (vocalization) according to the rule "it occurs abundantly in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*). Regarding *sujyotiṣaḥ*:

in the analysis (*vigraha*) "shining excellently" (*suṣṭhu dyotamānā*), from the root *dyut* in the sense of "to shine," the suffix *isin* is applied by the rule "*dyuterisinādeśaśca jaḥ*" (Uṇādi Sūtra 2.267), whereby the suffix *isin* is added and the letter *d* is replaced by *j*.
[In the case of a *kṛt* compound,] there is the accentuation of the original form (*prakṛtisvara*) of the final member.
However, in the case of a *bahuvrīhi* compound, by the rule "after *nañ* and *su*, [the final syllable of the second member is acute]," the final syllable of the second member would be udātta;
as in: *sujyotiṣe aktavastau abhi vyūḥ*.

1. la—after *sad* and *prati*; 2. ca—na—la—ending with *māthā*; 3. kha—ga—ja—na—bha—having Vaiśvadeva as the deity; ca—la—having Vaiśvadevatā as the deity; 4. ta—*vahniḥ*: the bearer of praises; la—*vahniḥ*: the bearer of praises, the Hotṛ priest; 5. ta—in those that have dawned; 6. ta—there is no mention of the gods; 7. ta—being cherished together, mutually united; 8. kha—ga—ca—na—bha—sa—in the act of sending away; 9. kha—ta—pha—the natural accent (*prakṛtisvara*).

In this passage (*Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* 10.89.15), the final syllable bears the acute accent (*udātta*). Therefore, this is not a compound here, but rather a *tatpuruṣa* [case-determinative] compound. As for *bhru*: from the root *bhṛ* in the sense of "hearing" (*śravaṇe*), by the rule *śruvaḥ śra ca*, the form *bhruḥ* is derived; simultaneously with that, the substitution of *śra* for the root occurs. It receives the *nighāta* (unaccented) accent. Regarding *vāvaśānāḥ*: this is the form of the root *vaś* in the sense of "desire" (*kāntau*) in the *yaṅluk* (intensive without *yaṅ*) conjugation. The lengthening of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) occurs by the rule *dīrgho 'kitaḥ*. The suffix *śānac* is used by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*), and it carries the *cis* accent.

O Agni, three are your strengths, three your abodes, and three are your many tongues, O you who are born of Truth. Three are your bodies beloved by the gods; with these, protect our songs of praise without negligence. 2. O Agni! Three are your powers; three are your stations; three are your many tongues, O you who are born of Cosmic Order (Ṛta)! Indeed, three are your bodies favored by the gods; with those, protect our hymns, never being heedless. 2.

O Agni, those three strengths (*vājina*) of yours—consisting of clarified butter, herbs, and Soma—are your three foods; there are three abodes (*sadhasthā*), namely the three hearths beginning with the *āgnīdhra*.
Alternatively, they are the three stations known as the *ekāha*, *ahīna*, and *sattra* sacrifices.
Or else, they are the three worlds.
O Agni, born of *ṛta*— you who have arisen from the *ṛta*-born, true, and established sacrifices— your ancient three tongues, beginning with the *gārhapatya*, which fill the bellies of the gods;
O Agni, your three bodies, desired by the gods (*devavātāḥ*), consisting of the three forms known as Pavamāna, Pāvaka, and Śuci.

Being thus disposed, remaining unwearied, vigilant, and attentive, protect—that is, preserve—with those [three] our *tanūs*, our bodies; protect our *girah*, our hymns, that is, the words of our praises, *stotras*, *śastras*, and so forth.
[The word] *tisraḥ* [is used];
the acute accent on the final syllable of *jasaḥ* is according to the rule "tisṛbhyo jasaḥ."

Jihvā: [derived from] the root *lih* in the sense of "tasting. Because they lick (*lihanti*) flavors, the suffix *van* is applied by the rule of irregular formation (*nipātana*): “*śevā-ya-hva-jihvā-grīvā-pvā-mīvāḥ*.”
The letter *la* becomes *ja*;
there is an absence of *guṇa*;
and by transposition, the word-final syllable is udātta.
*devavātāḥ*: [derived from] the root *vā*, meaning "to go" or "to blow"; from this, the suffix *kta* is applied in the sense of the object (*karman*).
In the phrase *tṛtīyā karmaṇi*, the initial accent of the preceding word (*pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*) applies. *Pāhi* is the form of the root *pā* (meaning "to protect") in the imperative (*loṭ*).
Nighāta: *aprayucchan* (not being heedless). [The root] *yuccha* [is used] in the sense of "heedlessness."
Impermanent.

O Agni, Jātavedas, many are your names, O divine one, self-dependent, immortal. And those many wondrous powers of the masters of illusion, O all-pervading one, they have placed within you, O you whose back is firmly bound. O Agni! Many! Your! O Jātavedas! O God! O self-dependent one! Of the immortal! The name! And which! Wondrous powers! Of the masters of illusion! O all-pervading one! Within you! Many! They have placed! O you whose back is firmly bound! 3.

1. *Ta-pūrvī*: "The tongue of the gods," which is of three kinds according to the divisions of *sāttvika* and so forth. Alternatively, because of the Vedic revelation: "There are three fires: *Havyavāhana* for the gods, *Kavyavāhana* for the ancestors, and *Saharakṣas* for the *asuras*"; thus, due to the threefold nature of the fire, there is a threefold nature of the tongues.
Or else:

2. *Kha-ga-ca-pha-bha-jihvā*: the tongue is of three kinds according to the division of *svāhikā* and so forth; *gha-pa-jihvā*: the tongue is of three kinds according to the division of *sattva* and so forth (*gha-sattvikādi*); *ja-ṇa-na-jihvā*: the tongue is of three kinds according to the division of *sāttvika* and so forth.
3. *Gha-pa-pālaya*. *U* is the filler.

O shining one, O Jātavedas—whose nature is born wisdom—O Agni, while you are consuming [the oblation], the gods have placed many names and splendors within you, belonging to you who are immortal and free from the law of death. Moreover, O Agni, friend of the back—that is, the supporter of those who offer praise for the sake of desired fruits—you have taken upon yourself the many, manifold deceits of the deceitful Asuras, just as one holds the universe; these are present within you.
Therefore, having warded off the illusions of the deceivers who cause obstacles to the sacrifice, may you protect our sacrifice— O Bhava,
O Pūṣan,
O Svadhāvan!
The suffix *mat* is applied in the sense of "possessing" (*asti*), as in *svadhā asti*.
By the rule *matuvaso ruḥ*, the *n* of *amṛta* becomes *r*. Thus: *amṛtasya*.

In the word *nañ*, there is the acute accent on the first syllable of the following member (*uttarapadādyudāttatva*) according to the rule *naño jaramaramitramṛtāḥ*. [The word] *nāma* is used in the sense of salutation (*prahratve*), according to the rule *ṇām prahratve*.

By the rule “*nāmnasīmanavyayoman*” and so forth, there is the elision of the letter *m* and the lengthening of the vowel due to the irregular formation (*nipātana*) ending in the suffix *manin*. These are called *nāmāni* (names) because they cause all persons who have become their own substrates to bow down; thus they are *tejas* (splendors). The case-ending *sup* is elided according to the rule “*supāṃ suluk*... and so forth.
It is udātta on the first syllable due to the suffix *ni*. Regarding "māyinām": the suffix *ini* is applied according to the rule for the *vrīhy-ādi* group, meaning "those who possess *māyā*."
In the phrase “yasya 0,” there is elision; the accent is that of the suffix;
it is like “viśvam.”
From the root *miv* (meaning "to pervade" and "to please"), with the word *viśva* as an upapada, the suffix *aṇ* is applied according to the rule *karmaṇyaṇ*.

Although the suffix *num* would have been required by the rule *idito num dhātoḥ* during the stage of the verbal base (*dhātūpadeśāvasthā*), it does not occur because the *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel takes effect.
Thus, one who pervades or pleases the universe is called *viśvamiṣaḥ*.
In the compound *tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam*, there is no elision (*aluk*) of the second case ending. Because it is in the vocative case, there is no elision of the final vowel. They joined together.
The form [duvān] is the perfect (liṭ) third person singular (usi) of the root √dhṛ, meaning "to hold" or "to nourish.
Due to its connection with a preceding word, it does not undergo the loss of accent (anighāta);
rather, it bears the accent of the suffix (pratyayasvara).

*pṛṣṭhabandhaḥ*: From the root *pracch* in the sense of “desire to know,” the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*) is formed in the objective sense; by the rule *prahijyā-vadhi-*, etc., there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*), and by the rule beginning with *vaśrādi*, there is the substitution of *yat*.
From the root *bandh* in the sense of "binding," the suffix *u* is applied according to the rule *stṛ-snihi-ādi*;
this forms a genitive compound (*ṣaṣṭhī-samāsa*),
and it receives the *nighāta* (anudātta) accent because it is in the vocative case (*āmantrita*).
May Agni, the leader of the divine races, the god who upholds the light, the guardian of the sacred order and the observer of truth,
he who is the slayer of Vṛtra, the wise one, and the knower of all— may he carry the singer across all difficulties. 4.

Agni is the leader, like Bhaga for the human tribes; he is the god of the divine ones, the guardian of the cosmic order (*ṛta*), and the upholder of truth. He is the slayer of Vṛtra, the skillful guide, and the possessor of all knowledge. May he carry the singer across all difficulties. 4.
He who is this Agni, the leader of the *viś*—that is, of men and of the divine *viś* related to the gods—and the controller of them through his role as the inner restrainer (*antaryāmin*);
in this regard, there is an illustration:
he is like Bhaga, the drinker of the seasons (*ṛtupā*).
Just as the sun is the protector of the seasons, such as spring, and the impeller of all by bestowing its own light,

so too is that Agni— the one who is *vṛtravān* (possessing power), whose deeds are true (*satyakarmā*), the slayer of Vṛtra (*vṛtrahā*), the ancient (*sanayaḥ*), eternal (*sanātanaḥ*), primordial (*purāṇaḥ*), the knower of all things (*viśvavedāḥ*), the omniscient (*sarvajñaḥ*), and the radiant god (*devaḥ*)— may he, being of such a nature, carry across (*parṣat*) and lead to the further shore the singer who praises him, performing hymns directed toward him, passing beyond all difficulties (*viśvā duritā*). He is the leader.
This is the form of the root *ṇīñ* (meaning "to lead" or "to attain") with the suffix *tṛc*;
it has the accent on the *cit* syllable.
[The word is] *kṣitīnām*.
The root *kṣi* means "dwelling" and "going. By the rule *kiccakau ca saṃjñāyām*, the suffix *kic* is applied.
By the rule *nāmanyatarasyām*, there is optionally an udātta accent on the final syllable.
Regarding *daivīnām*: from the word *deva*, the suffix *añ* is applied in the sense of relationship by the rule *devādyañau*;
then, by the rule *ṭiḍhāṇañ*, the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is applied after *añ*.
*jīrṇavāda* is udātta at its beginning. *ṛtupāḥ*:
from the root *pā* in the sense of "to protect," the suffix *vic* is applied according to the rule *anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante*.

The compound *ṛtupā* is formed according to Pāṇini 2.2.19 (*upapadam atiṅ*), meaning "he drinks the seasons. It takes the original accent of the final member due to the rule regarding *kṛd*-derived compounds (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara*). [Similarly: *vṛtrahā*.

1. Thus, O Lord! 2. And one whose wisdom is born. 3. Kha, ga, ca, ta, bha, sa, ṇam. 4. Of that wicked Vṛtra. 5. Kha, ga, ca, na, pha, bha, sa, san; in the *ta* recension, ‘sanayaḥ’ is not present. 6. Gha recension: parinayatu; *ta* recension: nayet pāram. 7. Kha, ga, ca, ja, na, bha, la, sa, because of victory.

The root *han* is used in the senses of "killing" and "going. By the rule "brahmaṇvad-atreṣu kip," the suffix *kip* is applied [to form *viśvavedas*]. In the compound *viśvavedāḥ*, the final syllable of the first member is udātta by the rule "in a bahuvrīhi, when it is a name, *viśva* [is so]. [The word] *paryat*: from the root *pṛ* in the sense of "protecting" and "filling," in the *leṭ* tense, the suffix *sip* is added by the rule "the suffix *sip* is variously applied"; there is the augment *ad*; the vowel *i* is elided by the rule "there is elision of the *i* after [the *sip*]"; because it begins with a *pāda*, it does not receive the *anighāta* (non-suppression) accent; it ends in a *guṇa* vowel. [The word] *guṇantam*: from the root *gṛ* in the sense of "sound," the suffix *śatṛ* is applied for the present tense (*laṭ*); because it begins with a vowel, *śrā* is substituted; since it ends in *śatṛ*, the long *ā* is elided by the rule "of the *ā* of the *śatṛ* and the reduplicated [roots]. It takes the accent of the *śatṛ* suffix.
I invoke here Dadhikrāvan and the seer, the goddess Bṛhaspati and the god Savitṛ, the Aśvins, Mitra and Varuṇa, Bhaga, the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas.
