Regarding this, the table of contents (anukramaṇikā) states: "In 'asti idam,' the first, fourth, and tenth verses are *anuṣṭubh*s; the fifth, eleventh, penultimate, and [sixteenth] are *jagatī*s; and the fifth, eleventh, fourteenth, and fifteenth may also be *triṣṭubh*s.

Thus, the first, fourth, and tenth verses are *anuṣṭubh*s; the fifth, eleventh, and penultimate (fifteenth) are *jagatī*s; and the fifth, eleventh, fourteenth, and fifteenth may optionally be *triṣṭubh*s.
The remaining eight verses are *triṣṭubh*s. The fifth verse, “*amanthata naraḥ*,” has either the *ṛtvij*s or the objects of desire as its deity;
the remaining verses have Agni as their deity.
The application of the hymn (*sūktaviniyoga*) is based on its internal indicative mark (*laiṅgika*).
Among the Varuṇapraghāsa rites, during the carrying forward of the fire (*agnipraṇayana*), this verse, "In the place of Iḷā" (*iḷāyāstvā pade*), is used.

And it is stated in the Sūtra: "O Agni, we [invoke] thee in the place of Iḷā; with all the gods, O thou of beautiful face, begin the praise for the gods" (*iḷāyāstvā pade vayamagne viśvebhiḥ svanika devebhyarca āramet*; Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 2.17).
In that very context, when the fire has been brought forward and the *uttaravedi* altar has been established, the verse “Sit down, O Hotṛ” is used; this is prescribed by the Sūtra:

“When the fire has been placed, [he recites] ‘Sit down, O Hotṛ, being wise, in your own place’” (*Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra* 2.17). The ritual of depositing the fire into the two kindling woods (*araṇi*) is performed with the verse “This is your womb.”
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "This is your seasonal womb; O Gārhapatya fire, you are the two kindling woods, or the hands that shall enkindle you" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 3.10).
There is this friction; procreation has been performed.
Bring hither this Viśvapatnī; let us churn the fire as of old.
It exists; here is the wood for churning. It exists; the act of procreation has been performed. Bring this woman, the mistress of all; let us churn Agni as of old. || 1 ||
The sacrificer speaks to the Adhvaryu and the others:
"This is the splinter for this purpose;
it is for the upper friction."
The friction-sticks (*araṇī*) are placed above; the means for churning, such as the staff (*daṇḍa*) and so forth, is present.

The "procreative" (*prajanana*)—the *darbha*-grass brush (*piñjūla*) which serves as the instrument for generating fire—has been prepared and fashioned. Alternatively, "procreative" refers to a specific manner of holding the churning staff.

Since these pieces of wood for the sacrificial post (*yūpaśakala*) and so forth have been brought as the means for churning the fire, therefore, O Adhvaryu, bring—bring hither—this *araṇi* (lower fire-drill), which is the consort of the universe (*viśvapatnī*), the protector of the people (*viśaḥ*) through the bestowal of the attainment of fruits such as heaven by means of the Agnihotra sacrifice accomplished by the fire.

1. In the *ta* manuscript, the word "dhātoḥ" is absent. 2. *ta*: the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) offered after the oblation has been poured. 3. *ta*: the state of being its own sound (*svaratvam*). "Jupasva" is the imperative form of the root *juṣ*, meaning "to please" or "to serve. 4. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-pha-bha*: by means of the leading forward of the fire (*agnipraṇayanena*). 5. *ta*: and it is stated in the Sūtra. 6. *kha-ga-ca*: that which serves as the means for churning. 7. *kha-pha-bha*: flaming up (*abhijvalana*).
Upon this striking, just as we produced fire at the time of the original consecration (*ādhāna*), or just as the great seers of old produced fire, so do we now produce this fire in this ritual;
let us bring it forth by means of churning.
Because the two words *asti* occur at the beginning of a quarter-verse (*pāda*), they are not subject to the rule of unaccentedness (*anighāta*).
[The form] *viśarantīnām* [is derived from the root] *śṛ* with the prefix *vi*.
In the case of the two instances of the word *pati*, the feminine suffix *ṅīp* and the replacement by a stem ending in *n* are applied according to the rule *vibhāṣā sapūrvasya*.
The acute accent on the first syllable of the second member [of the compound] is due to the rule *pagadiśchandasi bahulam*.
Regarding *bhara*: from the root *hṛ* (in the sense of "carrying"), in the imperative (*loṭ*), the substitution of *bha* for *ha* occurs by the rule *hagrahorbhaṣchandasī*.
Let us churn. This is the form of the verb *mantha* (meaning "to churn" or "to stir") in the imperative mood (*loṭ*).
The elision [of the case-ending] is by *nighāta*.
In the word *pūrvathā*, the suffix *thāl* is added after the word *pūrva* in the sense of "like" (*iva*), according to the rule: *pra-napūrva-viśvā-māt-thāl chandasi*.
By the rule "liti," the vowel preceding the suffix *lit* is udātta (accented acute).
Jātavedas has been placed within the two fire-sticks; like a well-set embryo in pregnant women, Agni is to be praised day after day by watchful men who bring oblations.
Agni Jātavedas is deposited in the two fire-sticks; well-established like an embryo within pregnant women, he is to be praised day by day by watchful men who offer oblations. 2.
1. This Agni is Jātavedas, possessing knowledge of all objects; he is placed within the two fire-sticks. I have been firmly established by the gods for the sake of the sacrifice.
Here is an illustration:
it is like a fetus. Just as a fetus exists well-placed and securely deposited within pregnant women, so too is this.

Such a one is that Agni, who is to be served day by day—that is, every single day—by us humans, those who possess oblations and who perform the offering of oblations, being ever-watchful and vigilant in their ritual duties; he is to be praised with hymns consisting of words of praise.
In the word *ariyoḥ*:
from the root *ṛ* meaning "to go," the suffix *ani* is applied according to the rule beginning with “*atisṛṣṭadharmi*” etc. (Pāṇini 3.2.179).
The accent is that of the suffix.
[The form] *nihitaḥ* is derived from the root *dhā* with the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*) suffix; by the rule "for *dhā*, there is *hi*," there is the substitution of *hi*.
In the phrase "gatiranantaraḥ," the word *gati* retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*). *Sudhitaḥ*:
this is the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*) of the root *dhā* used in the sense of the object.
In that [word], by the rule of irregular formation (*nipātana*) beginning with "sudhita vasudhita," there is the substitution of *dhi* [for *dhā*].
*Divedive*. [The root] *div* is used in the sense of playing (*krīḍā*) and so forth.
The suffix *ka* is applied by virtue of the rule *igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ*. There is reduplication according to the rule *nityavīpsayoḥ*.
Since the *na* is not followed by a vowel (*adita*), it is unaccented (*anudātta*), and thus the accent of the preceding member remains.
*jāgṛvadbhiḥ*:
this is the form of the root *jāgṛ* (meaning "in the destruction of sleep") in the *kvasu* suffix.
Due to the rule "In the section on dual endings, it should be stated that [the dual] is optional in the Veda," the dual ending is optionally absent.
By the rule *vasusaṃmṛdhvanvanaḍuhāṃ daḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.72), the *m* of the suffix *vas* is changed to *d*;
this is the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
Place him here upon her who lies extended; the wise one, having been conceived, has immediately brought forth the bull.
With ruddy crest and radiant luster, the Son of Iḷā has been born for the sake of wisdom.

From her who lies extended, bring [the seed] down, O wise one; straightway, having been impregnated, she has brought forth the bull. Red-crested, his brilliance is shining; the son of Iḷā has been born for the sake of wisdom. 3.
O wise and knowing Adhvaryu, place the upper fire-stick (uttarāraṇi) upon the lower fire-stick (adharāraṇi) which lies flat; hold it downward.
Immediately thereafter, that lower fire-stick, being impregnated and having received the seed, shall give birth to Agni, the showerer of desires.
Then, let his brilliant splendor destroy the darkness. His power—his majesty.

1. The letters kha, ga, ca, ja, ṇa, pha, and bha undergo the substitution *asti* (the form *at*). 2. For the root *i*, when followed by the imperative suffix (*loṭ*), [the substitute *at* is applied]. 3. The letters l and s undergo the substitution *tatra*. 4. The suffix *an* is applied after the root *tan*. 5. The substitution *dhi* and so forth is applied [to the root *as*] in the imperative.

There was only light (*tejomātra*) there. Immediately thereafter, the formless *stūpa*—endowed with a mass of shining light—was born from the *uttaravedi* of *Iḷā*. Agni was born (*ajaniṣṭa*), he was produced (*jajāna*), in the *vayuna*, in the womb-place of the forest-wood (*araṇyāṃ*). [The root] *jan* means "to produce. The *liṭ* [perfect tense] is used in the sense of the *loṭ* [imperative]; the elision of the *ṇi* suffix occurs by the rule "optionally elsewhere also in technical names and Vedic meters" (*bahulamanyatrāpi saṃjñāchandasoh*). Because there is no suffix ending [other than the root], the initial [augment] remains. There is *nighāta* [of the verb]. *Arūpastūpaḥ*: "He whose form (*rūpa*)—meaning anger—is not present is *arūpa*. The meaning is that he shines because of his freedom from anger. By the rule "*nañsubhyām*" [Pāṇini 6.2.172], the final syllable of the second member (*uttarapada*) is udātta. [The root] *puñ* means "to praise. From the rule "*stauterdīrghaśca*" (Uṇādi-sūtra 3.305), the suffix *pap* is added. It is *kit*, and there is lengthening of the root vowel. That which is praised is a *stūpa*, a mass of light. In the *bahuvrīhi* compound "he whose mass of light is formless and shining," the accent of the first member prevails. *Ruśāna*: [The root] *ruś* means "to injure. This is the form in the *śatṛ* [present participle] suffix. *Vayune*: [The root] *aj* means "to go" or "to exhaust. By the rule "*ajayamiśīṅbhyaśca*" [Uṇādi-sūtra 3.54], the suffix *unan* is added, marked with *visarga*. That which is gone to or exhausted is *vayuna*. The suffix is udātta by the rule of transposition (*vyatyaya*). *Ajaniṣṭa*: [The root] *jan* means "to appear. This is the form in the *luṅ* [aorist] with *sic*. There is *nighāta*.
In the footprint of Iḷā, upon the navel of the earth, O Jātavedas Agni, we place thee so that thou mayest carry our oblation.
We place you, O Jātavedas, Agni, upon the navel of the earth, at the station of Iḷā, so that you may carry our oblation. 4.

O Jātavedas, O Agni of born wisdom, we today [place] you upon the earth, above the ground, on the *uttaravedī* (high altar), at its *nābhi*—that is, in the central region which is its very center. That place is further specified: at the *pada* of *Iḷā*, that is, in the footprint of the cow of Manu, in the form of the *iḍāpada* which constitutes the *uttaravedī*. There, we establish you so that you may carry the oblation (*havya*) characterized by the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) and other offerings.

Regarding the meaning stated, there is a Brāhmaṇa passage: "In the place of Iḷā, on the navel of the earth, we establish thee; for the place of Iḷā is the high altar (uttaravedī). 'O Jātavedas, we set thee down upon the navel,' for they indeed hold him fast. 'O Agni, for the carrying of the oblation,' for he is about to carry the oblation" (Ai. Brā. 1. 28).

In *nābhi*: from the root *ṇah* in the sense of "binding," with the suffix *iṣ* being understood [from a previous rule], there is the substitution of *iṣ* for *ṇah*, and the replacement of the final letter by *bh*. Thus, *nabha* + *iṣ* results in *nābhi*.
There is vṛddhi of the penultimate vowel due to the affix *jittva* and other conditions. That which binds (*nahyati*) is the *nābhi*, the central location.
The locative case ending is replaced by *ḍā* according to the rule *supāṃ suluk*.
*jitsvaraḥ* (is the accent on the *ji*).
*dhīmahi* is the form of the root *dadhāti* in the *liṅ* (optative) mood.
The suffix *sīyuṭ* is applied by Pāṇini’s rule 3.4.102 (*liṅaḥ sīyuṭ*). The absence of reduplication is a Vedic archaism (*chāndasa*). There is the *nighāta* accent.
*voḷhave*.
[The root] *vah* means "to carry.
In the sense of the infinitive (*tumun*), it becomes *taven*.
In the word *sahibahorihavarṇasya*, there is the substitution of *ū* for the vowel *a* of the verbal root;
in *ḍhavadhavarṇasya*, there is the elision (*lopa*) of the letters *ḍha* and *va*; and because it begins with *ni*, it is accented on the first syllable (*ādyudātta*).
O men, churn forth the immortal one who speaks like a seer, the most wise, the fair-faced;
O men, bring forth Agni, the banner of sacrifice, the first in the east, the very gracious.
Churn him forth, O men, like a sage—the one who is to be sought, the wise, the immortal, the fair-faced, the banner of sacrifice, the first in the east. O men, generate Agni, the most gracious. 5.
1. *pha* is of the nature of the *tejas* mantra.

2. There is no [reading] "arisen from the *uttaravedi*" (*ta*). 3. *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, and *la* have the sense of the imperative (*loṭ*); *ta* has the sense of the imperative (*loṭ*).
4. The original accent (prakṛtisvara) of the first member [of the compound] ending in -ta.
5. From the root √taṅk, meaning "to go" or "to destroy.
6. From the root √tal, used in the sense of the infinitive suffix -tum.

O men, leaders of rituals, O Adhvaryus and others— churn this Agni by means of friction; [him who is] a seer (kavi) of beautiful vision, who does not act with duplicity, who acts with unity through both mind and speech, performing a single kind of action, and for that reason wise (cetasaṃ), endowed with supreme knowledge, immortal (amṛta), free from the nature of death, and possessed of a beautiful countenance (supratīkaṃ) with splendid flames.

Furthermore: O men, leaders of rituals—such as the Adhvaryus and others—you [should worship] him who is the light (*ketu*) of the sacrifice, such as the Jyotiṣṭoma; that is, the indicator and the primary, principal limb of all subsequent rites, because all later rituals are preceded by Agni.
Generate such a fire—one that is "suśevam," endowed with excellent comfort—at the commencement of the ritual before you;
the sense is: "Make this very fire possessed of the qualities prescribed by the mantra-vidhi. Rub [the fire-sticks].
*Mantha* means "stirring";
this is the form in the *loṭ* (imperative) mood.
Due to its being at the beginning of a metrical foot (*pādādi*), it does not undergo the *anighāta* (lack of accentuation).
*Naraḥ*: [Derived from] the root *ṇīñ* in the sense of "leading" (*prāpaṇe*). By the rule *nayater dic ca* (Uṇādi Sūtra 2.257), the suffix *ṛ* is applied.
Due to the *ḍit* designation, there is elision of the suffix *ṭi*.
They lead the actions, or by means of them actions are led; thus they are "leaders" (*naraḥ*).
Because it is a vocative (*āmantrita*), it receives the *nighāta* (anudātta) accent.
"Non-dual" (*advayanta*): in the sense of "acting as if dual," the suffix *kvip* is prescribed after all nominal stems; thus, having stated this for the sense of "acting like," [we derive] *dvayati*.
The form of that [word] in the nominative plural is *dvayantaḥ*. Not two is *advayaḥ*;
him (*tam*).
In a *tatpuruṣa* compound, [the word] *navaravaraḥ*;
in [a *tatpuruṣa*] with *supratīkam*; and in a *bahuvrīhi*, [words] such as *karavādayaḥ*—these have the acute accent (*udātta*) on the first syllable of the final member (*uttarapada*).
[The root] *jan* means "to produce" or "to manifest. [It takes] the suffix *jic*.

Therefore, when the rule *ata upadhāyāḥ* would have required a *vṛddhi* [increment], the substitution of a short vowel occurs by the rule *mitāṃ hrasvaḥ*, due to the application of the augment *mit* according to the rule *janījṛṣkasurajo'mantāśca*.
There is *nighāta* (elision of the accent).
[The word is] *suśevam*.
The word *śeṣa* ends in the suffix *van*, and is thus udātta on its first syllable.
In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, by the rule "in Vedic [usage], the first syllable of the final member is udātta," the initial syllable of the final member becomes udātta.
If they churn with their arms, the ruddy steed shines like a prize-winning horse;
he is brilliant in the woods like the path of the Aśvins. Unrestrained, he bypasses the stones and the grass.
Burning.

When they churn with their arms, he shines forth like a spirited, ruddy horse in the woods; like the brilliant [light] on the path of the Aśvins, he, unimpeded, avoids the stones while burning the grass.

If the Adhvaryu and others churn him with their arms—that is, with their own hands—then that Agni, once born, being swift-moving (*vājī*) among the woods—that is, among the pieces of wood—red (*aruṣaḥ*), meaning radiant, and being a source of delight to all, shines forth; he blazes intensely on every side. In this regard, there is an illustration: "like a horse."
Just as a horse, swift and radiant, moves among the woods—meaning desirable places or training grounds—so it is here.
In this regard, there is another illustration:
"Like a variegated [horse]."
Just as the variegated chariot of various colors belonging to the two Aśvins, the sons of the gods, moves resplendently with great speed upon their journey,
even so this Agni— whose movement is unimpeded by anything— burning and reducing stones, rocks, and grasses to ashes, completely avoids (*parivṛṇakti*) the places already consumed;
such is the fire that shines forth, as connected with the preceding verse.
They churn.
*Mantha* means "to stir" or "to agitate";
this is the form in the present tense (*laṭ*).
From its connection with this, there is freedom from affliction.
It shines; the root *ruc* means "to shine."
The root *bhū* and others ending in *k*.

1. [The letters] kha, ga, ca, ja, ṇa, ta, pha, bha, and sa belong to the *karmaṇ* [root]. 2. By the churning (*mathana*) of kha, ga, ca, ja, ṇa, ta, bha. 3. [The letters] kha, ga, ca, ja, ṇa, ta, pha, bha, and sa belong to the *karmaṇ* [root]. 4. Ta and ha are the first [letters] of the *adhvaryu* [group]. 5. Of the root *ta-lil-ūḍane*. 6. From the root *ta-prāpaṇe*. 7. Of the root *ta-la-prādurbhāve*. 8. Because of the *mittva* (short vowel) of ja and ṇa; because of the *midvātva* (long vowel) of na, bha, la, and sa. 9. Ca means "then" (*tadā*). 10. Kha, ga, ca, ja, ṇa, bha, and na—this does not exist [in some versions]. 11. Kha, ga, ca, ja, ṇa, bha—this does not exist [in some versions]. 12. Ca means "going" (*yāne*), specifically "moving with speed" (*viśeṣavegagamana*). 13. Kha, ga, ca, ja, ṇa, pa, pha, bha, and devabhija—this does not exist [in some versions]. 14. Kha, ga, ca, ja, ṇa, bha, and various colors (*nānāvarṇaḥ*). 15. Kha, ga, ca, ja, ṇa, pa, pha, and sa mean "going" (*gamana*). 16. Kha, ga, ca, ja, ṇa, pa, and pha mean "he cuts grass excessively" (*tṛṇātīva*); bha and sa mean "he cuts grass excessively" (*tṛṇātiva*). 17. Kha, ga, ja, ṇa, pa, bha, and sa are the places of that horse (*aśvasthāna*); ca and pha are the places at the end of that (*tadantaca-sthāna*). 18. Ta means "churning" (*vilor̤ane*). Of this.

The form [of *yāti*] is in the present tense (*laṭ*). There is a *nighāta* (elision of accent). Regarding *yāman*: from the root *yā* in the sense of "reaching" (*prāpaṇe*), the suffix *manin* is applied by the rule *āto maninkaninvanipaśca*. By the rule *supāṃ suluk...* etc., there is elision (*luk*) of the locative case ending. It has the *nitsvara* (accent on the initial syllable due to the *ni*-augment). Regarding *anivṛtaḥ*: from the root *vṛñ* in the sense of "choosing" (*varaṇe*). In the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*), there is a prohibition of the suffix *it* by the rule *yasya vibhāṣā*. The prefix *ni-* preceding *vṛṇoti* functions in the sense of "obstructing. *Anivṛtaḥ* means "not obstructed. It has the *nañ-svara* (accent on the negative particle *na*). Regarding *vṛṇakti*: from the root *vṛjī* in the sense of "avoiding" (*varjane*). It belongs to the *rudhādi* class. There is the substitution of *ku* for *c* by the rule *coḥ kuḥ*. There is a *nighāta*. Regarding *tṛṇā*: from the root *tṛh* in the sense of "injuring" (*hiṃsāyām*). By the rule *tṛheḥ kro halopaśca* (Uṇādisūtra 5.686), the suffix *kra* is added. Because it is a *kit*, there is no *guṇa* strengthening, and the *hal* (consonant) is elided. That which injures or destroys grass is called *tṛṇam*. It has the *nitsvara*.
Once born, Agni shines forth, glorified— the vigorous one, the inspired sage praised by seers, the bountiful giver,
whom the gods have established at the sacrifices as the all-knowing bearer of oblations, worthy of praise.

Agni has been born; he shines forth, being celebrated—the vigorous one, the inspired singer, praised by sages, the bountiful giver, whom the gods have established at the sacrifices as the one to be invoked, the all-knowing bearer of oblations. 7.

Born—that is, produced immediately after churning—he is *cekitāna*, all-knowing; being *vājī*, he has the nature of constant movement; he is *vipra*, skilled in ritual action; for that very reason, he is *kaviśasta*, praised by the wise and intelligent *hotṛ* priests; and as *sudānu*, he is the excellent bestower of the fruits of ritual action. Such is *Agni*, who *rocate*, shines forth.

The gods—the deities such as Indra and others—established that Agni, who is worthy of praise by the Hotṛ and other priests, who is death, and who is all-knowing (viśvavit), the knower of the entire world; they established him as the carrier of oblations (havyavāha) in the sacrifices (adhvara) such as the Jyotiṣṭoma and others. That Agni is being praised; this is the connection with the preceding verse. [Regarding the word] *cekitāna*: from the root *kita* in the sense of "knowing," in the absence of the *yaṅ* suffix (i.e., in the *yaṅluk* form), the reduplication undergoes *guṇa* substitution according to the rule "guṇo yaṅlukoḥ."

In the word *abhyastānāmādiḥ*, the initial syllable is udātta according to the rule [Pāṇini 6.1.189]. In *kaviśastaḥ*, the final syllable is udātta according to the rule [Pāṇini 6.2.144]: *thāthaghañktājabitrakāṇām*.
They placed [it].
From the root *dhā* in the *liṅ* mood, there is the augment *nuṭ* by the rule "after *siC*, after reduplicated forms, and after [verbs] prescribed with *vidhi*" (*sijabhyastavidhibhyaśca*).
Because it is connected with a word beginning with *yat* (*yadvṛtta*), there is no loss of accent (*anighāta*).
The vowel with the augment *aṭ*:

"Sit down, O Hotṛ, in your own place, being wise; straightway [offer] the sacrifice in the womb of good action. As one who pleases the gods, worship the gods with the oblation; O Agni, bestow great vitality upon the sacrificer."

Sit down, O Hotṛ, in your own place, you who are wise; establish the sacrifice in the womb of good action. Favoring the gods, you shall worship the gods with the oblation. O Agni, bestow great vitality upon the sacrificer. 8.
The sacrificer says:
"O Hotṛ, O Agni, performer of the oblation, sit down in your own place, upon the navel of the northern altar; indeed, sit there for the sake of the oblation.

Thus, being wise and possessed of knowledge, establish the sacrifice—the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice—in the womb, that is, the station of the fruit born of good deeds, in the highest world."
Furthermore, "devāvīḥ":
he who protects the gods by the offering of oblations is *devāvīḥ*.
As such, you worship the gods with the oblation (*havis*), characterized by the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) and other offerings.

1. In *ta*, [the word] *varaṇe* is absent. 2. In *tai*, the "accent of the negative particle" (*nañ-svara*) is not present. 3. In *ṛ*, *tṛ*; in *ja*, *ṇa*, *tṛ*; in *ta*, *la*, *tṛhi*; in *ma*, *tṛṇa*. 4. In *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *pa*, *pha*, *bha*, the word "all" (*sarva*) is not present. 5. In *ma*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *pa*, *pha*, *bha*, [the phrase] "by the *hotṛ*-priests and others" (*hotrādibhiḥ*) is present. 6. In *ja*, *ṇa*, *bha*, *ma*, [the reading] is "on the *uttaravedi*" (*uttaravedyām*).

Sacrifice! Now, while I am performing the sacrifice as the sacrificer (*yajamāna*), bestow (*dhāḥ*) upon me this vast (*bṛhat*) abundance of cattle, sons, and so forth, as well as this food (*vayaḥ*). *Sāda*: This is the form of the root *sad* (to sit) in the imperative (*loṭ*). It means "settle" (*sādaya*). It is the form of the causative (*ṇyanta*) of *sad* in the imperative; the accent is on the causative suffix (*ṇic*). *Devāvīḥ*: [The root] *av* is used in the sense of protection and so forth. The suffix *ī* is applied according to the rule "after the roots *avitṛ*, *mṛ*, and *mantr*, the suffix *ī* [is added]. The accent falls on the final syllable of the compound (*kṛduttarapada-svara*). *Yajāsi*: This is the root *yaj* (to sacrifice) in the subjunctive (*leṭ*) with the augment *āṭ*. *Dhāḥ*: This is the form of the root *dhā* (to place) in the Vedic aorist (*luṅ*).

Produce smoke, O vigorous ones, you who are swift and free from enemies; go toward the prize. This Agni is the conqueror of armies and possesses excellent heroes, by whom the gods overcame the Dasyus.
Make him smoke; O companions, go toward the bull, being unerring, toward the prize. This Agni is the conqueror of armies, possessed of noble heroes, by whom the gods overcame the Dasyus. 9.

The sacrificer speaks to the Adhvaryu and the others: "O friends, you who are collaborators in the ritual, fashion—produce—the *dhūma*, the showerer of desires (*vṛṣaṇam*). [He is called] *dhūma* because he "shakes" (*dhunoti*) or causes to tremble; thus, fashion such an Agni by means of this churning. When the fire is produced, then he says: "Being *asridhantaḥ*—unfailing, with unimpaired power—you, go toward (*accha*) the *vāja*, the battle that is the occasion for churning. This Agni, possessed of excellent power (*suvīraḥ*), becomes a *pṛtanāpāṭ*, one who overcomes the battle characterized by the *pṛtanā*. By means of that Agni who overcomes the battle, the *devāsaḥ* (gods) *asaṃhanta*—overcame—the *dasyūn*, the Asuras who cause destruction. Therefore, the sense is: "With unfailing strength, perform the churning. **Grammatical Notes:** * **kṛṇota**: From the root *kṛvi* (to harm/make). In the imperative (*loṭ*), the suffix *tap* is replaced by *ta* according to *tasanasanathanāśca*; due to the *pit* designation, there is *guṇa*. The accent is on the first syllable due to the rule of *ādyudātta* etc. * **dhūmam**: From the root *dhṛñ* (to shake). According to the rule *ipidhudhṛndhidasi*, the suffix *mak* is added. Due to its *kit* status, there is no *guṇa*. He is called *dhūma* because he shakes the trees; the accent is on the suffix. * **itana**: From the root *iṇ* (to go). In the imperative (*loṭ*), the suffix *tap* is replaced by *tan*. There is *nighāta* (suppression of accent). * **pṛtanāpāṭ**: From the root *paha* (to endure/overcome). In Vedic (*chandasi*), the suffix *ṇvi* is used by the rule *chandasi sahaḥ*. Due to its *kit* status, there is no *vṛddhi* of the penultimate vowel. By the rule *sahaḥ sāḍaḥ saḥ*, the *h* is changed to *ṣ*. The accent is on the final syllable of the compound (*kṛduttarapadasvara*). * **asaṃhanta**: This is the form of the root *paha* (to endure) in the imperfect (*laṅ*). There is *nighāta* due to the *yaṇ* substitution. * **dasyūn**: From the root *dasu* (to destroy). The suffix *yuṣ* is added by the rule *yajimaniśumbhradasijanibhyo yuṣ*. They are called *dasyūn* because they destroy (*dasyanti*); the enemies. The initial vowel is acute (*ādyudāttatvam*) due to the *vyaya* suffix.
This is your seasonal womb, from which once born you shone forth;
knowing it, sit down upon it and cause our songs of praise to flourish.
This is your seasonal birthplace, from which, once born, you shone forth; knowing it, O Agni, sit down upon it, and then cause our songs of praise to flourish. 10.

1. The accentuation of the *na*-pada is not clearly manifest. 2. The forms *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, and *sa* are Vedic (*chāndasa*). 3. The forms *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *bha*, and *rūpa*; *u* is a filler. 4. According to *ta*, the Adhvaryus and others are the auxiliaries of the ritual action (*karman*). 5. In *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *pa*, *pha*, *bha*, and *sa*, the phrase "shakes... such as this" does not exist. 6. According to *na*, by means of churning (*manthana*). 7. According to *ta*, "it would be born" (*jāyeta*). 8. In *ca*, *na*, *bha*, and *sa*, there is churning (*manthana*). 9. According to *ta*, this is in the imperative (*loṭ*) mood. 10. According to *ta*, from the root meaning "to shake" (*kampana*). 11. According to *ta*, from the root meaning "to churn" (*mathane*).

O Agni, you who are seasonal (*ṛtviya*), be present during the seasons beginning with spring. This specific piece of wood, such as the *palāśa* and others, being pointed out by its secret name (*aṅguhya*), is the *araṇi*—your womb, your place of origin. From that *araṇi*, having been born, you shone forth; you were resplendent. Knowing that specific piece of wood in the form of the *araṇi*, sit upon it! Being placed upon this [wood], remain there in a state of stability. Then, immediately after that, cause our songs—our words characterized by praise—to flourish. Or rather, by the word *gīḥ*, those who possess such songs are indicated; thus, cause us, your praisers, to flourish. Make us prosperous with cattle, sons, and other blessings. Regarding the word *yoni*: from the root *yu* in the sense of "mixing" (*miśraṇe*), the suffix *nip* is applied according to the rule *vahipri* etc. Because it is marked with *nit*, the accent falls on the first syllable. Regarding *ṛtviya*: by the rule *chandasi ghas* (Pāṇini 5.1.106), the suffix *ghas* is added to the word *ṛtu* in the sense of "fit for" (*prāsa*). For *gha*, the substitute *iy* is applied. When the technical term *pada* is established, the substitution of *guṇa* prescribed by *orguṇaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.146) does not take effect because it depends on the technical term *bha*. The accent is that of the suffix. Regarding *arocathāḥ*: this is the form of the root *ruc* in the sense of "shining" (*dīptau*) in the *laṅ* tense. Due to its connection with *yadvat*, it is not subject to the *anudātta* (low-pitched) accent. Regarding *sīda*: in the imperative (*loṭ*) of the root *sad*, the substitute *sīd* is applied according to the rule *pāghrā* etc.; it receives the *nighāta* accent. Regarding *atha*: the lengthening is by the rule *nipātasya ca*. Regarding *vardhaya*: from the root *vṛdh* in the sense of "increasing" (*vardhane*), the causative suffix *ṇic* is added in the sense of "causing to do"; it receives the *nighāta* accent. || 33 ||

He is called Tanūnapāt, the Asura embryo; he becomes Narāśaṃsa when he is born. When Mātariśvan measured out [the world] in the mother, there occurred the emission of the wind in its swift course. 11. Tanūnapāt is called the Asura embryo; he becomes Narāśaṃsa when he is born. When Mātariśvan measured out [the world] in the mother, there occurred the emission of the wind in its swift course. 11.
When that fire exists within the womb as the embryo in the two kindling woods (*araṇī*), then that fire is called *Tanūnapāt*.
Alternatively, it is derived from the etymology: "he who does not cause the bodies (*tanūḥ*)—that is, the physical forms—to perish or burn.
Or else, by the word *tanū* water is denoted, and by the word *napāt* offspring who are beloved and well-born.
And likewise: "The nose of the waters.
How is this so?
"The waters are spread out in the intermediate space (antarikṣa)."

From them the herbs and trees are born; from those, food. When he is born—that is, when he is specifically born as a perceptible reality—then he is the "Asura," the slayer of the Asuras who perform various kinds of actions; for this very reason, he becomes the "Narāśaṃsa," one who is to be praised by men—the leaders of ritual action such as the Adhvaryu priests.
Whenever he measures out his own brilliance within the mother, the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*), then he becomes Mātariśvan;
for the etymological derivation is: "he breathes (*śvasiti*) or moves (*ceṣṭate*) within the mother, the intermediate space.
For such a fire, there occurs the emission (*sargaḥ*)—the creation—of Vāta, the wind, during its swift movement (*sarīmaṇi*).
When fire exists within the kindling woods as an embryo, it is then named Tanūnapāt;
when it is born, it is named Narāśaṃsa;
and when it spreads through the intermediate space, it is named Mātariśvan.

*Tanūnapāt*: [The root] *tan* [in the sense of] "to extend. By the rule "after the roots *kṛp*, *vam*, *tan*, *nidhā*, *sarj*, and *ji*, the suffix *ū* [is added]," the suffix *u* (which becomes *ū* after the penultimate vowel) is applied.
The first syllable is udātta due to metrical transposition (vyatyaya).
[The word] *napāt* [is derived from] either the root *pā* "to protect" or *pat* "to go," with the suffix *ap*.
The suffix *kvip* [is applied].
[The word] *napāt* means "he who does not protect" (*na pāti*) or "he who does not cause to fall" (*na pātayati*).
Due to the specific grammatical rule (nipātana) beginning with "na apnapāt pavedā," there is the preservation of the original form (*prakṛtibhāva*) for the negative particle *na*.
*anasvara*:
[The word] *tanūnapāt* means "he who protects the bodies.

Although the rule for the original accent of the final member of a compound (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratva*) would have applied, the rule "in the case of *vanaspati* and similar compounds, both members take their original accent simultaneously" (*ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat*) results in the original accent of both members.
*Āsura*:
belonging to an *asura*; [the term] *āsura* means "belonging to an *asura*" [in the sense of] being connected [to him] by virtue of causing harm.
The suffix *aṇ* is applied [in the sense] of "belonging to him" (*tasyedam*). It has the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*). [Thus:
*narāśaṃsaḥ*.

[The suffix] *ap* is applied by the rule *ṛdorap*. Because the suffix is marked with *p*, the accent is acute on the first syllable (*ādyudātta*). From the root *śaṃs* in the sense of "praise," the form ending in *ghañ* is acute on the first syllable. In the word *nara*, the lengthening occurs by the rule *anyeṣām api dṛśyate*. In the class beginning with *vanaspati*, there is the preservation of the original accent (*prakṛtisvaratva*) for the two initial acute syllables. [He] is born (*vijāyate*). From the root *jan* in the sense of "manifestation," the suffix *śyan* is applied because it belongs to the *divādi* class; the accent is that of the root. [He] measured (*amimīta*). From the root *māṅ* in the senses of "measuring" and "sound," belonging to the *juhotyādi* class; by the rule *bhṛjāmit*, the *abhyāsa* (reduplicated syllable) becomes *it*; the non-elision (*anighāta*) follows from its being in the same *yoga*. In *sarīmaṇi*: from the root *sṛ* in the sense of "motion," the suffix *īmanin* is applied by the *Uṇādi* rule *habhṛsṛstṛsūḥ* (Uṇ. Sū. 4.587); the accent is that of the *nit* suffix.
Well-churned, you have been churned; well-placed, the sage has been established.
O Agni, perform the sacrifice well; worship the gods for the divine one.
Well-stirred, thoroughly churned; well-placed, firmly set—the Seer, O Agni, perform the sacrifices well and worship the gods for the one who seeks the gods. 12.
O Agni, you are a sage, wise and possessed of intelligence; you have been thoroughly churned by excellent churning,
and likewise you have been well-deposited by means of an excellent placement—
you have been firmly established in the locations such as the high altar (uttaravedi).
Furthermore, perform (*kṛṇu*) our sacrificial rites (*svadhvarā*), which we are performing, so that they are well-done and free from injury;
likewise, for the sacrificer who desires the gods (*devayate*), worship (*yaja*) the gods, Indra and the others, who are worthy of sacrifice.
*Sunirmathā*. [The root] *math* means "to churn" (*viloḍane*).
From this, the suffix *kvip* is applied in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāve*), according to the rule for *saṃpad* and so forth.
A *prādi* compound; the accent falls on the final syllable of the second member (*kuduttarapadasvara*);
[the word] *nirmathitaḥ*.
In the phrase *gatiranantaraḥ*, the word *gati* retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvaratva*).
In *sunidhā*, the suffix *aṅ* is applied to the root *dhā* preceded by the prefix *ni* in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāve*), according to the rule *ātaścopasarge*.
By the rule *supāṃ suluk*, there is elision (*luk*) of the third case ending. The accent falls on the final syllable of the compound due to the rule *kuduttarapada-svara*. [The form is] *kṛṇu*.
From the root *kavi* in the sense of "to injure" or "to act," the suffix *loṭ* is applied; then, by the rule *dhṛṇikvṛṇvyoḥ*, the suffix *up* is added.
Furthermore, by the rule *uttaśca pratyayāt*, the suffix *hetuka* is applied.
There is *nighāta* (elision of accent).
Mortals have brought forth the immortal one— the tireless, crossing-over, firm-jawed [Agni]—
while the ten unwedded sisters, moving together, grasp him, the male, as soon as he is born.

The ten sisters, the young maidens, moving together, have brought forth the immortal one from among mortals—him who is tireless, the swift deliverer with firm jaws; they all together grasp him, the male child, at his birth.

The mortal priests generated—that is, produced by churning and kindling—that immortal [Agni], who is free from the law of death and therefore undecaying; whose jaws are firm for the purpose of consuming the oblation; and who is a deliverer, for by means of him the sacrificers cross over evil.

Then, observing that he had been born, the ten sisters—the ten fingers, so called because they move forward (*sarantyaḥ*) and are "agruvahaḥ" (literally "those who anoint the tips," meaning they perform the work of anointing)—being well-aligned (*samīcīḥ*), that is, joined together with one another, [placed him] upon the palm. [The word *samīcīḥ* is derived from the root *i* in the sense of "to go toward" (*saṃ-naye*), with the suffix *ap* added; the accentuation is not present in the *khaga-ca-ja-ṇa-na-pha-bha* recensions. By means of such [fingers], which are free from injury and abundant, [they received him].
5.3.a.2. Sūtra 29: [The section on] the non-existence of the self.

With weapons against enemies, like the advances of the Maruts, these first-born of the sacred word (Brahman) know this entire universe. The Kuśikas have fashioned a radiant sacred word; each one in his own home has kindled Agni. 15.

Armed with weapons against enemies, like the first-born of the Maruts, they have known all through the sacred word (*brahman*). The Kuśikas have brought forth the radiant *brahman*; each one in his own home has kindled Agni. 15.
"Amitrāyudhaḥ" means those who fight with "amitras"— that is, with the gods (asurāḥ) who create obstacles to their actions; or alternatively, "amitras" refers to sins,
and they are those who fight with them.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
"like the *prayas* of the Maruts.

Just as the *prayas* of the Maruts—the gods—advance pre-eminently against their enemies, so too these *prayas* are the slayers of the enemies of Brahman; likewise, they are the slayers of those who create obstacles to one's actions and of sinful deeds.
"Of Brahman" means of the creator of the entire world.

Aiming toward this Soma that has been pressed, "come near"—that is, approach. *Prayati* is a form of the root *iṇ* (to go) in the present participle (*śatṛ*). The case-ending is acute according to the rule *śatruranumaḥ*. *Avṛṇīmahi*: from the root *vṛñ* (to choose). It takes *śva* because it belongs to the *ṛyādi* class. In the imperfect (*laṅ*), third person plural, there is the substitution of *ī* by the rule *ī halyaghoḥ*. Because the vocative is treated as non-existent (*avidyamānavat*), it does not lose its accent (*anighāta*) since it occurs at the beginning of the verse-quarter (*pādādi*). *Ayāḥ*: from the root *yā* (to go/attain); this is the form of the imperfect (*laṅ*) second person singular. It loses its accent (*nighāta*). *Aśamiṣṭhāḥ*: from the causative of the root *śam* (to pacify), in the aorist (*luṅ*) passive; the augment *iṭ* is optionally added by the rule *syasicsīyuṭ* (Pāṇini 6.4.62). Because that [augment] is considered as if non-existent (*asiddha*), the *ṇi* suffix is elided by the rule *ṇeraniṭi*. It loses its accent (*nighāta*). *Prajanan*: from the root *jñā* (to know); this is a form in the present participle (*śatṛ*). *Yāhi*: a form of the root *yā* in the imperative (*loṭ*). || 34 || || 2 ||
"Revealing the meaning of the Veda and dispelling the darkness within the heart,
may Maheśvara, the seeker of knowledge, bestow the four goals of human life.

Thus ends the first chapter of the third book (*aṣṭaka*) in the *Ṛgvedasaṃhitā-bhāṣya*, titled *Vedārthaprakāśa*, composed by Sāyaṇācārya, the upholder of the imperial throne of the illustrious King Vīrabukka— the supreme sovereign of kings and the promoter of the Vedic path— under the patronage of Mādhava.
1. In the manuscripts Kha, Ga, Ca, Ja, Ṇa, Na, Bha, and Sa, the word ‘karmaṇi’ is absent.
2. In the manuscripts Kha, Ga, Ca, Ja, Ṇa, Na, Bha, and Sa, the phrase ‘prajānan...rūpam’ is absent. Homage to the illustrious Gaṇeśa!
I bow to that Great Lord Vidyātīrtha, whose breath is the Vedas and who created the entire universe from the Vedas.

In the third Anuvāka, there are nine hymns (*sūktas*). Among them, the first hymn, consisting of twenty-two verses, begins with "icchanti tvā. Regarding this, the index (*anukramaṇikā*) states: "icchanti; [it has] twenty-two [verses]; Indra [is the deity]."
Viśvāmitra is the seer who beheld the mandala;
Indra is the deity;
the meter is Anuṣṭubh, [and] the meter is Triṣṭubh.

On the first day of the *ābhiplavika* [period] and on the first day of the ten-night rite (*daśarātra*), at the midday pressing (*mādhyandina-savana*) during the *acchāvāka*’s recitation, this second *saṃpāta-sūkta* takes the place of the *ahīna-sūkta*. It is prescribed in the section titled "The *ābhiplava* days with the *pṛṣṭha-stotras*" in the *Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* (7.5): "The *saṃpātas* are 'imām divaḥ', 'accha tvā', and 'śāsad vṛṣṭiḥ'.
Regarding the animal sacrifice for Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, the verse beginning with "sahadānum" is the *yājyā* for the omentum (*vapā*).

Regarding the rule: "He praised Indra, the much-invoked Maghavan, as he lay with his consort when he [slain] the Vṛtras" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 3.8), this is the invitatory verse for the oblation in the animal sacrifice dedicated to Indra.

Furthermore, the rule states: "'For our well-being, O leader, with the swift ones; pure are your oblations, O Maruts, for you who are pure'" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 3.7). This is the offering verse for the oblation in the animal sacrifice dedicated to Indra.
In the Śunāsīrīya sacrifice, for the optional Indra-Śuna, the invitatory verse (*anuvākyā*) is "śunaṃ huvema" (We invoke auspiciously).
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "śunaṃ huvema madhavānam indram aśvāyanto gavyanto vājayantaḥ" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 2.20).
The Soma-loving friends desire you; they press the Soma and present the sacrificial offerings.
They endure the insults of men, for no other light exists but you, O Indra.
The Soma-loving friends desire you; they press the Soma and offer sacrificial foods. They endure the insults of men, for, O Indra, there is no wisdom whatsoever other than from you. 1.
Viśvāmitra praises:
O Indra, these Soma-offering Brāhmaṇas desire to praise you; for this very reason, they, as your friends, press out and pour the Soma for your sake.
They present other sacrificial foods (*prayāṃsi*) as well, holding them for your sake.

Impelled by you, they endure—that is, they patiently bear—the curse and the violence inflicted upon them by their rivals. Indeed, who else besides you could be such a benefactor? Truly, what man is there in the entire world who is *praketana*—one who makes himself known from every side?
For *praketana* means one who is made known (*praketyate*) everywhere.
It has been made known that it exists.

*Somyāsaḥ*: in the sense of "those who deserve the *soma*," the suffix *yaḥ* is applied according to the rule "that which deserves it" (*somamarhati yaḥ*). It bears the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
They press [the Soma]. "O son, at the pressing. By virtue of the *svādi* suffix, there is the substitution of *śru*.
Since the accent of a suffix taught by the grammarians (*śiṣṭasvara*) is stronger, it is the accent of the *jhi* suffix [that prevails].
*Dadhati* is the form of the root *dhā* in the present indicative (*laṭ*).

According to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 8.1.18, "In a single sentence, the substitutes for *yuṣmad* and *asmad* [receive] the *nighāta* accent," the word *soma* does not receive the *nighāta* because it belongs to a different sentence.
By the rule "The beginning of reduplicated [verbs] (*abhyasta*) [is acute]," it has the acute accent on its first syllable.
[Thus they] endure.
From the root *tij* in the sense of "sharpening," the suffix *san* is applied according to the rule *gu-ti-ky-abhyaḥ san*;
it has the accent of the reduplicated stem (*abhyasta-svara*). [The word is] *abhiśasti*.
From the root *śas* in the sense of "to injure," the suffix *ktin* is applied to form the abstract noun (*bhāve*).
By the rule "and when *tādi* follows *ni*, the *kṛt* suffixes [retain] the original accent of the verbal root" (*tādau ca niti kṛtyatau*), the root *gati* retains its original accent.
Thus: *praketaḥ*.
In the word *jñāna*,
the suffix *ghañ* is applied in the sense of the object (*karman*).
By the rule *thāthaghañ*, it has an udātta accent on the final syllable.

1. In the manuscripts Kha, Ga, Gha, Ca, Ja, Ṇa, Bha, the phrase "yasya...maheśvaram" is absent. 2. In manuscript Kha, it occurs at the end of the Ahīna-hymn. 3. In manuscripts Ta and Sa, it is the *vapā-yājyā*. 4. In manuscript Pa, it is "ājñāpitaḥ". 5. In manuscript Ta, it is "śrapratyayaḥ". 6. In manuscripts Kha, Ga, Gha, Ca, Ja, Ṇa, Pha, Bha, and Sa, it is "śiṣṭe". 7. In manuscript Kha, it is "pratyayasvaraḥ". 8. In manuscripts Kha, Ga, Ca, Ja, and Ṇa, it refers to "samānavākyeṣu". 9. In manuscripts Ta, La, and Sa, it is "uttaravākyena". 10. In manuscripts Ta and La, it is "ghañantaḥ". [The verse: "Those highest realms are not far away; come hither with your two bay horses, O Lord of the Bay Steeds."
For the steadfast bull, for him who hears all, these pressing-stones have been harnessed while the fire is kindled.

No, they are not far away, even though they are in the highest regions; come hither, O Lord of the Bay Steeds, with your two Bays! These pressed juices have been prepared for you, the firm and powerful one; the pressing-stones are yoked while the fire is kindled. 2.

"O *Harivaḥ*": he whose two horses are greenish-yellow (*hari-varṇa*) is this Indra, the possessor of bay horses (*harivān*). O *Harivaḥ*, even "the highest" (*paramā*), that is, the most distant "regions" (*rajāṃsi*) or stations, are not far from you.
Therefore, come quickly, "approaching with your two bay horses."
Come toward our sacrifice!

For you—who are steadfast in bestowing the fruit [of the rite], whose mind is firm, and who are therefore a "bull" (vṛṣṇe) raining down desires—these libations (savanā), namely the morning and subsequent ones, have been prepared again and again.
Furthermore:
When the Āhavanīya fire is kindled and blazing brightly as the locus for the oblation, the pressing-stones—the stones employed and prepared for the purpose of pressing the Soma—are ready;
therefore, the sense is that you should come quickly.
"Yāhi" is the form of the root "yā," meaning "to go," in the imperative mood (loṭ). "Harivaḥ."
The suffix *matup* is present in the word *harī-as-ya-staḥ*. By the rule "in the Veda, [the suffix] *iraḥ*," its *vatva* (substitution of *vat*) occurs.
Due to being an *āmantrita* (vocative), there is a pause (*śighāta*).

For *sthirāya*: from the root *sthā* in the sense of "cessation of motion," there is the elision of the vowel *ā* due to its being a word formed with the suffix *kira* by the rule beginning with *ajira-śiśira-*;
[the accent is] the *cit-svara*.

*Savanā*: From the root *sū* in the sense of "pressing" (*abhiṣava*), the suffix *lyuṭ* is applied according to the rule *lyuṭ ca* to form the locative base; thus, *savanāni* refers to those [times] such as morning (*prātaḥ*) and so forth, wherein the Soma is pressed.
*litsvaraḥ* | *samidhāne*: this is the form of the root *dīp* (meaning "to shine") with the suffix *kānac*.
Due to the *kittva* designation, there is the elision of the letter *k*;
[this results in] the *citsvara* accent.
O Indra, fair-cheeked, bountiful, overcomer of foes, leader of great hosts, mighty, and exalted—
when you, the fierce one, were oppressed by mortal man, what heroic deeds did you perform then, O Bull?

O Indra, fair-cheeked, bountiful, victorious, with a great host, performing many deeds, and exalted—when you, O fierce one, were oppressed among mortals, what were your heroic exploits, O Bull? || 3 ||
"O Indra, showerer of desires, O bull! He who is Indra, endowed with supreme sovereignty, is *suśipra*.
By the word *śipra*, a helmet is denoted;
[he is] one possessed of a beautiful helmet."
Or, he is one who possesses beautiful jaws; Yāska states, "Śipre refers to the jaws or the nostrils" (Nirukta 6.17).
He is the bountiful Maghavan, the protector.
Indra is called *tarutra* because "the gods cross over their enemies by means of him.
He is called *mahāvrāta* because he possesses a great host (*vrāta*), that is, a multitude of Maruts.

He is *tuvikurmi*, the performer of various deeds in battle. He is *ūrdhvavān*, one who possesses the power to slay enemies; for this very reason, he is *ugra*, the terrifier of foes. Being thus [described], you, though *bādhitaḥ*—oppressed by the Asuras in battle—performed those heroic deeds (*vīryāṇi*) among the *matyaiḥ*, the murderous Asuras.

1. *ta-sa-he* [is] *harivaḥ*. 2. *kha-gha-na-bha-* [are] *harivarṇau*; *ṇa-sa-* [are] *haritavarṇau*. 3. *ja-ṇa-tala-* [are] *haribhyāmśvābhyām*. 4. *kha-ga-ya-ja-ṇa-bha-sa-* [the reading] *'tu kṣipraṃ'* does not exist; *ta-la-* [is] *kṣipram*. 5. *kha-ga-gha-ca-ja-ṇa-na-bha-sa-* [have] *imāni savanāni*; *la-* [has] *imā imāni savanāni*. 6. *la-* [the reading] *'citsvaraḥ'* does not exist. 7. *ta-* [is] *yasya*. 8. *ta-* [is] *tedhvasureṣu*. 9. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-bha-sa-* [have] *vīryāṇi ca*.

You have now performed those heroic deeds; tell us, who can surpass them? *Suśipraḥ*: From the root *sūplṛ* (to go), the suffix *ran* is added according to the *Uṇādi* rules. By way of irregularity (*bāhulaka*), the syllable *sṛ* is replaced by *śi*. In the *bahuvrīhi* compound, the first syllable of the second member is acute-accented (*ādyudātta*) according to the rule "that which is [first] in the Veda. *Taraṇiḥ*: From the root *tṛ*, the suffix *ini* is added according to the rule "after *aśitrā* and others, *in* and *au*. There is an irregular shift of the acute accent to the beginning. *Mahāvānataḥ*: According to the rule "for *ātman* and *mahat*," the vowel *ā* replaces the *t* of *mahat*. *Nuvikramiḥ*: The suffix *mi* is added to the root *kṛ* according to the *Uṇādi* rules. Once the *guṇa* substitution has occurred, the change of the vowel of *kṛ* to *u* is Vedic (*chāndasa*). The lengthening occurs by the rule "before a consonant" (*halica*). *Ṛdhāvāna*: From *ṛn* (or *nṛn*) and *han*, the suffix *yu* is added. By the rule "it is seen after others as well," the suffix *vic* is applied. Due to the mention of *haśi*, there is elision of the letter *h* and its replacement by *gh*. In the sense of the possessive suffix *matup*, the suffix *vanip* is used according to the rule "in the Veda, *van* and *nip*. There is an irregular shift of the acute accent to the beginning. *Ka*: From the word *kim*, the suffix *an* is added in the sense of the locative case according to the rule "from *kim*, *an*. In that context, the substitution of *kā* for *ka* occurs. It has the accent of the third case.
For you alone, shaking what is shaken, advance against the Vṛtras as you strike them down;
heaven and earth, the mountains, and all things stand firm for your ordinance, as if fastened in place.
For you alone, shaking even the unshakable, move about as the sole slayer of Vṛtras; heaven and earth, and the mountains, stand fast according to your law, like subjects set in their places.

O Indra, you alone, without a companion, causing even those *acyuta*—the immovable and firm ones—to fall, that is, casting down from their respective places the demons who have become your adversaries; likewise, striking down *vṛtrāṇi*, meaning sins, you indeed move about, acting thus. Furthermore, for the sake of your *vrata*—your deed or command—the two worlds, heaven and earth, and the mountains stand as if measured out, remaining motionless like those sheltered from the wind.
The prefix *ca* and others are unaccented;
[the form] *cyāvayan*.
The form *carasi* is the present active participle (*śatṛ*) of the causative (*ṇyanta*) root *cyu*, meaning "to go" (*gatau*), with the accent on the causative suffix (*ṇic-svara*). You move.
The root *car* means "to move" and "to eat.
Due to its connection with the prefix *hi*, it becomes *vanivātaḥ*.
[The form] is *jighnamānaḥ*.

From the root *han*, meaning "to kill" or "to go," the suffix *ka* is applied according to the rule "there is the application of *ka* in the sense of *ghan*. Because of the rule "in the Veda, [the suffixes] are optionally both [verbal and nominal]," this [suffix *ka*] is treated as a verbal suffix (*sārvadhātuka*), and thus the suffix *śap* is applied.
The elision of this [suffix *śap*] follows by the rule "its [elision]."

By the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pāṇini 7.1.8), this [substitution] occurs for the reduplicated syllable. From the root *han*, we derive *jighna* by adding the suffix *kvip* in the sense of habitual action (*ācāra*).
From this [root], the suffix *vāna* is applied in the sense of habit (*tācchīlya*) and so forth; then *śap* is added;
and by transposition (*vyatyaya*), the initial syllable is acute-accented (*ādyudātta*).
*dyāvāpṛthivī*:
By the rule *devatādvandve ca*, there is the preservation of the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) for both members of the compound. It is as if [they were] fixed in place.
The suffix *niṣṭhā* is applied to the root *ḍumiñ* in the sense of "throwing" (*prakṣepaṇe*).
By the rule *gatiranantaraḥ*, the preceding prefix retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*).
By the rule *supāṃ suluk*, the case-ending (*sup*) is replaced by the suffix *ḍā*.
The accent of the first member [of the compound] was stated by the rule *ivena vibhaktyalopaḥ*.
They stood (*tasthuḥ*).

Regarding the root *sthā* (meaning "to stop" or "cease moving") in the perfect tense with the suffix *us*, after the elision of *āna*, there is reduplication because of the status of being a *sthānivadbhāva* (the substitute behaves like the original) according to the rule *dvirvacane'ci*.
The elision of the accent.

1. [The suffix] *ta* has the sense of the abstract suffix (*matvartha*). 2. A *ta* that bears the *tiṅ* marker is circumflex (*svarita*). 3. [The letters] *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *jha*, *bha*, and *cyava* are excluded. 4. And [the letters] *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *pa*, *pha*, *bha*, *sa*, *parva*, *ta*, and *asa*. 5. In *kha*, *pha*, and *bha*, the accent is that of the *cit* suffix. 6. The suffixes *ta*, *u*, and *ka*. 7. [The letters] *kha*, *ga*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, *la*, *sa*, and *jighnatīni*. 8. A compound with *iva*. 9. [The rule] regarding the elision (*lopa*) of *ja* and *ṇa*.
"O Puruhūta, you alone, being the slayer of Vṛtra, are firm and free from distress through your glories;
even these two boundless worlds, O Maghavan, you grasped together when you were eager for the prize."

Moreover, O fearless one, much-invoked Indra, as the slayer of Vṛtra, you alone have spoken with renown that which is firm. Even these two boundless worlds, O Indra, when you grasp them together, O Maghavan, are but a handful to you. 5.
The word "uta" is used as a vocative particle.
O Indra, "puruhūta," you who are invoked by many— by numerous gods—
or indeed, you who have been summoned many times by the gods for the sake of protection from the Asuras.

"By means of thy glorious deeds and heroic forms, O thou who art alone and without companion, thou hast spoken that word to the gods—'I am the slayer of Vṛtra; do not fear the Asuras because of me'—and that word was indeed firm and true.
Furthermore, O Maghavan Indra, even these two worlds, heaven and earth, though they are boundless and far-extended, [are encompassed by thee]."

The suffix *vati* is applied according to the rule *sargāc chandasi dhāvarthe* (Pāṇini 5.2.109). It bears the accent of a primary suffix (*pratyayasvara*). In *pramṛṇan*: the root *mṛṇ* means "to injure. In *jahi*: the root *han* means "to injure" or "to go. In the imperative (*loṭ*) third person singular, the suffix *sip* is replaced by *hi*. In that context, the rule *hanter jaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.36) prescribes the replacement of *han* with *ja*. Although the rule *ato heḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.105) would have required the elision (*luk*) of this *hi*, it is blocked because the preceding grammatical operation is considered as if non-existent (*asiddha*) according to the principle *ābhācchāstrasyāsiddhatvāt*. Since *hi* is marked with *h* (indicating it is *anudātta*), it is unaccented. In *pratīcaḥ*: the root *añc* means "to go" or "to honor. According to the rule *accchandasyasarvanāmasthānam* (Pāṇini 6.1.166), the case-ending receives the acute accent. In *parācaḥ*: by the rule *aniganto 'nnatau vapratyaye* (Pāṇini 6.2.52), the preceding prefix retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvaratva*). In *kṛṇuhi*: the root *kṛvi* means "to injure" or "to do. In *astu*: the root *as* means "to exist."
To whomsoever Dhāyu has granted a dwelling, he shares even a portioned-out house;
auspicious is your favor, O Indra, dripping with clarity, and your gift, O Much-invoked One, consists of thousands.

To whatever mortal man you grant a full lifespan, he shares even a house that was not his own. O Indra, your benevolent favor is dripping with clarity; O Much-invoked One, your gift bestows thousands. 7.

O Indra, you who possess the power to bestow sovereignty without interruption, for whichever mortal man you grant wealth—that mortal man attains even that which was previously unshared and unobtained; whatever exists within the home, such as gold, cattle, and so forth, he enjoys and acquires.
Furthermore, O Puruhūta, Indra invoked by many, [you are] Ghṛtācī.
The word *ghṛta* indicates sacrificial oblation (*havis*) in general.
Thus, [the goddess] is called *ghṛtācī* because she partakes of the oblation characterized by Soma, clarified butter (*ājya*), sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*), and so forth.
Your benevolent thought (*sumatiḥ*)—your excellent and auspicious intellect—is *bhadrā*, that which brings about welfare.
Likewise, your bounty—the power of your giving—is endowed with the gift of thousands, accompanied by the bestowal of immeasurable wealth.
Regarding Indra’s status as a great giver, there is a Vedic mantra: "O bountiful giver, give us abundantly; do not give little; bring to us abundance" (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 4.32.20).
*Dhāyuḥ*: the suffix *u* is added to the root *dhā* according to the *Uṇādi* rules. *Ardhāḥ*.
This is the form of the root *dhā* in the *lṛṅ* (conditional) tense;
it lacks the *nighāta* accent because it is connected with *yad-vṛtta*.
[The word is] *martyāya*.
*Martya* means "mortal. The suffix *yan* is applied in its own sense (*svārthika*) because it is listed among the words beginning with *vasu*.
By the rule *yato ’nāvaḥ*, the first syllable is udātta (accented).
*geham*. From the word *geha*, in the sense of "that which exists there" (*tatra bhavaḥ*), the suffix *yan* is applied by the rule *bhave chandasi*;
it has an indicatory letter *t* and is svarita-accented.
Sumatiḥ:
By the rule "mantre vṛṣa" and so forth, the word *mati* has its final syllable accented (antodātta).
In a compound, the accent falls on the final syllable of the second member (*kṛduttarapadasvara*).
*Rātiḥ*: from the root *rā* in the sense of "giving" (*dāne*). By the rule "in mantras, after *vṛṣa* etc.," the suffix *kvi* is applied, and the word is udātta-accented.
O Indra, much-invoked, crush Kuṇāra to pieces along with his followers as he lies there;
O Indra, with your might, you struck down Vṛtra, the footless, arrogant, and swelling enemy.
Along with Dānu, O Indra, much-invoked one, you crushed the handless Kuṇāru as he lay still; you struck down with your might, O Indra, the footless Piśāru who was growing strong against Vṛtra.
O Indra, invoked by many, you [overcame] Dānu;
Dānu is the mother of Vṛtra, and [you overcame him] as he was together with her.
Thus says the mantra-text: "Dānu lies there together with her calf" (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1.32.9).

Or rather: "together with the *dānus*, the *dānavas*"; [1] the suffix *talavati*; [2] *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-pa-pha-bha-sa* for the parasmaipada; [3] *tannidadhāsi*; [4] *kha-ga-gha-ca-ja-ṇa-bha-sa*—gold, cattle, and so forth; [5] *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa*—"likewise" (*tathā*) is not present; [6] *kha-ga-ca*—"the power of wealth" (*dhanaśakti*); [7] *kha-ga-gha-ca-ja-ṇa-bha*—"*dānuḥ*" is not present.

"He who dwells together" is *sahadānuḥ*. Him, "dwelling" (*kṣiyantam*), meaning harassing, "the roaring one" (*kuṇāham*)—a certain Asura who makes a sound—you "struck down," having rendered him handless; you "crushed him thoroughly" (*saṃ piṇak*), that is, you ground him to powder. Furthermore, O Indra, "Vṛtra," the injurer who was "increasing" (*vardhamānam*) on all sides to the measure of an arrow—according to the Śruti: "He grew arrow-length by arrow-length" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 2.4.12.2)—you, having made him footless, "struck him down with might" (*tavasā abhi jaghantha*). Alternatively: *sahadānum* means endowed with the giving of water (*udaka-dāna*), "dwelling" (*kṣiyantam*)—residing in the sky—"the roaring one" (*kuṇāham*), Vṛtra. For Vṛtra is the cloud, so called because it "covers" (*vṛṇoti*) or veils the sky. You, having made this increasing cloud devoid of hands and feet, "crushed it together" (*saṃ piṇak*), that is, you crushed it into a mass. Thus says Yāska: "O Indra, having made the thundering cloud handless, you crushed it" (Nirukta 6.1). Regarding *sahadānum*: from the root *do* in the sense of "cutting" (*avakhaṇḍane*), the suffix *nu* is added by the rule *dābhyāṃ nuḥ*. *Dānuḥ* is thus "giving" (*dānam*). In the Bahuvrīhi compound, the accent remains on the first member. *Kṣiyantam*: from the root *kṣi* in the sense of "dwelling" (*nivāsa*) and "going" (*gati*). By being in the *tudādi* class, the suffix *śa* is applied. The accent is that of the suffix. *Piṇak*: from the root *piñ* in the sense of "crushing" (*sañcūrṇe*). By belonging to the *rudhādi* class, the suffix *śnam* is applied. The substitution of *he* for *leṭ* occurs. The change of *pa* to *ka* is Vedic (*chāndasa*). *Kuṇāham*: from the root *kuṇa* in the sense of "sound. The form is established by general usage (*bāhulakāt*). It has the acute accent on the first syllable. *Jaghantha*: this is the form of the root *hana* (meaning "to strike" or "to go") in the Perfect tense (*liṭ*) with the suffix *thal*. By the rule *abhyāsācca*, the *ha* of the root becomes *gha*. There is the suppression of the accent (*nighāta*). The prohibition of the augment *it* applies by the rule *upadeśe'cvataḥ*.
O Indra, you have established the level-headed earth, vast and boundless, upon its foundation;
as a bull, you propped up the sky and the mid-air, and here the waters flow forth, released by you.
O Indra, you have established the swift, vast, great, and boundless flood in its seat; the Bull has propped up the sky and the mid-air. By you the flowing waters were set loose here. 9.

O Indra, [make] this great earth vast indeed—boundless, vigorous, and moving as if by its very nature; such is the earth, which is *sāman*, meaning "equal. Thus says a Vedic verse: "The two cows of yours are equal" (*Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* 10.85.11).
Or rather, that which is equal (*sama*) is itself *sāma*.

And thus it is heard in the *Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa*: "Because it is equal to a wolf, equal to a gnat, equal to an elephant, and equal to these three worlds, therefore it is called *Sāman*" (*ŚB* 14.4.1).
One who possesses that [quality] is *sāmanaḥ*.
Having made her *sāmyavatīm* (possessing equanimity), you caused her to settle, you established her, in her own place, in her proper station.
Likewise, Indra, the bull who rains down desired fruits, "stabilized" (astabhnāt) the sky—the celestial world—so that it does not fall;
likewise, he stabilized the intermediate space.
When heaven and earth are thus established, may the waters, released by you through the various clouds, flow here upon this earth.
And thus says a Vedic mantra: "He who upheld the trembling earth" (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 2.12.2).
Sāman:
*sama* itself is *sāma*. The suffix *ca*, which occurs after words beginning with *pāman* in the sense of the possessive suffix *matup*—as in "that which has this"—is applied here.
The accent is due to the suffix (pratyaya-svara). [The form] *iṣirām* [is derived from the root] *iṣ* in the sense of "to go."
By the rule *iṣimadimudikhidicchidibhidivṛśo 'dṛśaḥ kiran* (Uṇādi Sūtra 1.51), the suffix *kirac* is applied.
Due to its *kit*-nature, there is no *guṇa* substitution.
It bears the *citsvara* accent.

*Sasattha*: [This is derived] from the root *ṣaṭ*, meaning "to fall apart," "to go," or "to weaken," with the causative sense (*antarbhāvitaṇyartha*) implied. In the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*), because of the rule "in the case of a consonant following [the suffix]," there is a prohibition of the substitution of *it* by the rule "not after a vowel in the original instruction (*upadeśe*). There is also the *nighāta* (elision of accent).
He obstructed. The verbal root *stambh* (in the form *stambhu*) meaning "to obstruct" is a Vedic (sautra) root.
The suffix *ap* is applied according to the rule beginning with "*stambhustambhu*."
By the rule "elision of the suffix -śna," there is the elision of the root vowel *kāra*. Then follows the accent of the augment *aṭ* in the word *ta*.
2. Having made the *ta*, *la*, *ap*, and *rāṃ* [phonemes] equal to the *pu*, *ru*, and *pārāṃ*;
3. having made the *ja*, *ṇa*, *sā*, and *mānāṃ* equal to the *sāmyavartī*;
4. the reading "samānāṃ" is not found in the manuscripts *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *bha*, and *sa*.
5. *ta-sāmanā*. 6. The letters *kha-ga-gha-ca-ja-ṇa-bha-sa* do not exist in the word *sve*. 7. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-bha* read *nivedayāmāsa*; *gha-pa-sa* read *niveśayāmāsa*.

8. By the rule "there is elision of the *n* of roots [ending in] *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *sa*, or *śra*," there is elision of the *n* of the root. *Arṣenu*: from the root *ṛṣ* (meaning "to go"), with the suffix *śap* by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*), followed by *guṇa*. It is not subject to the *anighāta* accent because it begins the foot. *Āpaḥ*: from the root *āplu* (meaning "to pervade"), with the suffix *kvip* and shortening of the vowel. In the nominative plural (*jas*), there is lengthening by the rule "for *ap*, *nu*, *tu*, etc. Since the *jas* is unaccented due to being a *suhit* suffix, the accent of the root remains. *Prasūtāḥ*: this is the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*) of the root *pṛ* (meaning "to impel") used in the sense of the object. According to the rule "the preceding prefix retains its original accent," the prefix retains its natural accent.
O Indra, the enclosure of the cow was opened by you, the unsubduing one; before the slayer could strike, it burst open in fear.
You made the paths easy to traverse and drove the cattle out into the open air. The voices of those singing your praise went forth toward the one invoked by many, as they followed his law.

Alātṛṇa, Vula, Indra, Vraja, Go, Purā, Hanta, Bhayamāna—having opened them wide, he made the paths easy to traverse and led the cattle out; the voices of praise, yearning for him who is invoked by many, gave him their full support. 10.

O Indra, you are *alātṛṇa*. Because he is not obstructed (*alamartya*) due to his great power, he is called *alātṛṇa*—one who cannot be harmed. *Goḥ* refers to the speech of the intermediate region (*mādhyamikā vāk*). *Vrajaḥ* is the enclosure, the *vala*. It is called *vala* because it covers (*vṛṇoti*) the sky; thus, *vala* is the cloud. *Pura hantoḥ*: before your strike with the thunderbolt, being terrified and afraid, it became scattered (*vyāra*). Thereafter, that Indra made the paths easy to traverse (*sugān*) in order to drive out (*niraje*) the cows—the waters. Therefore, those waters, desirable (*vāṇīḥ*) and flowing (*dharmantīḥ*), went toward the much-invoked (*puruhūtam*) earthly water. Yāska explained this ṛc as follows: "Alātṛṇa is Vala, the enclosure of the cow. Alātṛṇa means 'not able to harm,' the cloud; Vala is from the root *vṛ*, to cover; Vraja is the atmosphere, the enclosure of the cow, of that intermediate speech. Before the striking, being afraid, it was scattered. He made the paths easy to traverse to let the cows out. The desirable voices flowed toward the much-invoked one. The waters, or the voices, flow because they carry or because they speak; the water is so called because it is seized by many. *Dhamati* is a verb meaning 'to move'. (Nirukta 6.2). *Alātṛṇaḥ*: From the root *tṛh* (to injure), preceded by *alam*, the suffix *ka* is added in the sense of the object according to the rule "the addition of *ka* is prescribed in the sense of *ghañ*. The *m* of *alam* becomes *a*. The accent is that of the compound. *Valaḥ*: From the root *val* (to cover). That which covers or conceals the sky is *vala*, the cloud. The suffix *gha* is used in the masculine for a name. The accent is that of the suffix. *Vrajaḥ*: From the root *vraj* (to go). By the rule "gocara-saṃcara... etc., it is a word ending in *gha*; hence there is no *kutva* change. *Vraja* is the atmosphere. The accent is that of the suffix. *Bhayamānaḥ*: From the root *bhī* (to fear). The *śap* affix is used by transposition. *Āra*: This is the form of the root *ṛ* (to go) in the perfect tense (*liṭ*), with the suffix *gal*. It receives the *nighāta* accent. *Sugān*: From the root *gam* (to go), the suffix *ḍa* is added in the sense of location according to the rule "su-duro-r-adhikaraṇe. Due to reduplication, there is elision of the radical vowel. The accent is that of the whole word. *Niraje*: From the root *aj* (to move/throw), the suffix *kip* is added in the sense of an abstract noun (*bhāve*) according to the rule "saṃpad-ādi-lakṣaṇā. The accent is that of the subsequent *kṛt* suffix. *Āvan*: This is the form of the root *ava* (to protect/move) in the imperfect (*laṅ*). *Puruhūtam*: From the root *hve* (to call), the past participle suffix (*niṣṭhā*) is applied. Because it belongs to the *yajādi* group, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). The lengthening occurs by the rule "halaḥ. The accent is that of the first syllable of the root. *Dharmantīḥ*: From the root *dham* (to sound). With the *śap* affix, the substitution of *dham* for *dhamā* occurs by the rule "pāghrā...". In the Vedic language, the *jam* (nasal) is optionally replaced by a long vowel (*savarṇadīrgha*).
