Third Aṣṭaka, 317:
O Indra, you alone have filled the two world-halves, the earth and the heaven, as well as the mid-air.
From the atmosphere, come to our encounter, O charioteer of nourishment, O hero of power, and bring us strengths and spoils of war.

One; two; Vasumatī (the earth rich in wealth); Samīcī (the two meeting together); Indra; hither; forward; the earth; and also the sky; and from the intermediate space; toward us; in the encounter; the driver of the chariot; with his companions; O hero, [bring] strengths and spoils of war. 11.
This Indra, being alone and without companion, has filled from all sides these two—the earth and the heaven, these two joined and united worlds, rich in wealth—in an instant.

And furthermore, O Hero, you who possess such power, being the master of the chariot, desiring for us to stay near the battle, drive hither from the mid-air those yoked steeds who go toward the spoils; "vājās" are horses, so drive them forth from the intermediate space.

In *rathārūḍhatvam*, there is a short vowel by [Pāṇini 6.3.134] *asmatsamaramīnāternigama*. In *haryaśvaprasūtāḥ*, there is the original accent of the first member [of the compound] by [Pāṇini 6.2.49] *turīyā kaḥ ṇi*. In *ānaṭ*, the substitution of *luṅ* for *laṭ* occurs by [Pāṇini 3.4.78] *bahulaṃ chandasi* from the root *aś* meaning "to pervade"; the augment *nuṭ* is applied by [Pāṇini 7.1.58] *abhyastācca*; and the change to *ṣ* [in *ānaṭ*] is due to the presence of *va* and so forth. Furthermore, there is no *anudātta* (unaccented) status for *yat* because it is not part of a *samāsa* (compound).
They longed to behold the wondrous countenance of the Night as she approached, like the light of the sun;
all recognize her greatness when she has come, for Indra’s well-wrought deeds are many.
They desire to behold the wondrous face of the Dawn as she comes at the end of night; all recognize her majesty when she has arrived, for Indra’s well-performed deeds are many.

"All people (viśve janāḥ), when the departure of the night (aktaḥ) connected with the dawn (uṣasaḥ)—belonging to Vivasvat (vivasvatyāḥ)—has occurred at every departure (yāman yāmani), they desire to see (didṛkṣante) the great (mahi), wonderful (citram), and beautiful (anīkam) solar splendor.

When (yat) the time of dawn (uṣaḥkālaḥ) has arrived from all sides, then all people, desiring to see that splendor, recognize (jānanti) by its greatness (mahinā) the great (mahinā) rites such as the Agnihotra, understanding them as duties to be performed."
O Indra, "many" means numerous; "well-done" means properly performed; "deeds" refers to actions; [these belong] to you alone, O Indra.
They wish to see (*didṛkṣante*).
From the root *dṛś* in the sense of "seeing," when the desiderative suffix (*san*) is added, the Ātmanepada ending is applied according to Pāṇini Sūtra 1.3.57: *jñā-śru-smṛ-dṛśāṃ sanaḥ*.
It bears the accent of the reduplicated (*abhyasta*) form.
Of *vivasvatī*:
[it is derived] from the root *vi-vās* with the suffix *kvip* according to the rule for *saṃpad* and so forth;
by transposition, there is the substitution of *s* for the penultimate vowel.
Therefore, the suffix *matup* is applied [to form *bhagavat*] according to the rule "tad asyāsti. By the rule "mādupadhāyāḥ," its *v* is substituted for *m*.
Since the *matup* suffix is enclitically unaccented when following a word ending in *paśu*, the accent of the verbal root remains.
They know.
[The root] *jñā* means "to understand.
By the rule *jñā-ur-jā*, the substitution of *jā* occurs.
Nighāta (elision of accent). *Agāt* is the form of the root *iṇ* (meaning "to go") in the *luṅ* (aorist) tense.
And as for the absence of elision (*u-gāda-nighāta*): it is *sukṛtā*. By the rule “*gatiranantaraḥ*” (Pāṇini 6.2.49), the preceding *gati* retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*).
A great light is deposited within her flanks; the cow moves about bearing both the raw and the cooked.
All vigor has been gathered within the cow, which Indra bestowed for the sake of enjoyment.

Great light is deposited within her flanks; the raw cow moves about bearing the cooked milk. All strengthening nourishment has been gathered within the cow, which Indra established for the sake of enjoyment.

"In the *vakṣaṇās*— those in which waters flow, the *vakṣaṇās* being rivers— in them, 'great' (*mahi*), that is, vast, 'light' (*jyotiḥ*), meaning luminous water, has been 'placed by Indra. The 'raw' (*āmā*) cow, meaning one that has recently calved, 'bearing' (*bibhratī*) or possessing the 'cooked' (*pakam*), such as milk and so forth, 'moves,' that is, exists everywhere."
"From whatever water [it comes], that which is more delicious than sweet—curds, clarified butter, milk, and so forth, produced by itself—Indra placed all this within the cow for the sake of food;
therefore, the cow wanders bearing milk and such things. This is the connection with what precedes.

In the sense of "wrath" (*vakṣaṇāsu*), from the root *vakṣ* meaning "to be angry," [the suffix -ana is applied] by the rule "and in the sense of instrument and locus" (*karaṇādhikaraṇayośca*). At the time of dawn (*uṣaḥkāle*), he arrived from all sides.
2. They understand the state of being to be performed by *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *na*, *bha*, and *sa*.
3. *la*: these are the actions.
4. *ca* and *pha* belong to the root *vivāsayati*.

The suffix *lyuṭ* is used in the sense of an instrument (*karaṇe*). [The word] *lisvaraḥ*. [The word] *pakram*. In the root *pac*, the letter *ṣ* of the past participle suffix (*niṣṭhā*) is changed to *v* by the rule "paco vaḥ. The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*). [The word] *carati*. The root *car* has the sense of moving (*gatyartha*). [The word] *bibhratī*. From the root *ḍubhṛñ* in the sense of supporting and nourishing; it belongs to the *juhotyādi* class. Because of the presence of the marker *ṛt* (indicating the *ugit* designation), the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is applied by the rule "ugitaśca. The initial vowel is acute by the rule "abhyastānāmādiḥ. [The word] *ustriyāyām*. From the root *vas* in the sense of dwelling. The suffix *rak* is added in the sense of a location (*adhikaraṇe*) by the rule beginning with "sphāyitañca. There is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) because it belongs to the *yajādi* group. The absence of the change to *ṣ* (as in *patva*) by the rule "śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca" is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*). The suffix *gha* is added in its own sense (*svārthika*). The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
O Indra, the quivers have become firm; grant aid for the sacrifice to the singer and to his friends.
Let the mortals who are ill-intentioned, evil-doing, armed with bows, and hostile enemies, be struck down.

O Indra, the quivers have been fastened; bestow aid upon the sacrifice for the sake of the singer and his friends. Let the mortals who are ill-disposed, evil-doers, armed with swords, and treacherous enemies, be struck down. 15.

O Indra, be firm and steadfast (*darha dṛḍha bhava*). For there were *yāmakōśāḥ*—those who go upon the path (*yāma*) are the way; their *kōśāḥ* are those who, like sheaths (*kōśa*), cover and obstruct that path, namely the Rākṣasas. You, for the sake of the sacrifice (*yajñāya*), for the sacrificer (*yajñakartre*), for the one who sings praises (*gṛṇate*), and for your friends (*sakhibhyaḥ*) such as sons and others, grant (*śikṣa*) the desired fruit. *Durmayavaḥ*: those who cast down (*minvanti*) evil weapons (*duṣṭamāyudhāni*) are *durmayavaḥ*. *Durevāḥ*: those who go toward evil (*duṣṭaṃ gacchantaḥ*), mortal killers. *Niṣaṅgiṇaḥ*: by the word *niṣaṅga*, a quiver (*iṣudhi*) is designated; they possess these within. Such enemies, foes, and Rākṣasas, endowed with such power, are *hantvāsaḥ*—those to be slain by you. *Darha*: from the roots *raha*, *daha*, *vṛha*, *vṛhi* in the sense of "growth" or "firmness. By transposition (*vyatyayena*), the suffix *śyan* is used; this is the form in the imperative (*loṭ*). It is unaccented (*nisvaraḥ*). *Abhūvan*: from the root *bhū* in the sense of "existence. This is the form in the aorist (*luṅ*). By the rule *gātisthā*, the *sic* suffix is elided. By the rule *bhṛsuvostiṅi*, the *guṇa* substitution is prohibited; then by *bhuvo vugluṅliṭoḥ*, the augment *vuk* is added. It is subject to *nighāta* (enclitic accent). *Śikṣa*: from the root *śikṣa* in the sense of "acquiring knowledge. This root here functions in the sense of "giving. By transposition, the *parasmaipada* (active voice) ending is used. It is subject to *nighāta*. *Durmayavaḥ*: from the root *mī* (to cast down), the *uṇ* suffix is applied according to the rule *kṛvāpājimi*, etc. It takes the accent of the final member of the compound (*kṛduttarapadasvaraḥ*). *Durevāḥ*: from the root *dṛṅ* in the sense of "going. By the rule *iṇsīdbhyāṃ van*, the suffix *van* is applied in the sense of the agent. *Ripavaḥ*: by the rule *rericopadhāyāḥ*, the suffix *up* is applied. The penultimate vowel is shortened. It takes the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvaraḥ*). *Hantvāsaḥ*: from the root *han* in the sense of "injury" or "motion. By the rule *kṛtyārthe tavaikenyantyatvanaḥ*, the suffix *tvan* is applied. Being a *niv* suffix, it is udātta on the first syllable. 3. 1. 3. 3. 10–12. *Atharvaveda* 7.50.3–5. (The text provided corresponds to the commentary on this verse.)
The clamor of the base enemies is heard; strike down those who do not seek refuge.
Shatter their strength, break them with your might, and overcome them! O Maghavan, slay the Rakṣasa and bring him under your control.
A clamor is heard from the nearby enemies; strike them down! Strike their most powerful weapon beneath them and shatter it. Overpower them, slay the demon, O Maghavan, and bring them into subjection.
O Indra, that thunderbolt—emitted by the gods as a roaring sound, being heated, and heard clearly by us from nearby enemies and foes—that most scorching weapon, we direct against these very enemies.

"Having placed [the weapon], say: 'Slay! Kill! The sense is: 'Cause the thunderbolt employed by them to reach those very [enemies]. 'Cut down'—that is, sever—'these enemies from below,' that is, from their very root. Furthermore, 'break apart'—afflict them specifically—and 'overpower'—subdue them. O 'Maghavan Indra,' 'slay'—kill—the 'Rakṣases,' those who create obstacles to ritual acts. Immediately after this, 'conquer'—lead to completion—'this sacrifice. *Śṛṇve*: [The word] has the *nighāta* (anudātta) accent. *Jahi*: from the root *han* meaning 'to injure' or 'to go'; this is the form in the imperative (*loṭ*). *Aśanim*: from the root *aś* meaning 'to pervade'; the suffix *ani* is added according to the rule *aśyavitṛbhyo 'niḥ*; it takes the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*). *Napiṣṭhām*: the suffix *iṣṭha* is added to the word *namra*; it takes the accent of the *nit* suffix (*nitsvara*). *Vṛśca*: from the root *vaśca* meaning 'to cut'; it belongs to the *tudādi* class; there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) according to the rule *prahijyādi*. *Mahasva*: because it begins a new sentence (*vākyabheda*), it does not have the *nighāta* accent. *Randhayasva*: from the root *radh* meaning 'to injure' or 'to accomplish'; in the imperative of the *pyant* form, the augment *num* is inserted according to the rule *radhijabhorantra*; because it begins a new sentence, it does not have the *nighāta* accent."
O Indra, milk out the Rākṣasa root and forth with it; rend his middle and crush what is fresh. How far have you cast the *salalaka*? You have hurled your weapon at the hater of prayer.

Uproot the Rakṣas together with its root, O Indra; cut off its middle, and strike down its tip. How long have you been active? You have cast forth your weapon against the hater of prayer; quench his heat. 17.

O Indra, uproot the race of demons (*rakṣas*) that obstructs our work, along with its very roots. Furthermore, cut through its middle part; strike down its fresh tip. Within that race of demons, drive away the ever-moving demon from whatever distance—*ā* being used here as a limit—however far it may be, even from an indefinite distance. And having done so, hurl against that demon who hates the Brahmins a scorching weapon, a destructive missile. Regarding the meaning stated here, Yāska said: "Uproot the demon along with its root, O Indra. The word *mūla* [root] is derived from *muc* (to release), *mop* (to crush), or *muh* (to delude). Cut through the middle; he pierces the tip. It has come near (*adrāgata*). From how far a distance? *Salalaka* is that which is moving (*sarala*); the etymologists say it means 'sinful' (*pāpaka*), or it may mean 'suffering' (*saruka*) from the root *sṛ* (to move). *Tarpipa* is from *tap* (to heat) or *hiṃs* (to injure). (Nirukta 6.3). Grammatical notes: * *vṛha*: A form of the imperative (*loṭ*) of the root *vṛh* (to uproot). * *śṛṇīhi*: From the root *śṛ* (to injure); in the imperative second person singular (*hau*), the vowel is lengthened by the rule *ī halyaghoḥ*. There is a *nighāta* accent. * *kīvataḥ*: From the interrogative pronoun *kim*, in the sense of "of what measure," the suffix *vatup* is applied by the rule *kimidabhyāṃ vo ghaḥ*. The absence of the *vā* substitute is Vedic (*chāndasa*). By the rule *idaṃ kimorīśkī*, *kim* is replaced by *kī*. * *salalakam*: From the root *sṛ* (to go); the formation is Vedic. * *cakratha*: A form of the perfect (*liṭ*) third person plural of the root *ḍukṛñ* (to do); there is the presence of the *krādi* group. There is a *nighāta* accent. * *tarpipam*: From the root *tap* (to heat); the suffix *usi* is added by the rule *atiparvāpayajitanidhanitapivyo nit*, and it is marked as *nit*. The change of *a* to *i* is Vedic. The accent is on the *nit*. * *hatim*: From the root *han* (to injure or kill); it is an antodātta (accented on the final syllable) due to being included in the list beginning with *uti-yuti-jūti-sāti*. * *asya*: From the root *asu* (to throw); a form of the imperative (*loṭ*).

1. *ta-na-la-ra* are employed [in the word] *aśanim*. 2. *gha-ja-ṇa* are constant (*nitya*) [in the word] *atha*. 3. *ta-sa* [indicate that] "*sahasva*" does not exist. 4. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-ka* [indicate that] "*nayasva*" [is used]. 5. *ma-na* [indicate that] "*vṛśca*" [is used]. 6.
