When that very *dhiṣaṇā* (inspiration) has arisen, may that Indra carry us across from distress—that is, from the heart in the form of sin—just as he would lead us to the further shore; thus do the supplicants dwelling on both sides invoke him.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
"like one going upon a boat."
Just as people dwelling on both banks call out to a man traveling by boat upon rivers and the like, so it is here.
*vivepa*: this is the form of the root *viṣ* (meaning "to pervade") in the perfect tense (*liṭ*) with the suffix *ṇal*;
it bears the accent of the *liṭ*.
*jajāna* is the form of the root *jan* (to be born) in the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*), third person singular (*uttama puruṣa*) with the suffix *ṇal*.
Due to the difference in syntactical construction (*vākya-bheda*), there is no loss of accent (*anighāta*).
Regarding *aṃhas*:
[the root] *am* is used in the sense of "going" and so forth.
By the rule *bhamerdhuk ca* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.652), the suffix *asun* is applied and the augment *huk* is added.
*Nisvaraḥ*.

[The form] *pīparat* is derived from the root *pṛ*, meaning "to protect" and "to fill," in the *luṅ* (aorist) tense with the *caṅ* suffix; [the resulting forms] are *hrasva* (short vowel), reduplication (*abhyāsa*), *itva* (change to *i*), shortening (*hrasva*), and *guṇa*.
According to the appropriate application, there is no elision; it has the *li*-accent; as in "nāu-iva".
From the root *ju* in the sense of "impelling," the suffix *ḍau* is applied according to the rule *glānudibhyāṃ ḍauḥ* (Uṇādi Sūtra 2.222).
That which moves (*nau*) is a boat (*nauḥ*), meaning a float.
By the rule *sāvekācaḥ*, the third case ending receives the udātta accent.
There is an obligatory compound with *ivena*, elision of the case-ending, and so forth.
In the word *ubhaye*: after the word *ubha*, the suffix *tayap* undergoes the substitution of *ayac* by the rule *ubhādādattau nityam* (Pāṇini 5.2.44).
By the force of the statement, the initial [syllable] is acute.
*havante* is the form of the root *hve* in the present tense (*laṭ*).
At the midday pressing (*mādhyandina-savana*), "āpūrṇo asya" is the fixed *yājyā* for the Āgnīdhra cup;
and it is stated [in the ritual manuals]: "The midday [offering] is with the formula: 'āpūrṇo asya kalaśaḥ svāhā'" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 5.5).
1. In the manuscripts kha, ga, gha, ca, ja, ṇa, ta, na, pha, bha, and sa, the word "stotraiḥ" is absent.
2. In manuscript ta, it reads "indram".
3. In the manuscripts kha, ga, gha, ca, ja, ṇa, bha, and la, the word "āhvayanti" is absent.
4. He states the example:
5. For instance, those seeking wealth who dwell on both banks of a river as it flows along;
6. In the versions marked *kha*, *ga*, *ba*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, and *la*, there is no "nityasamāsa" (invariable compound).
7. After the words *kha*, *ga*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *bha*, *la*, and *sa* when they occur in both [the first and second] positions, [the following vowel is pluta]:
"Filled is his jar, svāhā! Like a stream, he has poured it into the vessel for him to drink;
the dear Soma-drops have turned toward Indra for exhilaration, moving in a clockwise direction."

15 | Full is his jar; Svāhā! Like a pourer [into] a treasury, he has poured it out for drinking. Together, the dear ones have turned toward him for exhilaration; the Soma juices, moving clockwise, have flowed toward Indra. 15.

O Indra, for the sake of your drinking, this jar—the *droṇakalaśa*—is filled with Soma. Hail! This jar, accompanied by Soma, has been consecrated with the cry of *svāhā*, offered, and poured out for your drinking. I shall pour that Soma into the directed receptacle.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
"like one who sprinkles from a bucket.
Just as a sprinkler, a person who pours water, pours from a bucket full of water—that is, from a vessel—into another water-vessel, so it is here.
The Soma juices are dear and most sweet; these Somas, O Indra, have been given to you. You [are] Indra.

The root *gāṣ* is used in the senses of standing firm (*pratiṣṭhā*) and desiring (*lipsā*), as well as in the sense of a book (*grantha*). From this root, the suffix *īran* is added. The letter *dh* is replaced by *bh*, and the vowel *ā* is shortened; thus, by the rule *gambhīra-gambhīrī* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.475), the form *gambhīra* is derived as an irregularity (*nipātyate*). *Cisvaraḥ* means "flowing. *Sindhuḥ*: from the root *syand* in the sense of flowing (*prastravaṇe*). By the rule *syandeḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ caśca*, the suffix *u* is added, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*), and the letter *d* is replaced by *bh*. Because the term *nit* is understood to carry over [from previous rules], it is accented on the first syllable (*ādyudāttaḥ*). *Paripantaḥ*, *mantaḥ*: these are forms of the root *ag* with the suffix *śatṛ*. By the rule *upasargaprādurbhyāṃ mannijvacparaḥ*, they receive the designation of a *pada*. Some others maintain that there must be a connection with an action (*kriyānvayam*); in that case, the word-form would be untenable. *Pari*: a particle (*nipāta*), hence its accent. *Santaḥ*: the accent of the suffix. *Varanta*: from the root *vṛñ* in the sense of choosing (*varaṇe*); it belongs to the *bhvādi* class; this is the form in the *laṅ* tense. *Nidhānaḥ*, *arujaḥ*: this is the form of the root *raj* in the sense of breaking (*bhaṅge*) in the *laṅ* tense. *Gavyam*: in the sense of a modification of a cow (*gorvikāraḥ*), the suffix *yat* is applied by the rule *gopayamoryan*. By the rule *yano'nāva*, it has the accent on the first syllable.
May we invoke for our good fortune.

From the vicinity of the mountains, the hills, and the crags, they have emerged and are eager to go to the ocean. Their departure is illustrated by the example: "like two mares" (*aśveva*), as if released from their stalls, neighing and competing with each other's speed; or rather, like two mares (*vaḍave*) going swiftly, each desiring the other. Likewise, "like two cows" (*gāveva*); just as two cows exist in a beautiful state, so too are these two "beautiful ones" (*śubhre*), shining brightly. Furthermore, "like two mothers" (*mātarā*); just as two mother-cows lick [their calves], the root *lih* here has a hidden secondary meaning: desiring to lick the moisture with their tongues, they go swiftly to reach that ocean, joined with water. Regarding the names: *Vipāṭ* is so called because of "cleaving the banks" (*kūla-vipāṭanāt*), or "untying" (*vipāśanāt*), or "liberating" (*vimocanāt*). *Sutudrī* means "she who flows swiftly" (*su-kṣipram-tu-drī*); she runs or flows quickly, hence *Sutudrī*. These two rivers named thus flow rapidly toward the ocean. On this point, the *Nirukta* says: "From the vicinity of the mountains, being seen and longing, like two mares released, or 'released' (*vipaṇe*)—meaning competing with one another—or longing; or like two beautiful cows, shining, two mothers licking, the Vipāṭ and Sutudrī flow forth with water" (*Nirukta* 9.39). Grammatical notes: *uśatī*—from the root *vaś* (desire), with the suffix *śatṛ*, followed by the feminine suffix *ṅīp*; there is vocalization (*prasāraṇa*) according to rules such as *abhyastānām ādiḥ*. *Vipite*—from the root *piñ* (binding), in the passive past participle (*niṣṭhā*); in the *saṃhitā* stage, *patva* occurs according to rules such as *parinivibhyaḥ sevasitasayasusah*. By the rule *gatiranantaraḥ*, the preceding prefix retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*). *Hāsamāne*—the root *hāsmati* means to compete, or *has* means to laugh; the suffix is *śānac*. When the accent of the *lasārvadhātuka* suffix is applied, the accent of the root remains. *Rihāṇe*—from *lih* (to taste); since it is *svarita*-accented, it is both-paradigmatic (*ubhayapadī*). The suffix is *śānac*. Due to belonging to the *adādi* class, there is elision of the *śap* suffix. The *repha* for the *lakāra* is Vedic. The *ṇatva* is due to the presence of *repha*. It is oxytone (*antodātta*) because of the *cit* suffix. *Vipāṭ*—from *paṭ* (to go) or *paś* (to strike/afflict); with the causative suffix (*ṇic*) and the suffix *enau*, the form *viprau* arises; the *śakāra* becomes *pakāra* by the rule *vaśrādi*. *Sutudrī*—the formation of the form is Vedic. *Javete*—from *jṛ* (to go); it belongs to the *juhotyādi* class. Because of the *ḍit* suffix, it is *ātmanepada*. By the rule *āto ḍitaḥ*, there is the substitution of *iy*. There is *nighāta* (suppression of accent).

Sent by Indra, begging for a flow, you two go toward the ocean like two chariot-drivers. Meeting together, swelling with your waves, O radiant ones, one of you follows after the other. *Indraiṣite* (sent by Indra); *prasravam* (a flow); *bhikṣamāṇe* (begging); *acchā* (toward); *samudram* (the ocean); *rathyeva* (like two chariot-drivers); *yāthaḥ* (you two go); *samārāṇe* (meeting together); *ūrmibhiḥ* (with waves); *pinvamāne* (swelling); *anyā* (one); *vām* (of you two); *anyām* (the other); *api* (also); *eti* (goes); *śubhre* (O radiant ones).
O two rivers, impelled by Indra, sent forth by Indra, seeking and requesting that flow as a boon from Indra, you two go toward the ocean;
there is an illustration for this:
"like two chariot-horses."

Just as two chariot-warriors approach their target destination, so did they; what were they doing? Meeting one another (*samārāṇe*), swelling with waves (*ūrmibhiḥ*) and surging toward the surrounding region (*parisarapradeśaṃ saṃtarpayantyau*), and shining brightly (*śubhre*).
The syntactical connection with the preceding verse is: "You two go to the ocean.
Likewise, between you two, one goes toward the other river; that is, she merges with the other.
The meaning is that they attain mutual unity.
In *indraiṣite*,
[the suffix] is the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*) of the root *iṣ* meaning "to go," with the augment *iṭ* added according to the rule beginning with *nīpamaha*.

1. In the *ta* recension, the word *girīṇām* does not exist. 2. In the *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *pa*, *pha*, and *bha* recensions, it is *vipāṭchutūdrī uśatī*; in the *dha*, *ja*, and *ṇa* recensions, it is *vipāṭchutūdrī uśatī*. 3. In the *ta* recension, [the words] are "mutually with speed" (*anyonyam javena*). 4. In the *ja* and *ṇa* recensions, the two words *hyanyanyau* do not exist. 5. In the *kha*, *ga*, *pra*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *pa*, *pha*, and *bha* recensions, [the phrase] is "they hasten to go" (*gantum prajavete*). 6. In the *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, and *bha* recensions, it is *śu*; in the *ta* recension, it is *tujñā*. 7. In the *ta* recension, [it refers to] those having this name (*etannāmike*). 8. In the *ja* and *ṇa* recensions, [it is] "the edge of the ocean" (*samudraprāntam*). 9. In the *la* recension, [it is] "of this" (*ityasya*). 10. In the *ta* recension, [there is] "vowel-ness" (*svaratvam*). 11. In the *kha*, *ga*, *ja*, and *ṇa* recensions, it is *spaśa*. 12. In the *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, and *bha* recensions, the word "thus" (*iti*) does not exist. 13. In the *ta* recension, [it occurs] in the sense of the past passive participle (*niṣṭhāyām*).

In the word *prasavam*, the accent of the first member is determined by the rule *tṛtīyā karmaṇi*. [The root] *pra-sū* is derived from *pū* in the sense of "impelling" (*preraṇe*) with the suffix *ap*; it takes the accent of the *thā-thādi* group. In *bhikṣamāṇe*: the root *bhikṣ* is used in the sense of "begging" (*yācñāyām*) and is conjugated in the Ātmanepada. Since the suffix *śānac* is unaccented by the general rule for *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes, the accent of the verbal root remains. In *ryeva* and *rathyyamau*: the suffix *yat* is applied in the sense of "belonging to this" (*tasyedam*) according to the rule *rathādyat*. The *ti* is elided; [the compound is formed] with *iva* without the elision of the case-ending, and so forth. In *yādhaḥ*: this is the form of the root *yā* in the *leṭ* mood. In *samārāne*: this is the *liṭ* (perfect) of the root *ṛ* meaning "to go. Because the root *ā* preceded by *sam-* takes the Ātmanepada according to the rule *samo gamiḥ* etc., the suffix *kānac* is substituted for it. The *guṇa* substitution occurs according to the rule *ṛcchahṛtām*. In *pivvamāne*: the root *piv* is used in the sense of "drinking" (*mecane*) and belongs to the *bhūvādi* class. Since the suffix *śānac* is unaccented by the rule for *lasārvadhātuka* accents, the accent of the verbal root remains. 3.
I have come to the Sindhu, the most excellent mother, to the Vipāś, the broad and auspicious;
they lick each other like two mother cows, moving together toward their common source.
To the Acchā, to the Sindhu most motherly, to the Āyāsī, to the Vipāś, to the broad [Urū]. (Atharva Veda 3.3.33) Third Book, 349.

The plural number for *dyoḥ* (of heaven) is used for honorific purposes. Of those [heavens], for us, the impulse toward birth—that is, the effort directed toward going forth into creation—cannot be turned back; it does not cease. Desiring what? Seeking what? This wise one (*vipra*), this Brāhmaṇa, calls out repeatedly to us, the rivers (*nadyaḥ*). *Enā*: For the word *etad*, the third-case form is replaced by *enā*. By the rule *supāṃ suluk...* there is the substitution of *ā* for the third case ending. By the rule *aḍidam...*, the case-ending receives the udātta accent. *pivamānāḥ*: From the root *piv* (to moisten). *devakṛtam*: By the rule *tṛtīyā karmaṇi*, the original accent of the first member of the compound is retained. *vartave*: From the root *vṛt* (to turn). The suffix *taven* is added in the sense of the infinitive (*tumun*). It has the *ni*-accent. *sargatakaḥ*: By the rule *ke ca*, the original accent of the first member is retained. *kiṃyuḥ*: "Desiring what? By the rule *kvaci māntāvyayapratiṣedhaḥ*, because this is Vedic usage, the prohibition against adding *kvac* after a word ending in *m* or an indeclinable does not apply; thus *kvac* is applied. By the rule *kyācchandasi*, the suffix *ap* is added. It has the accent of the suffix. *nadyaḥ*: A Vedic substitution of *yaṇ* occurs. *johavīti*: From the root *hu* with the intensive (*yaṅ*) affix elided (*yaṅluk*). When the samprasāraṇa is performed, by the rule *guṇo yaṅlukoḥ*, the reduplicated syllable receives the guṇa vowel. By the rule *yaṅo vā*, the augment *iṭ* is added. Then the guṇa is applied. It is accented as *nicāt* (by the general rule for intensives).
Delight yourselves for my glorious, Soma-like splendor, O observers of Truth, for a moment with your movements!
Toward the river, the daughter of Kuśika, the son of Avatsāra, has sent forth a lofty hymn of wisdom.

Rejoice for my glory, O you who are worthy of Soma, O observers of the Eternal Law! For a moment, come hither with your swift movements toward the river. With a lofty hymn, the son of Kuśika, seeking aid, has called out to you. 5.
The rivers respond to Viśvāmitra: "O you who possess the *ṛta*— that is, water— for that purpose,
O rivers, you are for me, Viśvāmitra, for my sake, as one worthy of the *soma*."
"Having crossed over, I shall prepare the Soma"—thinking thus, [he spoke] to Varcas, the preparer of the Soma, for that very purpose.
The instrumental case is used in the sense of the ablative;
[it means] "from those who travel swiftly," [saying] "cease for a moment, for just a muhūrta."
The prefix *upa* is used here in the sense of "stopping.
"Cease for a moment" means desist from moving swiftly.
Speaking generally to his daughter standing before him—who, like other rivers being filled by the flood, was not yet accomplishing her desired purpose—he says:

I, Viśvāmitra, the son of the royal seer Kuśika, desiring protection for myself—that is, seeking my own preservation—with great and lofty wisdom (*manīṣā*), through praise, call out toward you, O Sindhu Sutudrī, with intensity.

Regarding this, the *Nirukta* states: "Come near to me for splendor that is worthy of Soma; O you who produce Soma, you who possess the cosmic order (*ṛtāvarīḥ*), for *ṛta* is a name for water; indeed, you have come forth for a moment by means of swift movements, whether old or new."
"I impel the Sindhu with a lofty, great inspired thought—with the impulse of the mind, with praise, or with wisdom—for the sake of winning over [the river], O son of Kuśika.
"Kuśika was a king" (Nirukta 2.25).
"Rejoice!
[The root] *ras* means "to cease.

The Ātmanepada ending is applied because of the rule "vibhāṣākarmakān" (Pāṇini Sūtra 1.3.85), which states that after roots preceded by the prefix *upa*, the Ātmanepada is optionally used when they are intransitive.
*Ṛtāvarī*:
[The suffix] *vanip* is applied after the word *ṛta* in the sense of "possessing" (*matvartha*) according to the rule "in Vedic [language], *vanip* [is used]";

then, by the rule "after [a stem ending in] *van*, there is *ṅīp* and the substitution of *ra* for the final [consonant]," the feminine suffix *ṅīp* and the replacement of the final consonant with *ra* are applied.

In the Vedic language (*chandasi*), there is a long vowel by rule of *savarṇadīrgha*. Because the vocative (*āmantrita*) begins the quarter-verse (*pāda*), it bears the acute accent (*udātta*) on its first syllable according to Pāṇini 6.1.198.
[The word] *evaiḥ*.
The root *iṇ* means "to go.
[The suffix] *van* is applied after the roots *iṇ* and *śī*.
There is *guṇa* substitution according to the rules for *ārddhadhātuka* suffixes.
Nisvara:
*bṛhatī manīṣā*.
In both cases, there is a long vowel resulting from the substitution of the preceding sound for the third case ending.
*Avasyu*: desiring protection (*ava*). [The suffix] *kyac* is applied after a word ending in a case-suffix to express a desire for oneself.

No; because the designation *pada* has been restricted to words ending in the letter *n*, the substitution of *ru* for the *s* in *ana* does not occur. [The suffix] *ap* is added by the rule "kyācchandasi. [Thus: *ahe*.
In the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, after the root *hā*, the substitute *iyaṅ* optionally occurs for the *sic* suffix in the *ātmanepada*;
[then] *guṇa* [is applied];
[and finally, by the rule] *nicca taḥ*, [the augment *iṭ* is inserted].

1. For the turning of *kha*, *ga*, *gha*, *ca*, *ja*, *pa*, *pha*, and *bha*; for the present state of *ṇa*; for the ceasing of *na*; for the present state of *sa*. 2. *Ca* [is used] for the word *idam* (this). 3. *Ga*, *ca*, *na*, and *bha* [are used] in the sense of service (*sevane*); *ja* and *ṇa* in the sense of pleasing (*prīṇane*). 4. *La* [is used] in the sense of abandoning (*haya*). 5. And *ta* [is used] in a general sense.
Indra, whose arm wields the thunderbolt, dug out for him the channel of the rivers.
The god Savitṛ, the fair-handed, led them forth; by his impulse we go along the broad expanses.

Indra, whose arm wields the thunderbolt, has dug us out; he struck down Vṛtra, the dam of the rivers. The god Savitṛ, the fair-handed, has led [us] forth; at his impulsion, we go toward the wide expanses. 6.

The rivers replied: "O Viśvāmitra, Indra, whose arm is armed with the thunderbolt (*vajrabāhuḥ*)—that is, he whose arm is joined with the *vajra*—that powerful Indra dug us out. The root *radati* means 'to dig,' [thus] he excavated. How did he dig? It is said: having made a barrier (*paridhim*) of the waters—that is, having placed water all around, meaning that which exists within—the [water] of the rivers; [he dug] such a *vṛtra*. *Vṛtra* is the cloud, so called because it covers (*vṛṇoti*) the sky. He struck down (*apāhan*) that cloud; when it was slain, the waters fell. Because they were not reaching the navel, a hollow was dug out. Thus he excavated by way of slaying the cloud. Not only did he dig, but furthermore: Savitṛ, the impeller of the entire world, the fair-handed (*supāṇiḥ*) one—fair-handed because he is the agent of its production and maintenance—the shining (*devaḥ*) god Indra led us. Having split the cloud, by impelling the water, he filled the ocean. By his such power, at the impulse (*pramave*)—that is, under the authorization—of this Indra, we, the wide ones (*urvīḥ*), abundant with water, go; we proceed. We do not stop there merely because of the word. Regarding the stated meaning, Yāska says: "'Indra dug us out, O you whose arm is armed with the thunderbolt. The root *radati* has the sense of digging. 'He struck down the barrier of the rivers'—this is the explanation. 'The god led us, Savitṛ, the fair-handed'—one with beautiful hands. 'Hand' (*pāṇi*) comes from the root *daṇ*, meaning 'to honor'; having taken the hand, people honor the gods. At his impulse (*prasave*), we go, the wide ones. (Nirukta 5.26) Grammatical notes: * *aradat*: Form of the root *rad* in the *laṅ* (imperfect). * *vajrabāhuḥ*: In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the accent falls on the first member. * *ahan*: Form of the root *han* in the *laṅ*; subject to *nighāta* (elision of accent). * *paridhim*: From the root *ḍudhāñ* (to hold/nourish); with the prefix *pari* and in the object case, the suffix *ki* is applied according to Pāṇini 3.3.92 (*ghoḥ kiḥ*). There is elision of the *ā* of *dhā*. The accent falls on the second member due to the *kṛd*-suffix. * *anayan*: Form of the root *nī* in the *laṅ*. * *supāṇiḥ*: From the root *daṇ* (to transact/to praise); the suffix *in* is added according to Uṇādi-sūtra 4.572 (*aśipaṇākhyo ruḍāyalukī ca*), resulting in *āyaluk*. In the *bahuvrīhi*, the accent follows Pāṇini 6.2.172 (*nasubhyām*). * *prasave*: From the root *pū* (to impel); the suffix *ap* is added in the sense of an abstract noun (*bhāva*) according to Pāṇini 3.3.57 (*ṛdorap*). The final syllable of the second member is accented according to Pāṇini 6.2.144 (*thāthaghantā*). * *yāmaḥ*: Form of the root *yā* (to go) in the present tense (*laṭ*); subject to *nighāta*. * *urvīḥ*: From the word *uru*; the suffix *ṅīp* is added according to Pāṇini 4.1.44 (*voto guṇavacanāt*). In the Vedic language (*chandasi*), there is a long vowel by Pāṇini 6.1.107 (*vā chandasi*). The accent falls on the suffix.
That heroic deed of Indra is to be proclaimed forever: how he tore asunder the dragon;
how with his thunderbolt he struck down the one who sat encompassing [the waters], while the waters went forth seeking their course.

It is to be proclaimed forever: that heroic deed of Indra, when he tore apart the dragon; with his thunderbolt, he struck down those who sat around him. The waters flowed on, seeking their course. || 7 ||

This deed of Indra’s—namely, that he struck the serpent (ahi), the cloud, in order to impel the waters—which consisted of the act of cleaving—that very heroic power and capacity of that Indra is to be proclaimed preeminently at all times (śaśvadhā).
Likewise, that Indra struck down with his thunderbolt (vajra) the *pariṣadaḥ*, the Asuras who sat around as obstructors.
Now, the word *ayana* means a place or station.

1. [The suffix] *u* is applied in the sense already stated after the roots *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *na*, and *ma*. 2. Regarding *la*: this refers to the fact that the final syllable of the subsequent member (*uttarapada*) is udātta; it is a single-substitute accent (*ekādeśasvara*). 3. Regarding *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *pha*, *bha*: these are to be recited [as such]. 4. Those who sit around are *pariṣadaḥ*; [it means] those sitting all around (*parita āsīnān*).

*icchantyaḥ* means "desiring. *āpaḥ* means "they went" (*āyan*). [Regarding the word] *pravācyam*: from the root *vac* in the sense of "speaking," the suffix *ṇyat* is applied according to Pāṇini 3.1.124 (*ṛhalorṇyat*). There is Vṛddhi of the initial vowel and the penultimate vowel (*giravādyupadhāvṛddhiḥ*). By Pāṇini 7.3.67 (*vaco'śabdasaṃjñāyām*), there is an absence of *kutva*. The acute accent on the first syllable occurs by metrical transposition (*vyatyayena*). Alternatively, it is derived as *vācyate* with the suffix *yat* according to Pāṇini 3.1.97 (*aco yat*). The accent is governed by Pāṇini 6.1.213 (*yato'nāvaḥ*). *śaśvadha*: after the word *śaśvat*, the suffix *dhā* is seen in the sense of the same meaning (*svārthe*), along with the elision of the letter *t*. *vivṛścata*: from the root *vaśca* in the sense of "cutting," belonging to the *tudādi* class. In the *laṅ* tense, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) according to Pāṇini 6.1.16 (*grahijyāvayi...*). The compound is formed by splitting the rule *saha supā* (Pāṇini 2.1.4) into two separate rules (*yogavibhāga*). The accent is that of the compound. *pariṣadaḥ*: [formed with] the suffix *kvip*. In *saṃhitā*, it becomes *pada* form according to Pāṇini 8.3.108 (*sadiprateḥ*). *jaghāna*: this is the form of the root *han* in the *liṭ* tense with the suffix *ṇal*. It receives the *nighāta* (elision of accent). *āyan*: this is the form of the root *aya* in the sense of "going" in the *laṅ* tense. Because it begins a quarter-verse (*pāda*), it does not receive *nighāta*. *icchamānāḥ*: from the root *iṣu* in the sense of "desiring," the suffix *śānac* is applied by metrical transposition (*vyatyayena*). When the accent of the *lasārvadhātuka* is applied, the accent of the suffix remains.
This is the splendor for you, O singer, through our inspired hymns; may it reach you as the later ages resound.
O maker of songs, take pleasure in our praises; do not abandon us in many places—salutations to you!
This is your splendor, O singer; do not wipe it away! When future generations raise their voices for you, O poet, be pleased with our hymns; do not cast us down in many places—homage be to you! 8.
In the course of the narrative, having composed a hymn of praise to Indra, they spoke to Viśvāmitra:

"O singer, O Viśvāmitra, you who are worthy of praise, do not forget—that is, do not allow it to be lost—that speech consisting of our dialogue which you have uttered for us while proclaiming aloud; do not let that speech vanish.
For what reason?

"O you who are the maker of the *kāra* (the call) for the *uktha* hymns during the later sacrificial sessions—the later ages, the days, and the recitations—be pleased with us; through that speech consisting of dialogue, favor us.
Now, do not make us among men subject to the *ni-kaḥ* (shame);
do not make us bold enough to utter words of dialogue in a manner that is excessively forward."
"Salutation to you."
*mṛṣṭhāḥ*:

This is the *laṅ* (imperfect) of the root *mṛjūṣ* in the sense of "purification"; the *ātmanepada* ending occurs by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*), and there is elision of the *śap* suffix because the root belongs to the *adādi* class.
The word *vaśrādinā* has a *padapāṭha* [reading];
it is unaccented (*nighāta*);
[the word] *ghoṣān*.

In the case of the root *ghuṣir* (meaning "to sound") with the suffix *śatṛ*, because all grammatical rules are optional in the Vedic language (*chandas*), the substitution of the single substitute for the preceding and following sounds (*pararūpa*) by the rule *ato guṇe* does not occur.
Instead, there is a long vowel by the rule of homogeneous vowels (*savarṇadīrghaḥ*).
Once the accent of the *śatṛ* suffix—which is part of the *sārvadhātuka* class—is applied, the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) remains.

The word *yugāni* [is derived from] the root *yujir* in the sense of "joining. Due to its being listed among the *ucchādi* group as a form ending in the suffix *ghañ*, there is no *guṇa* substitution.
And it is intended that this be an irregular formation (*nipātana*) with a specific meaning;
because it is read in the rule "in reference to a specific time and in reference to equipment such as a chariot," its final syllable is udātta by virtue of that very reading.
Furthermore, the accusative case ending is applied according to the rule "the accusative is used for duration of time and distance when there is continuous connection."
*Kāraḥ* [is derived] from the root *kṛ*.
By the rule beginning with "kṛ-vā-pā-jim," the suffix *uṇ* is applied.
There is the elision of the suffix due to its being an *āmantrita* (vocative).
Which [suffix]? It is the *cli* of the root *kṛ* in the *liṅ* mood, which is elided by the rule "In mantras, [the *cli*] of *ghas*, etc. (*mantre ghasa*).
By *halyādinā*, there is the elision (*lopa*) of the suffix *sic*. By the rule *na mādyoge*, there is the absence of the augment *aṭ*.
[The form is] *purutrā*.
According to the rule *devamanuṣyapuruṣapurumartyebhyo dvitīyāsamyogyarbahulām*, the suffix *trā* is applied in the sense of the seventh case (*saptamī*).
It bears the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
1. [The reading] "na-la-sa-sadeprateḥ" [is adopted]. 2. [The phrase] "having composed a hymn to Indra because of the lack of occasion" does not exist in manuscript *pa*.
3. [The manuscripts] kha, ga, ca, ja, ṇa, pa, pha, and bha read: "proclaiming such sounds as 'tvaṃ manīṣā'"; [manuscript *pa* reads "ityāghoṣān"].
4. In the manuscripts Kha, Ga, Ca, Pha, and Kuśika, [the reading is as above]; in Ja and Ṇa, "in the sacrifices" (yājñikeṣu) is not present.
5. In Na, "in the sacrifices" (yāgeṣu); in Sa, "in the conjunctions" (yogeṣu). 6.
In Kha, Ga, Ca, Ja, and Ṇa, [the reading is] "of the treatises" (śāstrāṇām).
7. [The suffix *u* is applied] after *kha*, *pha*, *bha*, and *mṛj*.
8. [The suffix *up* is applied] after *kha*, *ga*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, *la*, *sa*, and *ghu*. 9. [The suffix *viśabda* is applied] in the sense of "calling out."
10. [The rule] has as its specific domain *kha*, *ga*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, *la*, and *sa*.
11. In the case of *acaleḥ*, *ca* is not present; [the letters are] *kha*, *ga*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, and *sa*.

O sisters, listen well to the singer; he has come to you from afar with a wagon and a chariot. Bow down low for him; become easy to cross, O rivers, with your downward-flowing currents, you whose axles are below. o | su | svasāraḥ | kārave | śṛṇota | yayau | vaḥ | durāt | anasā | rathena | ni | su | namadhvam | bhavata | supārāḥ | adho'akṣāḥ | sindhavaḥ | srotayābhiḥ || 9 ||
Viśvāmitra replied to the rivers:
"O sisters, O sisters, O Sindhus—O rivers!—listen well, as it were, to my words, for me who am performing a hymn of praise (*kāru*).
With a wagon (*anasa*) and with a chariot (*ratha*), I have come from afar, from a great distance, unto you."

Bow down well and thoroughly; become yourselves easily fordable. Likewise, be easy to cross over; and so that there may be easy ascending and descending from the banks for chariots and other vehicles, be possessed of beautiful shores.

Furthermore, the intended meaning is: "Moreover, you [should be] such that you possess water flowing with streams—that is, flowing by nature—'under the axle,' meaning beneath the axle of the chariot; for only then can the chariot and other vehicles be led.
Therefore, the sense is: 'May you be possessed of water of that measure.'"
The syllable *o* is designated as a *pragṛhya*.
[In the word] *śṛṇota*,
the suffix *ta* of the root *śru* (meaning "to hear") in the imperative (*loṭ*) is replaced by *tām* according to the rule *tasantasanathanāśca*.
By virtue of being a *pit* (a verbal root ending in *i*), there is *guṇa*.
There is *nighāta* (elision of accent).
He went (*yayau*).

In the case of the root *yā* (meaning "to go" or "to reach") in the perfect tense (*liṭ*), third person singular (*uttama-puruṣa-ekavacana*) with the suffix *ṇal*, the vowel *au* is substituted by the rule *āta au ṇalaḥ*.
This results in a single-substitute accent (*ekādeśasvara*).
[The form is] *yau*. *Vaḥ*.
For the second case plural of the word *yuṣmad*, the substitute *vas* is applied according to the rule "for the plural [of the second case], *vas* and *nas*"; thus, *yū*.
By the rule "of a particle," there is a long vowel in the *saṃhitā*.

"Namadhvam. Regarding the root *ṇam*, which [is listed] under the meanings "bowing" and "sound," there is an absence of the *ya*-suffix when it functions as a reflexive object (*karmakartṛ*), because of the prohibition: "The *ya*-suffix and the *ciṇ* suffix are not applied after the roots *duh*, *snus*, and *nam*. [Thus we have: *adho'kṣāḥ*.

Regarding the word *adhara*: by the rule "for *pūrva*, *adhara*, and *avara*, there is the suffix *asi* and the substitution of *adha*" (*pūrvādharāvāṇāmasi puradhravaścaiṣām*), the suffix *asi* is applied and *adha* is substituted for *adhara*.

Regarding the word *akṣa*: from the root *aś* in the sense of pervasion (*vyāpti*), it is formed with the suffix *sa* according to the rule "from *aś* etc., with *devan*" (*aśerdevene*; Uṇādisūtra 3.345).
It bears the original accent of the final member of the compound (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara*).
The rivers (*sindhavaḥ*): they have the *nighāta* accent because they are vocatives. With the flowing streams (*srotayābhiḥ*).
From the word *srotas*, the suffix *dyat* is applied according to Pāṇini’s rule 4.4.113, *srotaso vibhāṣā dyaḍdyau*.
Due to the indicatory letter *ḍ*, there is elision of the final syllable (*ṭilopa*). The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).

In the sound of your chariot, we would hear your words, as you come from afar with your wagon and your chariot. We would gaze upon you as a swelling woman gazes at her lover, or as a maiden gazes at a young man; may you always be ours. 10.
The rivers, having previously rejected Viśvāmitra, now heeded his words:
"O Kāru, as you perform this hymn of praise, we hear these words of yours, O Viśvāmitra;
that is, we shall carry out your desired purpose."
"O Anamā, you have come from afar with the wagon and the chariot;
we have lowered our naves for your sake."
The singular number here is used because each [of them] is intended to be addressed individually.
The meaning is: "Become those whose waters are shallow enough to cross by chariot.

1. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-na-pha-bha-sa*: Listen well, indeed listen very well. 2. *ja-ṇa*: Become humble. 3. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-na-la*: Those whose waters are limited in measure. 4. *gha-la*: The intention. 5. *ta-mu*. 6. *la-sa*: The speech of Viśvāmitra. 7. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-bha-la*: The word "tava" (of you) is not present. 8. *kha-ga-ca-bha*: We have heard; *ja-ṇa*: we have heard. 9. *ja-ṇa-la*: Because of the desire to express each one individually.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
"Like a swelling woman.
Just as a woman—a mother—swelling with milk becomes humble while suckling her breast to her son.
Another illustration:
Just as a young maiden, for the sake of her father or her brother, constantly bows down to embrace a human youth, so too do you bow down for their sake.
The repetition of the word "te" (for them) is for the purpose of showing respect.

Regarding this verse, Yāska explains it as follows: “‘We would hear your words, O Kāru; come with your chariot that is difficult to restrain. We bend down for you, like a woman nursing her son, or like a maiden embracing a man—‘we bend down,’ so [it says]. (Nirukta 2.27). Here, *kāro* is the vocative. According to Pāṇini’s rule, “In the vocative, according to Śākalya, *it* [is pragṛhya]” (Pā. Sū. 1.1.16), it bears the technical designation *pragṛhya*. [The word is] *śṛṇavāma*.

From the root *śru* in the sense of "hearing," in the imperative (*loṭ*), there is the augment *āṭ* by the rule *āḍuttamasya piñca*; because of its being marked with *p*, there is *guṇa* substitution;
[and finally] there is *nighāta* (elision of accent).
In *yayātha*:

regarding the root *yā* in the sense of "to go," when the *liṭ* suffix *thal* occurs in the simple past (*bhūta-mātra*), there is a prohibition of the *it*-augment by the rule *ekāca upadeśe'nudāttāt*; thus, the accent is that of the *lit* suffix.
By this [word], the third case is used in the sense of accompaniment (sahārthe).
[The form] is *naṃsai*.

In the word *namu*, derived from the root *ṇam* in the sense of "bowing" (*prahvatve*), the suffix *sip* is applied according to the rule *leṭi sibbahulam*. By the rule *vaito'nyatra*, the substitution of the vowel *ai* occurs. There is also the *nighāta* (elision of accent).
*pīpyāneva*:
This is the form of the root *pīḍ* (meaning "to drink") with an internally contained causative sense (*antarbhāvita-ṇyartha*), in the perfect tense (*liṭ*) with the suffix *kānac*;
it bears the *citsvara* accent.
*Yoṣā*: [derived from] the root *yu* in the sense of "mixing" (*miśraṇe*).
The suffix *map* is applied according to the rule beginning with *vṛtuvadihani* (Uṇādi Sūtra 3.342).
She joins (yauti) is a "yoṣā" (woman);
it is accented on the first syllable because it belongs to the *vṛṣādi* group;
and it is also [accented] by virtue of being feminine (*śaśvat*).
From the root *śvañj* in the sense of "embracing," the suffix *kvip* is applied according to the rule for *saṃpad* and so forth to form the abstract noun;
the specific form is established by its inclusion in the *pṛṣodarādi* group, and it is accented on the final syllable (*antodātta*).

When, O friend, the Bharatas cross over you toward a cattle-rich village, impelled and urged by Indra, may I flow forth, released at the impulse of the sender; I choose for myself the favor of you who are worthy of sacrifice.

When the Bharatas cross over you, O Aṅga, let the troop of cattle, impelled and urged by Indra, flow forth; let me, impelled by the impulse and set in motion, flow toward you. I choose the favor of you who are worthy of sacrifice. 11.
Viśvāmitra replied to the rivers:
“Aṅga” is used as a term of address;

O rivers, since my crossing has been permitted by you for the sake of [my] passage, therefore all my Bharatas—those born of the Bharata lineage—having attained unity with one another, shall cross you, the river, and emerge safely on the other side.
He specifies that very thing:

"Desiring to cross the waters (gavyam), being impelled (iṣitaḥ)—that is, permitted by you—and urged by Indra (indrajūtaḥ)—that is, impelled by your leader Indra—let the host (grāmaḥ), the assembly of the Bharatas (bharatānām saṃghaḥ), flow forth (arṣāt) through the midst.
For their impulse (prasavaḥ)—their exertion for the sake of going—is set in motion (sargataktaḥ). I was previously permitted by you."
I, however, choose from all sides and fully enjoy your auspicious praise—the beautiful hymn of you who are worthy of sacrifice and deserving of worship.
The Bharatas:
from the word *bharata*, by virtue of its belonging to the *uṣmad-ādi* group; for it, there is elision (*luk*) according to the rule *yajajośca*.
And for this reason, the accent belongs to the suffix (*pratyaya-svara*). *Saṃtareyuḥ* is the form of the root *tṛ* in the potential mood (*liṅ*) with the suffix *jhi*.
In the case of affixes (pratyaya) that are not sārvadhātuka and before vowels, the accent of the verbal root (dhātu-svara) prevails.
By the rule "niḍi codāttavati," there is the elision of the accent (nighāta).
[Thus we have] *gavyam*.
Desiring cows for oneself:
*supaḥ kyac* [Pāṇini 3.1.8],
with the accent of the single substitute [ekādeśasvara].

*Grāmaḥ*: [The suffix] *map* and the substitution of the vowel *ā* [for the root vowel] are applied by the rule "from the root *gras*, [the suffix *man* with] *ā*" (Uṇādi Sūtra 1.140). It is devoid of accent (*nissvara*).
*Indrajūtaḥ*: *ji* is a root belonging to the *sautra* class meaning "to go.
According to the rule *ṛ-yuk-kiti*, there is a prohibition of the *it*-augment in the case of the *niṣṭhā* suffix.
By the rule "the third [case-ending] is used in the sense of the object," the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member [of the compound] is maintained.
It is from the root *ṛ*, meaning "to go"; in the *leṭ* mood, with the suffix *tip*, the suffix *sip* is applied according to the rule "the suffix *sip* is frequently used."
The āḍ augment is added in the leṭ [subjunctive] mood. By the rule “ekācaḥ,” there is a prohibition of the *it* augment. Then, *guṇa* substitution occurs.
Because the suffix *pratyaya* is marked with the *pittva* indicatory letter, it is *anudātta*; thus, the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) remains.
*Vṛṇe* is the form of the root *vṛṅ* (meaning "to choose" or "to select") in the present tense (*laṭ*).
Regarding *yajñiyānām*: the suffix *gha* is applied by the rule “*yajñi-vābhyāṃ ghañ-au*”; it bears the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).

1. In the manuscripts kha, ga, ca, ja, ṇa, na, bha, and sa, the word *vā* does not exist. 2. In the manuscripts kha and ga, *tadvat te* does not exist; in ca, ja, and ṇa, it is *te*; in la, it is *tadvat*. 3. In the manuscripts kha, ga, ca, ja, ṇa, and na, it is *prahībhāvam*. 4. In the manuscripts kha, ga, ca, ja, na, pha, and bha, the phrase *te... iti* does not exist. 5. In the manuscript na, it is *vṛttvadihani*. 6. In the manuscript ta, it is *samābhaje*. 7. In the manuscripts kha, ga, ca, ja, ṇa, na, bha, and ma, there is the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*) here. 8. In the manuscript la, the augment *āṭ* is applied according to the rule *leṭo'ḍāyau* (Pāṇini 3.4.94). (ṚV 3.45)

The Bharatas, seeking cattle, have crossed over; the sage has shared in the favor of the rivers. Flow forth, you who provide nourishment and great wealth; fill your bellies and go toward the dry land. 12. They have crossed over; the Bharatas; seeking cattle; together; he has shared; the sage; the favor; of the rivers; flow forth; providing nourishment; O you of great wealth; fill; your bellies; go; to the dry land. 12.

Desiring cattle for themselves, the Bharatas—those born of the Bharata lineage—all crossed over; they traversed that river. The wise sage Viśvāmitra bestowed his excellent praise (*sumati*) upon the rivers. But you, flowing as before through the channels of irrigation, being thus rich in wealth (*surādhāḥ*), do you swell forth (*prapinvadhvam*) the *vakṣaṇās*—the artificial streams or canals—and fill them completely on all sides (*āpṛṇadhvam*). Go quickly (*śīrdham*)! *Atāriṣuḥ*: From the root *tṛ* (to float/cross) in the *luṅ* tense, with the augment *sic*, there is the *vṛddhi* strengthening according to the rule "there is *vṛddhi* in the *parasmaipada* endings after *sic*. The accent belongs to the augment *aṭ*. *Gavyavaḥ*: From the noun *go* (cow), the suffix *kyac* is added. In the Vedic language, the suffix *up* is added by the rule "after a word ending in *kyac*, [the suffix *up* is added] in the Chandas. Its accent is [that of the suffix]. *Abhakta*: From the root *bhaj* (to serve/share) in the *luṅ* tense, with the suffix *sic*. By the rule "elision of what precedes *al* when *al* follows," there is elision. It is unaccented because it begins the quarter-verse (*pāda*). *Pinvadhvam*: This is the form of the root *pivi* (to sprinkle/swell) in the imperative (*loṭ*). It receives the *nighāta* (elision of accent). *Iṣayantīḥ*: Meaning "making food" (*iṣam kurvantyaḥ*). The suffix *ṇic* is added by the rule "it performs that" (*tat karoti*). Because of the treatment as an *iṣṭhan*-ending stem by the rule "in the case of a nominal stem, as if it were an *iṣṭhan*," there is the elision of the final *ṭi* by the rule "elision of *ṭi*. There is the lengthening of the vowel due to the rule "optionally in the Chandas. Its accent is that of the suffix. *Pṛṇadhvam*: From the root *pṛṇ* (to please/fill). This is the form in the imperative. The *ātmanepada* ending occurs by transposition (*vyatyaya*). It is unaccented because it begins a new sentence. *Yāta*: This is the form of the root *yā* (to go) in the imperative. Here too, there is no *nighāta*. *Śīrdham*: From the root *śībhra* (to speak/urge). That which possesses this [quality] by which one is urged is formed with the suffix *ghan* in the sense of an instrument (*karaṇa*). Its accent is that of the suffix.

Let the wave rise up; let the pins be struck out; O Waters, release the thongs! Let the two ill-doers, the two who have committed an offense, swell with water and perish. 13. Let your wave rise up; let the pins be struck out; O Waters, release the thongs! Let the two ill-doers, the two who have committed an offense, swell with water and perish. 13.
Having previously spoken of crossing the rivers after Viśvāmitra had crossed, Guṇa now says, desiring to cross:
"O rivers, let your wave (*ūrmi*) go upward, so that it may rise above the *śamyās*—the ropes attached to your necks, sides, and so forth.
Let the wave not go beneath the ropes; such is the intention."
Likewise, O Waters, you must release the *yoktrāṇi*, those ropes;
the intention is that they should pass by so as not to touch [us].

O *vyenasā*, free from sin, and therefore *aduṣkṛtau*, performers of auspicious deeds—O *adyau*, two who are today not to be disregarded by anyone, whose splendor is a wonder even in adversity—let *śūnam*, prosperity, not come to us in a state of distress (*ārtām*).
Thus, having praised the rivers, Viśvāmitra crossed over them with their permission.
*Ūrmiḥ*. [Derived from] the root *ṛ*, meaning "to go. The suffix *mip* is applied according to the rule: "After *ṛ*, [the suffix *mip* is added] and *ṛ* is replaced by *u*."
The substitution ‘ūḥ’ occurs for the verbal root [ṛ]. Thus, from the root *ṛcchati*, we have *ūrmiḥ*. It takes the accent of the suffix.
*Śamyāḥ*: from the root *śam* meaning "to pacify" (*upaśame*), with the suffix *ya* according to the rule *poradupadhāt*.
The word *anāvaḥ* has an udātta accent on the first syllable according to the rule *yato ’nāvaḥ*.
[The root] *han* means “to kill” (*hiṃsā*).

1. *la-gamanam* (the transition of *la*). 2. Elision (*lopa*) of *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, and *ṇa*. 3. *la-uttīrṇaḥ* (crossed beyond *la*). 4. *kha*, *ga*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *na*, *pa*, *bha*, and *sa* occur. 5. *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *na*, *bha*, and *ma* do not exist in the "first" [section]. 6. *ṛñ* follows *ta* and *artaiḥ*.

*gavyoḥ* is the form in the *loṭ* (imperative) mood; it is unaccented (*nighāta*). *Yoktrāṇi*: from the root *yujir* in the sense of "joining"; the suffix *cha* is applied by the rule *dāmnīśasayuyuja* etc.; it has the *nisvara* accent. *Sunna*: from the root *succh* in the sense of "releasing"; it is unaccented (*nighāta*). *Adupakṛttau*: by the rule *isusoḥ sāmarthye*, the *visarjanīya* becomes *pa*. *Vyenasā*: in a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the accent falls on the first member; the case-ending (*sup*) is replaced by *ḍā*. *Adyau*: from the root *hana* in the sense of "killing" or "going," preceded by *na*; the suffix *yak* is applied by the rule *adyādayaśca*; due to its being *kit*, there is elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhālopa*); by the rule *ho hanteḥ*, *ha* becomes *gha*. Since all rules are optional in the Veda (*chandas*), the substitution of *au* for *as* does not occur; consequently, there is no application of the *śī* replacement [for *jas*]. It has the accent of the single substitute (*ekādeśasvara*). *Śūnyam*: from the root *dhayati*; the suffix *kta* is applied in the neuter sense of state (*napuṃsake bhāve ktaḥ*); there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) because it belongs to the *yajādi* class; lengthening occurs by the rule *halaḥ*; the suffix is marked as *niṣṭhā* by the rule *oditaśca*; it is acutely accented on the first syllable by the rule *niṣṭhā ca dvayajanāta*. *Aratām*: from the root *ṛ* in the sense of "going," in the *luṅ* (aorist); for the *cli* suffix, *aṅ* is substituted by the rule *matiśāstyatibhyaśca*; by the rule *ṛdaśo'ṅi guṇaḥ*, *guṇa* is applied; by the rule *na māṅayoge*, the augment *aṭ* is absent; it is unaccented (*nighāta*). || 14 ||
"Indraḥ pūrbhiḥ" is the fifth hymn, consisting of eleven verses; it belongs to the seer Viśvāmitra and is addressed to Indra.
Regarding this, the Anukramaṇikā states: "Indraḥ pūrbhiḥ—eleven [verses].
In the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, at the midday pressing (mādhyandinasavana), the hymn "Indraḥ pūrbhiḥ" is used in the recitation (śastra) of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin priest.
In the section titled "Of the Hotrakas," it is prescribed in the Sūtra: "Indraḥ pūrbhidudu brahmāṇi" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 5.16).

On the first day of both the Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava Ṣaḍahas, during the midday pressing (mādhyandina-savana), in the recitation (śastra) of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, there are three *saṃpāta* hymns in place of the *ahīna* hymn extended from the Caturviṃśa [day].
Of these, this is the first.
"Indra alone, with his fort-crushers, went seeking the sacrifice" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 7.5).
This hymn, beginning with *udvīda abhinat* and *indraḥ pūrbhid*, is to be inserted as the *nivid* in the *niṣkevalya* litany.
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "The midday [pressing] consists of *indra soma* and *indraḥ pūrbhid*" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 9.8).
Indra, the breaker of forts, the slayer of Dāsa, the wise one, has subdued his enemies with his weapons;
impelled by prayer (*brahman*), increasing in body, the giver of much has filled both heaven and earth.

Indra, the destroyer of forts, overcame the Dāsa with his hymns; finding the cattle, showing mercy, he scattered his enemies. Impelled by prayer and growing mighty in body, the giver of many gifts filled both heaven and earth.
Viśvāmitra praises [Indra]:

"The breaker of forts, the destroyer of the cities of the Asuras; for this very reason, the possessor of wealth (*vidadvasu*), endowed with riches that make known your greatness through their manifestation; 'vidayamānaḥ', meaning especially harming the enemies, the Asuras.
And thus Yāska says: "'Vidadvasu'—harming the enemies; for it is a word denoting the act of harming" (Nirukta 4.17).

Such an "Indra" [increased] the "dāma"—the *dāsa* being the day, so called because darkness (*tamas*) is destroyed (*dasyate*) by it. He "atirat," that is, he increased it "samantāt" (on all sides), with "arkaiḥ"—that is, with his own splendors worthy of worship (*arcanīyaiḥ*). Thus, Indra’s nature as the Sun was magnified.
And thus says the Smṛti: "In the month of Caitra, Indra shall scorch.
Furthermore, "impelled by Brahman" means drawn forth by the *stotra* (hymn).
Or rather, impelled by Brahmā, the creator of the universe, "tanvā" means with his own body, "vāvṛdhānaḥ" meaning increasing; he is "bhūridātraḥ.
A "dātra" is a weapon, so called because by it the heads of enemies are cut (dāyate) or severed;
thus, he is endowed with many kinds of weapons.
Such an Indra filled both the *rodasī*, heaven and earth, completely on every side.
*pūrbhiḥ*: [derived from] the root *bhid* in the sense of "cleaving" (*vidāraṇe*),
with the suffix *kvip*.
The augment *at* is applied.
1. [The substitutes] *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *na*, and *yat*.
2. [The substitution of] *ka* and *ṇa* for *ca* and *na* respectively.
3. *kha-pha-bha-auhaḥ* does not undergo the substitution of *śī*; *ta-na-auhaḥ* undergoes the substitution of *śī*. 4.
*kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-ta-na-bha-la-sa* belongs to the Mādhyandina school.
5. *ca-pha* [belongs to] the destroyer of the city of Amura. 6. *ma-ga-gha-ca-ja-ṇa-pha-bha-ā* [belongs to] Samantāta.
7. Not in Caitra month; nor in Jyeṣṭha month. 8. Not that which is "born" does not exist.
9. Pha: He alone is the creator of the world; Sa: He is the created world.
10. Increasing with his body—that is, possessing the nature of growth—he is the bestower of much, endowed with many means of cutting, [filling] both worlds (rodasī).

The suffix *śa* [is applied] after the root *tṛ* by means of the *dhāyya* [affix]. There is the substitution of *i* for the vowel *ṛ* of the root according to the rule *ṛta iddhātoḥ*. There is the *nighāta* (anudātta accent). *Dāsam*: [This is formed with] the suffix *ghañ* in the sense of an instrument (*karaṇe*). It has the accent of the suffix *jhi*. *Vidadvasuḥ*: [This is derived from] the root *vid*, which has the causative sense (*antarbhāvita-ṇyartha*) inherent in it, followed by the suffix *śatṛ*. Because it belongs to the *ad* class, there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix *śap*; thus, by the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*), the suffix *śatṛ* is acute (*udātta*). In the *bahuvrīhi* compound, the accent falls on the first member. *Dayamānaḥ*: [From the root] *day* in the senses of giving, going, protecting, harming, or taking. It is *ātmanepada*. The suffix *śānac* is used for the present tense (*laṭ*). By the rule *na lokāvyaya*, the prohibition of the genitive case applies. *Vavṛdhānaḥ*: [From the root] *vṛdhu* in the sense of increasing. This is the form with the suffix *kānac*. In the *saṃhitā*, the reduplication (*abhyāsa*) undergoes the substitution of *d* due to the rule beginning with *tujādīnāṃ dīrgho'bhyāsasya*. *Bhūridātraḥ*: [From the root] *dāp* in the sense of cutting. The suffix *dan* is applied by the rule beginning with *dāmnī-śas-y-iti*. In the *bahuvrīhi* compound, the original accent of the first member remains. *Apṛṇata*: [From the root] *pṛṇa* in the sense of pleasing. When the suffix *iy* is elided, the suffix *śa* is applied because it belongs to the *tudādi* class. There is the *nighāta* accent. *Gedamī*: This is the form [of the root] *rud* with the suffix *asun*. *Nimbaraḥ*: [This is the form of the root *ni-mṛ* with the suffix *asun*.]
I urge forth the impetuous speed of you, the bounteous Maghavan, the mighty one, with my speech that adorns the immortal.
O Indra, you are the foremost protector of human settlements and also of the divine tribes.

I send forth my speech as an impulse for you, the bounteous Maghavan, the powerful one, adorning it for the sake of immortality. O Indra, you are the foremost of the human settlements and of the divine tribes. 2.

O Indra, O Lord, adorning yourself as the protector, I send forth with my mind your impulsion (*jūti*)—your speech characterized by praise—for the sake of immortality (*amṛta*), that is, for food. You are the one who goes before (*pūrvayāvā*) the human settlements (*mānuṣīṇāṃ kṣitīnām*), born of Manu—that is, of men—and also of the divine clans (*daivīnāṃ viśām*), the offspring related to the gods. Regarding *maghavasya*: from the root *maha* in the sense of "worship" (*pūjā*), with the suffix *kvap* and the elision of the *hal* following the rule *naherhalopaśca* (Uṇādisūtra 5.709), where *halopaḥ* is understood. He is "great" (*maha*) because he is worshipped by all; thus he is *makha*. The final accentuation is according to the rule *svāntamyāsādeḥ*. Although it begins with *m*, it occurs here by virtue of the specific grammatical statement. Regarding *taviṣasya*: from the root *tavati*, the suffix *ṭipca* is added. It has the *citsvara* accent. Regarding *jūtim*: by the rule *ūtiñūti* etc., the suffix *cin* has the acute accent. Regarding *iyarmi*: it belongs to the class beginning with *anirjuhāti*. By the rule *atipivatyośca*, there is the substitution of *i* for the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*). By the rule *abhyāsasya*, there is the replacement of *iy* for the reduplication. Because it begins a *pāda*, there is no *nighāta* (suppression of accent); rather, it takes the accent of the reduplicated form. Regarding *bhūpan*: this is the present participle (*śatṛ*) of the root *bhūpa* in the sense of "adornment" (*alaṃkāra*). The accent of the verbal root remains due to the rule regarding the accent of *ārdhadhātuka* suffixes. Regarding *asi*: this is the form of the root *as* in the present tense (*laṭ*). There is *nighāta*. Regarding *mānuṣīṇām*: the suffix *añ* is added by the rule *manorjātau* with the augment *puṅ*. The feminine suffix *ṅīp* is added by the rule *ṭiḍḍhāṇañ*. The accent is that of the *jhī* suffix. Regarding *daivīnām*: the suffix *añ* is added by the rule *devādyañau*. Here too, as before, *ṅīp* is added, and the accent is that of the *jhī* suffix. Regarding *pūrvayāvā*: from the root *yā* in the sense of "going" (*prāpaṇe*), the suffix *vanip* is added by the rule *āto maninkvanivvanipaśca*. The accent is that of the secondary member (*kuduttarapadasvara*).
Indra, whose guidance is through might, overthrew Vṛtra; he, whose guidance is through pride, destroyed the wiles of the deceivers.
On that day, he burned them up in the forests and made manifest the cattle of the Ramyas.

Indra, whose leadership is bold, encompassed Vṛtra; his leadership is full of majesty, for he subdued the wiles of the deceivers. He struck down Vyansa, burning fiercely among the woods, and made manifest the lovely milks of the cows.

1. [The suffix] *him* is applied after the roots *kha*, *ga*, *ja*, *ta*, *na*, *bha*, and *la*. 2. [The suffix] *vāvṛdhāna* is applied after *ja* and *ṇa*. 3. [The suffix] *prāṇana* is applied after *bha* and *sa*. 4. [The suffix] *saṃharṇāya* is applied after *pa*. 5. [The suffix] *amṛtāya* is applied for the purpose of drinking (*pānārtham*); *la* is applied for the purpose of drinking nectar (*amṛtapānārtham*). 6. [The suffix] *mavārādi* does not occur after *na*. 7. The suffix *ḍapaca* is applied after *ca* and *pha*. 8. [The suffix] *kina* is applied after *ja*, *ṇa*, and *la*. 9. [The suffix] *svareṇa* is applied after *ta*. 10. [The suffix] *iti* is applied after *la*. [End of] Sūtra 34, Chapter 3, Section 3, Part 1.3. Third Aṣṭaka, Verse 357.

*Śardhanītiḥ*: *Nītiḥ* means leading or action; he whose action is *śardha*, meaning increased or powerful, is thus called *śardhanītiḥ*. That Indra *avṛṇot* (enclosed/overpowered) the Asura Vṛtra by his strength. Likewise, *varṣanītiḥ*—Indra, whose action in battle is the warding off of the blows of enemies—*pra amināt* (completely destroyed) the *māyinām* (of the magicians). The genitive case is used in the sense of the accusative; he killed the magical Asuras pre-eminently. *Uśadhak*—desiring the slaughter of the enemy—Indra struck (*ahan*) the Asura who moved hidden in the forests, making him *dhyasam*, that is, one whose shoulders were gone, just as it might happen. Now, when that night-walker, the stealer of the cows, was slain, he made manifest (*āviḥ akṛṇot*) the *dhenāḥ* (cows) situated within the *rāmyāṇām* (of the nights). *Rāmaḥ* is the pleasure consisting of sport with women; those nights which deserve such pleasure are *rāmyāḥ*. Within those nights he made the cows visible. Regarding the nights being occupied by the Asuras, the Taittirīya [Saṃhitā] says: "The day belonged to the gods, the night to the Asuras. Those Asuras entered the night together with whatever wealth and property belonged to the gods. Thus, the *dhenāḥ* are the voices of those who praise during the day within the nights. *Akṛṇota*: This is the form of the root *vṛj* (in the sense of covering) in the *laṅ* tense; there is a *nighāta* accent. *Śardhanītiḥ*: The root *śardh* has the sense of power. From this, the suffix *ghañ* is added in the sense of an action (noun). In the *bahuvrīhi* compound, the accent falls on the first member. *Amināt*: From the root *miñ* (in the sense of injury), in the *laṅ* tense, the shortening occurs according to the rule *mānāternigame*; there is a *nighāta* accent. *Ahan*: The form of the root *han* in the *laṅ* tense. *Uśadhak*: From the root *vaś* (in the sense of desire). The form is established through the addition of *guṇa* and the *udittva* designation. *Āviḥ*: It is listed among the *svarādi* group as ending in an udātta vowel, hence it is antodātta. *Dhenāḥ*: From the root *dhā* (in the sense of drinking). By the *uṇādi* rule *gheṭa iñ*, the suffix *iñ* is added, resulting in the replacement of the final vowel with *ī*. There is *guṇa*. They drink from it, thus it is *dhenā*, speech. In the verse *dhenā jigāti* (RV 1.2.3), it is udātta by the accent of the suffix, but here, by transposition (*vyatyaya*), it is ādyudātta. *Akṛṇota*: From the root *kṛvi* (in the sense of injuring or doing); there is a *nighāta* accent. *Rāmyāṇām*: From the root *ram* (in the sense of sporting). In the sense of "those which deserve pleasure" (*rāmam arhanti*), the suffix *ya* is added according to the rule *chandasi ca*; its accent follows. Alternatively, from the root *ram* with the causative sense internalized, the suffix *ya* is added according to *adhyādayaśca*. Yāska says: "It causes beings to move at night, and causes others to cease" (Nirukta 2.18). There is a change of vowels (*varṇavyatyaya*).
Indra, the winner of light, generating sacred hymns, conquered the hostile armies with his helpers;
he caused the banner of wisdom to shine for Manu and found the light for great joy.

Indra, winner of the light, generating the days, victorious with his eager followers, the helper, has overcome the hostile armies. He caused the signal for man to shine forth; he found the devouring food and the light for the great battle. 4.

The bestower of heaven, Indra—generating the days with his own splendors together with the *uśij*, the desiring priests—being victorious (*abhiṣṭi*), conquered the enemy armies; he subdued the foes. Following the slaying of the enemies, he caused the sun, the banner of the days and the indicator, to shine forth for Manu, the human performer of the rite, the sacrificer; thus, through the destruction of the demon Tamoṣas, he caused it to blaze intensely.
Then, for the sake of great and vast battle—that is, for the manifestation of war—he found, that is, obtained, light as illumination.
Svarṣāḥ. [The root] paṇ [is used] in the sense of "giving.
[The suffix] kvip [is applied].

By the rule *janasanakhanām sañcau*, there is the substitution of *āt* (ā). By the rule *sanoter anah*, there is the substitution of *an*. By the rule *aharādīnām patyādiṣūpasaṃkhyānam*, there is the substitution of *s* for the *visarjanīya*.
*jigāya*.

Regarding the root *ji* in the sense of "to conquer," in the *liṭ* (perfect) tense, by the rule *saniṭojeḥ*, there is the substitution of *k* for the letter following the reduplication (*abhyāsa*). It takes the accent of the *liṭ*.
*pṛtanāḥ*. [The root] *pṛṅ* means "to exert oneself.
By the rule *kṛbhyāṃ kit*, the suffix *tanan* is applied.
The *pṛtanās* are armies, so called because warriors (*yoddhāraḥ*) exert themselves (*vyāpriyante*) therein; the accent is udātta on the first syllable due to the suffix *ni*. [The word] *abhiṣṭiḥ*.
*Abhigantā* [is derived from] the root *iṣ*, meaning "to go. By the rule beginning with "in *mantra*, *vṛṣa*, etc.," the suffix *ti* is udātta.
For even though it is intent upon the state (*bhāva*), it fully indicates the agent (*bhavitṛ*).

1. *ca-ja-ṇa-ṛddham*. 2. *la-atra tu*. 3. *kha-ga-na-bha-sa* read *antarṇītasyārthāt*; *ja-ṇa* read *antarbhāva-taṇyarthāt*. 4. *la-sa* lack the word "for the sake of" (*mahate*). 5. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-ta-na-pha-bha-sa* lack the word "accented" (*lisvaraḥ*). 6. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-na-bha-la-sa* read *āyāme*. 7. *na-la-sa* read *iṣu*. 8. *kha-ga-ca-ja-ṇa-na-bha-la-sa* lack the passage "for... it indicates."

By the rule *tinutrantha* etc., there is a prohibition of the augment *iṭ*. Due to its inclusion in the *śakandhvādi* group, there is the substitution of the subsequent form (*pararūpa*). The accent is that of the *kṛt*-suffix at the end of the compound. *Arocayat*: this is the form of the root *ruca* in the sense of "shining" in the *laṅ* tense. *Manave*: from the root *man* in the sense of "knowing"; the suffix *u* is added by the rule *śṛ-snihi* etc.; because of the continued application of the rule [regarding the suffix], it is udātta on the first syllable. *Avindan*: from the root *vid* in the sense of "obtaining"; the nasal augment *num* is added by the rule *śe sucādīnām*; there is no *nighāta* (elision of accent) because it occurs at the beginning of a *pāda*. *Raṇāya*: the designation of the recipient (*saṃpradāna*) applies here according to the principle "the mention of the action must be made. The root *raṇ* has the meaning of "sound. The suffix *ap* is added by the rule *vaśiraṇoraṇasaṃyānam* (Pāṇini 3.3.58). Since the warriors roar—that is, make sound—against one another here, it is called *raṇa*, a battle. Because the suffix is marked with *p*, it is anudātta, and thus the accent of the verbal root remains.
Indra has entered into his two arms with great power, bestowing many heroic deeds upon men.
He has perceived this for the singer; he has fashioned this bright color for them.
Indra has entered into his impetuous strengths and powers, assuming many manly exploits as he goes.

They praise—the word *panayanti* is derived from the root *pan*, meaning "to praise," with the suffix *āya* added according to the rule *gupū-dhūpa-vichi-paṇa-panibhya āyaḥ*; the short vowel is a Vedic archaism; it receives the *nighāta* accent. The phrase *indrasya mahāni puruṇi sukṛtā karma*—"the many well-performed deeds of Indra"—is not analyzed as separate words during the *padapāṭha* here because of the specific sense required. They praise the great, worthy, and numerous well-done deeds (*sukṛtā*)—such as the slaying of Vṛtra and others—of this Indra who possesses such power. Such an Indra, by means of his *vṛjanena*—*vṛjana* is strength, so called because enemies are warded off (*vajryante*) by it—with that strength, he thoroughly pulverized (*saṃ pipeṇa*) the *vṛjinān*, the Asuras who are of the nature of evil. Likewise, he is *abhibhūyojāḥ*: *abhibhūti* is the conquest or overcoming of enemies; he whose *ojas* (strength) consists in that is *abhibhūyojāḥ*. He is capable of the defeat of his foes. Such an Indra, with his *māyābhiḥ* (deceptions), thoroughly pulverized the *dasyūn*, the Asuras who cause destruction. Regarding the grammatical analysis: *Panayanti*: From the root *pan* (to praise), the suffix *āya* is applied; the shortening is Vedic; it takes the *nighāta* accent. *Vṛjanena*: From the root *vṛji* (to ward off). The suffix *kyu* is applied according to the rule *kṛpṛ-vṛji-mandi-nidhābhyaḥ kyuḥ*. Due to the *kit* designation, there is no *guṇa* substitution; the accent is that of the suffix. *Vṛjinān*: From the root *vṛji* (to ward off). The suffix *dvat* is applied according to the Unādi Sūtra 2.205 (*vṛjeḥ kicca*). *Vṛjina* means sin or evil; those who possess it are *vṛjinān*. Alternatively, it may be derived from the *arśas-ādi* group. The accent is that of the single substitute (*ekādeśasvara*). *Pipeṇa*: From the root *piplu* (to pulverize). This is the form in the perfect tense (*liṭ*), third person singular, with the suffix *ṇal*. It takes the *nighāta* accent. *Abhibhūyojāḥ*: *Bhūti* is the act of becoming (*bhavana*); the suffix *kin* is used in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāve*). According to the rule *tādau ca niti*, the root *ami* retains its original accent. He whose *ojas* is "overpowering" (*abhibhūta*) is *abhibhūyojāḥ*. This is a *bahuvrīhi* compound according to the rule *masyupamānapūrvapadasya bahuvrīhiḥ*. In a *bahuvrīhi*, the accent is that of the first member (*pūrvapada-prakṛtisvara*). Thus, such an Indra, by his powers and deceptions, completely crushed the destructive Asuras. They praise him for these deeds.
The lord of battle, the great master of the people, has created wide space for the gods; as the true lord, he fills the world.
At the dwelling of Vivasvat, the inspired poets and sages praise those deeds of his with hymns.

Through battle, Indra, the great lord of the people and protector of men, has created wide space for the gods. These deeds of his in the dwelling-place of Vivasvat, the inspired sages and seers proclaim with their hymns. || 7 ||

The Lord of the True Ones (the gods), the fulfiller of desires for human beings by granting them the fruits they expect—Indra, through great battle, secured vast wealth (*varivas*). Wealth is so called because it is intensely sought after by those who desire it;
having obtained such wealth through combat, he bestowed it upon the gods, that is, upon the worshippers who delight in praising him.

The wise ones—the learned sages and singers—praise with hymns those deeds of this Indra, such as the slaying of Vṛtra and the bestowing of many gifts, in the dwelling, that is, the house of this sacrificer who especially abides in the performance of the Agnihotra and other rites. They extol them with songs of praise.
By *yudhā*. [The root] *yudh* [is used] in the sense of "striking together" (*saṃprahāra*).
The suffix *kvip* is applied in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) according to the rule beginning with *saṃpadādi*.
The acute accent on the case-ending is due to the rule "sāvekācaḥ.
Regarding *varivaḥ*: from the root *vṛñ* (meaning "to choose"), when the suffix *ya* is elided, the augment *ri* is added to the reduplicated syllable according to the rule "ṛtaśca."
The suffix *asun* is applied after that [stem] ending in *-t*. By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), there is elision of the *ṭi* portion;
it is unaccented (*nisvara*).
The form is *cakāra* (he did) and *karoti* (he does). [In these cases,] there is elision of the accent (*nighāta*).

*Satpati*: *sat* is the form [of the root] in the present participle (*śatṛ*). In the word *pāyāva*, meaning "sovereignty," there is the accentuation of the original form of the first member (*pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratva*).
*carṣaṇiprāḥ*:
[from] *prā* in the sense of "filling" (*pūraṇe*), with the suffix *viṣ*.
Regarding *vicaravat*: from the root *vas* (meaning "to dwell") in the sense of the abstract noun (*bhāva*) characterized by the *saṃpad-ādi* group, there is the suffix *kvip*.
Then, by the rule *tad asyāsty asmin*, the suffix *matup* is applied.
By the rule "mādupadhāyāḥ," its *v* is substituted;
since the suffix is marked with *p*, it is unaccented, and thus the accent of the verbal root remains.
They praise.
This is the form of the root *gṛ* in the sense of "sound" (*śabde*) in the present tense (*laṭ*);
[it takes] the *nighāta* accent.

1. [The suffix *kvip* is applied] after the roots *kha*, *ga*, *ja*, *ṇa*, *na*, *bha*, and *sa* when preceded by a well-formed vowel (*sukṛta*); and after *ca* when preceded by a well-formed vowel. 2. The goddesses rejoice after Indra, the ever-conquering, the excellent, the giver of strength, the winner of light and the divine waters—he who has won the earth and this heaven; after him, the wise ones exult. satrāsāham | vareṇyam | sahodām | sasavāṃsam | svar | apaḥ | ca | devīḥ | sasāna | yaḥ | pṛthivīm | dyām | uta | imām | indram | madanti | anu | dhīraṇāsaḥ ||8||

The wise ones, possessing intelligence and worthy of praise, the praisers—rejoicing after Indra, who is all-conquering, the overcomer of the great Vṛtra and others, and for that very reason desirable by all; who bestows strength upon the weak seeker; and who, being divine in nature, has won for himself the waters and the heavenly world—they rejoice and exult after him. The meaning is that they themselves become joyful following his joy. As for that Indra...
Indra has seized the plants and the trees; he has won the mid-air.
He split Vala and drove away the contending voices; thus he became the measureless one among those of superior mental power.

Indra bound up the plants; he bound up the days; he split the firmament; he struck down Vala; he drove away the disputants; then he became the subduer of those who were overweening in their power. 10.
Such an Indra bestowed the plants—consisting of grasses, shrubs, and so forth, endowed with ripe fruits—for the enjoyment of living beings;
likewise, he granted the days for the purpose of determining the span of life.
Furthermore, he bestowed the lords of the forest—trees characterized by the *khadira*, *palāśa*, and other species—for the sake of sacrifice.
Likewise, he gave the intermediate space for the purpose of movement;
likewise, he gave *vala*. It is called *vala* because by it the sky is enclosed (*saṃciyate*); thus, *vala* is the cloud.
He split that cloud, cleaving it for the purpose of propelling the waters;

he drove away the Asuras who were "virācaḥ," those of conflicting speech, and he oppressed them for the protection of living beings; then, immediately thereafter, [he acted] against those of hostile intentions.
*Kratu* means action.
Come toward us for the sake of battle; like Vāyu, come with your three bay horses yoked to the chariot, as you do with your teams of steeds.
Drink the pressed juice that has been offered to you; O Indra, Svāhā! We have presented it to you for your exhilaration.

Stay! O two bay horses, being yoked to the chariot, come toward us like Vāyu with his teams of horses. You shall drink the soma-juice when it has been touched for us; O Indra, Svāhā! We have offered it to you for your exhilaration. 1.
Viśvāmitra praises:
O Indra, mount for a short while the two bay horses (*harī*) being yoked to your chariot (*ratha*).
In this regard, there is an illustration: "like Vāyu."
Just as the *niyut*—the teams of mares yoked to the chariot of Vāyu—remain for a certain time while awaiting him, so it is here.
Now, having mounted [your chariot], come toward us, come quickly.
And having arrived, being touched and permitted by us (*asme*), drink the *andhas*, the food characterized by Soma.
Svāhā!
This Soma has been offered;
we present this Soma, consecrated with the cry of "svāhā," for your exhilaration and joy. We give it to you.
Come hither like Vāyu with his teams; by means of sacred prayer, I yoke for you those two bay steeds yoked by prayer, your companions, swift to the joint revelry.
Mounting the firm and comfortable chariot, O Indra, come to the Soma as one who is wise and all-knowing.

With the prayer of Brahmā, I yoke for you the two bay steeds, the companions at the shared feast. O Indra, mounting your swift, firm, and well-seated chariot, come to the Soma as one who is wise and all-knowing. 4.
O Indra, [you and the priest] are to be yoked together by the priest through the mantra at the *sadhamāda*.
A *māda* is a place where warriors rejoice;
*sadhamāda* means a shared rejoicing (*saha-māda*).
In that battle, I yoke with a prayer—the hymn of praise—your two bay horses (*harī*), which are non-combatants, equally renowned, and therefore swift-moving.
Mounted upon such a chariot—one that is firm, very solid, and well-fashioned—come for the sake of drinking the Soma;
come, knowing the way here.
Joined with the Brahman. The suffix *kvip* is applied to the root *yuj* in the sense of the object (passive), according to the *ṇādika* group.

This Soma is yours; come hither toward us, and being well-disposed, drink of it most constantly. Having sat down upon the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) at this sacrifice, O Indra, place this drop (*indu*) within your belly. This is yours. Soma. You. Come. Hitherward. Most constantly. Being well-disposed. Of this. Drink. At this. Sacrifice. Upon the sacrificial grass. Having sat down. Place. This. Drop. Within your belly. O Indra. 6.

O Indra, this Soma is for you; it has been pressed for your sake. Come hither, turn toward the Soma. Having arrived, being well-disposed and of auspicious mind, drink—drink most abundantly—this Soma. Having sat down upon this sacrificial grass (*barhis*) that has flourished at this sacrifice, place within your belly this *indu*, this Soma which is by nature moistening; hold it so that it does not go below the navel. In the verse "Come with the limbs, with the sacrifices" (*Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* 10.14.5), the word *barhis* is not an adjective qualifying the sacrifices, nor is it considered a separate form; thus its distinctness is not admitted here. *ihi*: from the root *iṇ* 'to go', this is the form in the imperative (*loṭ*). It is subject to *nighāta* (accentual suppression). *śaśvattamam*: by virtue of belonging to the *ucchādi* group, it is oxytone (acute on the final syllable). *pāhi*: this is the form of the root *pā* 'to drink' in the imperative. By the rule "in the Veda there is diversely," there is elision of the suffix *śap*. It is subject to *nighāta*. *niṣadya*: from the root *sad* with the suffix *lyap*; by the rule "after *pra*, *pari*, *upa*, and *ni*, there is *ṣatva*," the change to *ṣ* occurs. It bears the *lim-svara* (the accent of the suffix). *dadhiṣva*: from the root *dhā* in the imperative; by the rule "in the Veda both ways," the suffix *sa* is treated as an *ārdhadhātuka*, resulting in the augment *iṭ*. The accent is that of the suffix. *indum*: from the root *undī* 'to moisten'; the suffix *up* is added by the rule "from *undī* and others, *up*"; the initial *d* of the root is replaced by *t*. Because of the continued application of the term *nit*, it is ādyudātta (acute on the first syllable).

The sacred grass is strewn for you; O Indra, the Soma is pressed; the parched grains are prepared for your two bay steeds to eat. To you, who dwell therein, the many-powerful, the bull accompanied by the Maruts—to you these oblations are offered. (7) *stīrṇam* (strewn), *te* (for you), *barhiḥ* (sacred grass), *sutaḥ* (pressed), *indra* (O Indra), *somaḥ* (Soma), *kṛtāḥ* (prepared), *dhānāḥ* (parched grains), *attave* (to eat), *te* (your), *haribhyām* (for the two bay steeds), *tad-okase* (to him whose dwelling is there), *puru-śākāya* (the many-powerful), *vṛṣṇe* (to the bull), *marutvate* (accompanied by the Maruts), *tubhyam* (to you), *rātā* (offered), *havīṃṣi* (oblations). (7)
O Indra, this sacrificial grass (barhis) has been spread out for you to sit upon;
likewise, Soma has been pressed for your sake.
For your two bay horses (haribhyām) to eat—that is, for their consumption—parched grains (dhānāḥ), prepared from roasted barley, have been provided.

Then, to you whose dwelling is upon the sacred grass (*barhis*)—that is, whose abode is there—to the one of many forms (*puruśākāya*), who is to be praised by many, or rather, who consumes much; to the showerer (*vṛṣṇe*) of desires; to the one accompanied by the Maruts—the Maruts being the divine clans—to you who are such, the oblations consisting of Soma and other offerings have been presented and given by us.
The sense is: "you should practice those."
*Stīrṇam*:
from the root *stṛñ* in the sense of "covering," there is the substitution of *i* for the radical vowel by the rule *kṛt-id-dhātoḥ*; and the change to the nasal *ṇ* occurs by the rule *radābhyām*.
The suffix *taven* is a conditional vowel (*pratyayasvara*).
In the word *attave*, the suffix *taven* is applied in the sense of the infinitive (*tumun*) to the root *ad*, meaning "to eat" (*ada bhakṣaṇe*).
The accent is acute (udātta).
In the case of *tadaukasaḥ*, it is the accent of the first member (*pūrvapada*) in a bahuvrīhi compound.
*Puruśākāya*:
[This is derived] from the root *śac*, meaning "in articulate speech," with the suffix *ghañ* in the sense of the object (*karman*).
By the rule *cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ*, the substitution of *k* occurs.
The accent of the final member of a *kṛt*-derived compound [is preserved].
In *marutvate*,
by the rule “*namo matvarthe*,” there is an absence of the *jaśtva* substitution for the letter *t* because it is not a technical name (*asaṃjñā*).
Since the suffix *pratyaya* has the marker *pittva*, it is *anudātta*; thus, the accent of the nominal stem (*prātipadika-svara*) remains. *Rātā*:
from the root *rā* in the sense of "giving," the suffix *kta* is applied in the passive (*karman*).
The accent of the suffix.
